## D-87 — THE PURGE'S LAST DELETION GETS ITS TWO SUCCESSOR ADDRESSES: the pane geometry at `['panes']` and the focus mirror at `['focus']`, two roots on the NORMAL crossing, and the frozen store is NOT deleted here

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's instruction this pass carries, verbatim — *"The purge's last deletion is the app's own frozen graph store … It cannot go until two data sets have a successor address … Build them."* — plus the measurements below, all driven 2026-11-03 on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`.

**THE GROUND, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN, AND IT DECIDES THE PASS.** **The pane geometry** is `file.settings.pane.<id>.size`/`.bounds` beside `mem.layout.pane.<id>.size`/`.bounds`: `readPaneSize`/`readPaneBounds` (`src/renderer/renderer.ts`, the `startSizeOf`/`boundsOf` closures) read **`mem` FIRST and `file` second**, and the release turn writes the SAME `final` to both tiers, `commit('file.settings.pane.pane-a.size', final)` then `commit('mem.layout.pane.pane-a.size', final)`. **There is ONE pane id under `src/` and it is not authored**: `paneIdOf` derives it from the caller's element or token and falls back to **`pane-a`**, which the release turn also hard-codes — while the authored DOM pane is a different string (`demo-envelope.ts` authors `gutter-pane`), so the address is keyed by the id the COMPOSITION addresses. **The default geometry is the tree's own and was measured, not invented**: the authored pane's `props` read `size '100'`, `min '0'`, `max '200'`, and `gutterSeamExample`'s `startSizeOf`/`boundsOf` fall back to the same three figures; **the frozen store holds NO pane default at all** (`grep -n 'pane' src/renderer/store-core-graph.ts` → 0), so a read that missed at both tiers answered `undefined` — an unusable value that made the release refuse `'unusable-default'` with ZERO writes. **The clamp is one site and one rule** (`src/shared/gutter.ts`'s `clampToBounds`): a non-number, or a pair whose `min`/`max` is not a number, answers `NaN`, and `NaN` makes the move INVALID; the release applies it only to a **standing `mem` value**, against `readPaneBounds({}, 'pane-a')`. **The focus mirror** is `mem.focus.entries` (`readonly FocusEntry[]`, each `{id, target, label?}` with `id` and `target` opaque) and `mem.focus.activeId` (`FocusId | null`): `mirrorStateOf` reads both, `answerForCarrier` commits both through the model's `persist` seam at one instant per reference, `createFocusCarrier`'s `persistTarget` is the same pair, and the mirror is CLEARED at the carrier's boot mint (`commit('mem.focus', undefined)` then `clear('mem.focus')` where the root is cold). **`focusCarrier` holds NO state** — it holds the STORE HANDLE, and its own docblock says the state lives in the `mem.focus.*` mirror and never in a module-level carrier.

**THE CROSSING IS THE NORMAL ONE, DECIDED ON EVIDENCE AND NOT PREFERENCE.** Both families are UI state with no security character — the tab record's own ground — while the secure crossing is the operator's security record and a resize or a focus transition is no authority act; and **the decisive finding is that the SECURE crossing's legacy rows address holds the frozen store's `file.*` projection of these very rows** (D-78's item (f)), so putting the new addresses there would stand the new value and its legacy projection inside ONE store, and the purge would be deleting from inside the operator's record. On the NORMAL crossing the legacy projection stays wholly in the secure store and every address this pass creates is wholly in the normal one, so **the purge deletes the projection and its rows and touches no address created here**. The cost, stated rather than hidden: until the purge, the same fact stands in two stores — a stale `file.settings.pane.*` row written by `Y-2`'s `STORE_FILE_PUT` and a fresh `['panes']` value — and nothing reconciles them.

**THE ADDRESS SHAPE IS TWO ROOTS, `['panes']` (`file`) AND `['focus']` (`mem`), AND THE TIER DECIDED IT.** The tab record's pattern is one root with members; it was followed until the measurement forbade it: **a nested write does not create its parent** (`write(['view','panes'], 'file', …)` over a fresh store answers `AddressNotFound: 'view' does not exist in ''`), so a one-root shape needs a THIRD declaration minting the parent branch, whose own body is handed `undefined` at the registration instant; and **a root written at `file` answers its descendants at `file` and `TierNotFound` at `mem`**, so one value could not carry the `mem` family at all. So the pattern is applied **once per tier** rather than once per family: each family is ONE WHOLE VALUE at its own root, under its own existence declaration.

**THE DECLARATIONS — TWO, BATCHED INTO THE BOOT'S ONE `createProfileStore` CALL BESIDE THE TAB RECORD'S SIX (D-65).** `panes-must-stand` at `['panes']` refuses a value that is not a plain record and repairs it to the measured default family; `focus-must-stand` at `['focus']` refuses the same arm and repairs it to the declared empty pair. **Both bodies judge `context.value` and neither is wrapped by the null-store guard** — `tabsMustStand`'s shape and its measured reason (the boot binds its holder only after `createProfileStore` returns) — and **both repairs write ONE whole legal value through the module's one repair-write path**, which branches on the record's own `write` member: three positions at a registration instant, and `writeJoinedAt`'s required carrier at `write`'s FOURTH at a landing one, every arm answering through `repairAnswer` (D-72, D-73). **`focus-must-stand` is `operator-exclusion-must-stand`'s shape exactly** and for its reason: a `mem` value can never come from a file (D-84), so a repair at the creation instant is its only lawful source. Files, each the tab record's counterpart: `src/main/view-record/index.ts`, `src/main/view-surface/index.ts`, `src/shared/view-channels.ts` (four constants), and the bridge member `view` declared in lockstep in `src/main/preload.ts` and `src/renderer/secure-panels.ts`.

**THE ACCEPTANCE BAR, DRIVEN PER ADDRESS AND READ OFF THE ROWS.** *(1) Existence + placeholder at the creation instant*: with the batch supplied and the address absent, the store's OWN read answers `{'pane-a': {size: 100, bounds: {min: 0, max: 200}}}` and `{entries: []}` before any route of the module runs, while a store carrying no batch answers `AddressNotFound` at the same address; **a fresh profile therefore answers the default geometry and the mirror at its default, both STANDING** — `read().source` reads `{panes:'record', focus:'record'}` — and a seeded family stands byte-identical (the pair is not a rewrite). *(2) The listener*: one delivery per committed change of EITHER family (1, then 2, then 3 over two pane commits and a focus commit), **ZERO** for a write at `['elsewhere']`, and the surface's `attach` turns the one subscription into the broadcast while the preload registers the same constant and does not re-spell it. *(3) Boot data*: two successive boots answer the same state, the profile carries `["panes"]` and **no byte of the `mem` family**, and boot two is handed `['focus']` **ABSENT** at the pair's own context and its repair mints it again — clause 3 answered for a family a file can never carry. *(4) Writes*: four paths and no fifth — `commitPane` and `commitFocus` (IPC routes, UI acts) and the two creation repairs — with **a read writing nothing, measured both ways** (the file's bytes unmoved over a standing family, and an absent `mem` family still absent after three reads) and no timer, interval or poll in the module or its surface. **Eight reverts were driven and each answered RED then restored**: either pair out of the batch (4 and 3 rows), the repair's answer widened to admit `void` (TS2578 twice, `npm run typecheck` over `src/**` staying CLEAN — the leg that catches it is `typecheck:tests`), the carrier position made optional (TS2578, and `src/**` still clean), the landing arm writing without naming the commit (the landing row), a read that repairs (the no-write-on-read row), the bridge half-widened in the renderer alone (the lockstep row), and the view record out of the boot's batch (the batch row).

**WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED.** The boot's profile image gains a root — `160 → 221` bytes over a fresh profile, `{"panes":…,"tabs":…}` — so **the declared bridge member set moves EIGHT → NINE in four censuses** (`tests/store-persist.test.ts`'s `DECLARED_TOP_LEVEL_BRIDGE_MEMBERS`, both `isolation.test.ts` files' `BRIDGE_MEMBERS`, and the settings-carrier scenario's ISO-4 list), each keeping its set assertion; `tests/integration/central-data/profile-file.test.ts`'s *THE APP'S OWN BOOT* is re-derived from one root to two, and it now batches the entry's own EIGHT declarations rather than six. **`tests/store-core-graph.test.ts`'s R-11 was re-derived rather than dodged**: its subject is the frozen paths' VALUE-SURFACE IMPORTERS, and it read raw `git grep` lines, so every later purge row's docblock naming the store it succeeds would red it — it now judges each candidate FILE's comment-elided code with that file's own `stripComments`, keeps the raw census as its subject list, and carries a two-arm positive control (a code mention is still a hit, the same mention in prose is not). Three other rows were saved by rewording this pass's own prose and not by touching them — `S-9`'s importing-FILE census and the settings-carrier ISO-7 address census are raw-byte reads, so this module names the package and the secure crossing's address without spelling either import or address. **`npm test` is `3,128 passed / 2 skipped` of `3,130` over `126` files** (`3,108` of `3,110` before this pass, so the `20` rows are this battery's), `srcTypeScriptFiles` `49 → 52`, `mapRows` `21 → 22`, and the marks `126` files with gating `134 → 154` sites in `22 → 23` files, REGENERATED by `strata-marks.mjs index` and never hand-edited; the four legs are **0/0/0/0**, and the boundary rows observed on the dirty tree were **two rows in each of TWO files** (`store-tabs-record.test.ts`'s `S-1` and `REG-EXEC`, `store-core-graph.test.ts`'s `R-9` and `I-11`) beside one in each of two more.

**THE FROZEN STORE IS NOT DELETED HERE, AND THAT IS THIS PASS'S ONE EXPLICIT LIMIT.** `src/renderer/store-core-graph.ts` (2,372 lines) stands, `src/renderer/renderer.ts`'s write paths are untouched, and the renderer is wired to these addresses NOWHERE: the swap is the NEXT pass, in the order the tab record's own sequence ran — crossing, then client, then purge. **Three facts the next pass inherits**: the pane geometry's `mem`/`file` precedence COLLAPSES to one `file` address (the `mem` copy is the in-gesture transient's), `activeId` is written as ABSENCE because `null` is refused at the crossing's boundary, and the legacy `file.*` rows keep being written by `Y-2` with nothing reading them until the purge deletes that arm.

**IT SUPERSEDES THE FRAMING OF THE ROWS ABOVE IT, NEVER THEIR DATED TEXT** (D-46). Its register is D-71 to D-86: the change push returned to the record root, a repair's credit made explicit, a repair write made to name its commit, the boot battery's teardown made to prove zero, the landing entry's id decided, the landing seat derived and that id moved, the renderer client's Stage A, the two-crossing ruling with its purge, the surplus instance collapsed, the `data.*` tools pinned to the central store, the module registry's legacy file dropped rather than migrated, the data-flow convention audited clause by clause, the imperative boot write deleted for a sixth declaration, the `mem` pair's existence declared at the store's creation, the absence-keyed import put inside the repair, and `1.9.1`'s landing-arm save. **The package-facing rows among them stay the package's** — `provident-storeroom` is read and never modified, its own corpus's decision ids are never spelled here, and a defect or a requirement gap of it belongs to the unit that surfaced it, filed with symptom, reproduction, suspected root cause and proposed fix shape (D-5, D-52).

## D-88 — THE RENDERER SWAP IS SOLVED IN DESIGN AND **STOPPED ON MEASUREMENT**: the shape that answers the async crossing, the timing it changes per call site, and the marked surface that pins the machinery it replaces — nothing moved, nothing deleted, and the tree is the head's

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's instruction this pass carries, verbatim — *"This pass points the renderer at them"*, *"the data shape is driven by the listener events"* — and the measurement below, driven 2026-11-03 on `c8e8689` over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`. **It is a measurement and a REFUSAL, which is the shape `D-78`'s item (f) stage took**, and it changes nothing in the tree: `git status --short` is empty at it.

**THE CRUX, AND THE SHAPE THAT ANSWERS IT.** The frozen store is SYNCHRONOUS AND IN-REALM; the crossing is IPC AND ASYNCHRONOUS. The synchronous callers are the pane-drag reads (`renderer.ts:1700-1722`), the `release` write (`:1823-1825`), the focus carrier's reads and commits (`:1104-1105`, `:1152-1153`, `:1967-1968`, `:1936-1937`) and the tab machinery. **THE USER'S CONVENTION IS THE SOLUTION, AND IT IS BUILT AS THE `tabs-client` PRECEDENT IS**: a RENDERER-SIDE CLIENT holds the data shape, is refreshed by `onChanged` deliveries, is read SYNCHRONOUSLY by the drag and focus paths, and writes through the crossing's routes. **THAT SHAPE IS NOT A STORE** — `D-78`'s ruling 3 and `D-82`'s clause 3: it holds **no address space** (a caller names a pane id, never a path and never a tier), it **owns no persistence** and opens no file, it **carries no constraint, no repair, no journal, no listener registration and no instance**, and it **is thrown away and refilled WHOLE by every delivery** — a store survives a restart by design and this survives exactly one delivery, which is the whole of why it can never be used as one and must never be named one.

**BUILT, TYPECHECKED AND DRIVEN, THEN REVERTED: WHAT THE SWAP WOULD HAVE DONE, WITH ITS TIMING AT EACH SITE.** `src/renderer/view-client.ts` was written (457 lines) with `src/shared/view-shape.ts` (85) carrying the two families' vocabulary and the measured defaults so both realms read one spelling; `typecheck` and `typecheck:tests` were 0 over both. *(1) READS* — `readPaneSize`/`readPaneBounds` answer `paneGeometryIn(shape.panes, id)` in the CALLER'S OWN TURN, the `mem`/`file` precedence collapsing to ONE `file` address (D-87's inherited fact (i)) and a pane the family does not name answering the MEASURED DEFAULT — 100 and `{min:0,max:200}` — instead of the `undefined` that made the release refuse `'unusable-default'` with zero writes; `mirrorStateOf` answers the shape's `{entries, activeId}` with the absent active read back as `null` (the crossing writes absence, D-87's fact (ii)); the tab record's reads answer the tab client's held reading. *(2) WRITES* — `release` sends ONE `commitPane(id, {size})` where it committed the same `final` to TWO tiers; it returns `void`, which it always returned, and the SINK is still invoked BEFORE the route is sent, so **no caller depends on the old timing** and the receipt lands in the client's `writeOutcome()` a tick later. The focus carrier sends ONE `commitFocus(wholeMirror)` where it committed two references, and its seam returns the client's `{status:'sent'}` statement rather than the store's receipt by identity — **no caller reads that receipt** (`persist`'s `value` member was always discarded), and the ROUTE'S ANSWER is the MODEL's next state, composed before the write, so a delivery arriving a tick later moves the SHAPE and never the answer. A mirror the crossing's boundary refuses (an id that is not a string, number or boolean) is recorded as a refusal where the frozen store would have taken it: a real behaviour change, stated. *(3) THE BOOT READ* — `startTabsClientInstrument`'s held reading becomes the TAB shape's first fill and the view client's `fill()` sits at the same last line of `main()`, beside it: **ONE STATED BOOT READ, then deliveries**, because a boot's own store acts and repair passes happened BEFORE this realm could subscribe and a cold profile changes nothing afterwards — so the first fill has no delivery to ride — and every later fill is a delivery's, with no timer, no poll and no write on any read. *(4) THE TAB MACHINERY* — `readTabsRef` is answered by the client's reading, `mintTabId` by its `order`, `closeTab` by the crossing's `remove`, and `driveTabsLandingPage` by the tabs client's OWN witness derivation, whose answer `main()` discards today (D-78's measurement). **`TABS_CONSTRAINT` LEAVES THE RENDERER** because the crossing declares `exactly-one-active` (`src/main/tabs-record/index.ts`, `D-83`'s batch), so the frozen store's construction is handed **NO `constraints` member at all** — nothing at all rather than an empty list, because an empty list is still a declaration that a constraint set exists and `buildWiredGraphStore`'s member becomes a name with nothing behind it.

**WHY NONE OF IT IS TAKEN: THE MARKED SURFACE IS A REWORK OF ITS OWN, MEASURED ROW BY ROW.** With the two families swapped and the tests untouched, `tests/pane-drag-compliance.test.ts` read **28 failed of 129** and `tests/store-focus.test.ts` **49 of 96**; giving each file's fixture a CROSSING DOUBLE — one client over a projected store, the delivery modelled at the write — took store-focus to **32**, and minting the `mem` mirror inside that double, as the crossing's creation repair does, took it to **20**. **THE RESIDUAL IS NOT A STALE EXPECTATION A PASS MAY RE-POINT**: in store-focus it is the file's `§2.4` registration/release family (P1, P3, P7, S24-1, SF-LEAK, F-3, M-5, R-4, P-2.6-4, both working defaults) together with the `§5.5.1` register's tally rows (P-SF-IM-2, P-SF-SM-1, P-SF-SM-2, P-SF-TP-1, P-SF-TP-2), whose declared terms COUNT the boot mint and the two `mem.focus.*` subscriptions — the two properties this swap deletes and the crossing's `focus-must-stand` plus the client's ONE subscription replace; in pane-drag it is the twelve `P-PD-IM-1` read rows, the `P-PD-SM-1`/`SM-3`/`TP-2` register rows and the write-census rows `F-5`/`F-6`/`M-5`, which count the old two-tier commit spelling. `tests/store-tabs-record.test.ts` was NOT attempted and is larger: its 100 rows pin the frozen store's tab region, 33 of them through `constrainedStore()`, and the invariant rows' successor is the crossing's own battery (`tests/integration/store-tabs-record/crossing.test.ts`) — so that file's disposition is `D-30`'s REPLACED-WHOLE and not a re-pointing.

**WHAT THE NEXT PASS OWNS, NAMED SO IT IS NOT REDESIGNED.** The `store-view-record` unit's swap pass takes the attempt as built (`/tmp/d88/attempt/` at this date: `view-client.ts` 457, `view-shape.ts` 85, the wiring and fixture diff 913 lines), **re-grains the two files' registers onto their subjects' new homes** — the crossing's `focus-must-stand` creation repair and the client's ONE subscription for the focus family, the client's shape and the route's call log for the panes family — deletes `tests/store-tabs-record.test.ts`'s rows WITH the region they pin, and carries the moved count into `brief.md` §6 in its own commit. **THE FROZEN STORE WAS NOT DELETED AND STANDING IS CORRECT**: `src/renderer/store-core-graph.ts` (2,372 lines) is untouched, the renderer is wired to `['panes']` and `['focus']` NOWHERE, and D-87's three inherited facts — the collapsed precedence, `activeId` written as absence, and the legacy `file.*` rows standing in two stores unreconciled — are all still the next pass's.

## D-91 — THE ZONE FAMILY GETS ITS ADDRESS: `['zones']` at `mem`, a third declaration in the boot's one batch, a route and a client read — and the frozen store still stands, because the deletion is the pass after

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's ruling this pass carries, verbatim — *"give zones an address in the view record"*, a third family beside `['panes']` and `['focus']` — which is `D-90`'s ruling (A) and nothing else: that row stopped here because *"it needs an address and that is a design act — stop and report rather than inventing one. Same for zones."* Measured on `20c1ddb` over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`.

**THE GROUND, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN, AND IT DECIDED THE PASS.** **Four members, EACH INDIVIDUALLY OPTIONAL** — `slot` (opaque: the flow's own word for the caller's token) and `distance` (caller-measured) read by `candidatesFor` (`renderer.ts:1937-1939`), `size` and `display` read by the render turn (`:1802-1803`) — and the optionality is driven, not assumed: the demo seeds `size`+`display` for three zones and `slot` alone for a third, while the two zone batteries write `slot`+`distance` and neither of the other two. **ZERO WRITERS UNDER `src/`**: every one of the four reads MISSes at this head, the render turn hands `undefined` straight to its layout call and `candidatesFor` answers `[]`, so the family's only writers in the tree are the demo (`demo/pane-drag-demo/demo.ts:158-166`, `MIN_ZONE_SIZE` 90) and the two test doubles (`tests/pane-drag-compliance.test.ts:490-491`, `tests/store-modules-seams.test.ts:965-966`). **TIER: `mem` ONLY, AND THAT IS WHAT THE ADDRESS TAKES** — `grep -rn "settings\.zone\|file\.[a-z.]*zone" src/` answers **nothing**, so no file-tier copy exists and there is no ascending read to collapse (the demo's one `file.settings.pane.zone-2.size` is a PANE member under a pane id spelled `zone-2`); a `mem` value can never come from a file (`D-84`), so the family's lawful boot source is a **repair re-minted at every boot**, `focus-must-stand`'s precedent. **DEFAULTS: NONE TO INHERIT** — a read that missed answered `undefined`, `candidatesFor` answered `[]`, and the tree states no zone size at all, so a repair minting a geometry would be a second authority. **IDS ARE OPEN** — `zoneIdOf` takes the caller's element's `zoneId` and falls back to `zone-1`, which the render turn hard-codes, so no closed set exists to declare and the placeholder cannot name one. **AND NO CALLER SUPPLIES ZONE INPUT**: `createPaneDrag` takes `frozen` as `unknown` (`:1716`, `:1721`) and has no caller under `src/` at all, so zones reach the composition by store READ alone and there is nothing to reconcile.

**Decision.** `VIEW_ZONES_ADDRESS = ['zones']` at **`mem`**, declared by **`zones-must-stand`** and batched into the boot's ONE `createProfileStore` call beside the tab record's six and this module's two (nine declarations, one construction, unchanged). **The body judges `context.value` and is not wrapped by a null-store guard** — `panesMustStand`'s shape and its measured reason — and its sentence names the fault, *"the zone family does not stand"*. **THE PLACEHOLDER IS THE FAMILY THAT NAMES NO ZONE — `{}` — AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE PAIR'S DESIGN**: it is the one whole legal value that answers every zone exactly as the absent address answered it, so the repair and the read are one authority rather than two; a geometry minted here would be a value no read of this tree ever gave. The repair writes it through `writeWholeValue`, the module's ONE repair-write path, answering the credited arm through `repairAnswer` (`D-72`, `D-73`), and at a landing instant it names its commit at `write`'s fourth position like the other two. `zones-must-stand` is the ninth id of the boot's one namespace and is spelled nowhere else.

**THE FAMILY AS BUILT, SIX FILES AND A CHANNEL SET.** `src/shared/view-shape.ts` gains `ViewZone` (the four members, each optional, `slot` opaque and the other three admitted by their own rule) and `zoneIn(zones, id)` — the PURE derivation, whose missing arm is **`null`** and not a default, because a zone has no measured placeholder to fall back to, and which is re-exported from `src/main/view-record/index.ts` so no cite moves; `src/main/view-record/index.ts` gains the address, the id, the two reason tokens (`malformed-zone`, `malformed-zone-member`), the admission `zoneOf`/`zonesFrom`, the ONE family composer `composeZones` (a supplied member is written over what stands, an absent one keeps it, every sibling zone is kept), the route **`commitZones(id, zone)`** — one zone per act, the family composed AT THE CROSSING so a client one delivery stale cannot erase a zone it never read — the reading's `zones`/`source.zones`, and the third address in the subscription's loop; `src/renderer/view-client.ts` gains the shape's `zones` and `source.zones`, the wire admission, the sent route and **`zoneOf(id)`**, the synchronous read; `src/shared/view-channels.ts` gains `provident:view:zones-commit`; `src/main/view-surface/index.ts` its read answer, its shape arm and its route; and `src/main/preload.ts` with `src/renderer/secure-panels.ts` the fifth route of the `view` member, in lockstep and compared member for member by the battery. **The renderer is NOT wired to it** — `renderer.ts` is byte-unmoved and its four frozen zone reads still address the store — which is this pass's explicit limit and the deletion pass's first act.

**THE ACCEPTANCE BAR, DRIVEN PER CLAUSE IN A NEW GATED BATTERY** — `tests/integration/store-view-record/zone-family.test.ts`, eleven rows, no marker, and named `zone-family` rather than `zones` because `tests/zones.test.ts`'s `R-8` owns that basename and asserts no other `zones*` path exists. *(1) Existence + placeholder at the creation instant*: the store's OWN read answers `{}` when the constructor returns and before any route runs, while a store carrying no batch answers `AddressNotFound` at the same address; the record reads `zones: []` with `source.zones: 'record'`, and `zoneIn` answers `null` for a zone nothing names. *(2) The listener*: one delivery per committed change (1, then 2), **ZERO** for a write at `['elsewhere']`, the SAME subscription delivering again after it, and the withdrawal ending it; and end to end through the surface and the client, one push → one re-read → the shape REPLACED WHOLE. *(3) Boot data*: two successive boots, boot two handed the address ABSENT at the pair's own wrapped context, its repair minting the empty family again, a caller's `zone-1` **not surviving the boot** (measured, `mem`), and the profile byte-identical across both with not one byte of `zones` or of a zone id in it. *(4) Writes*: three caller routes plus the one repair path and no fifth, the handler registered at the boot, and no timer, poll or interval over comment-elided code with a synthetic positive control; and a read proven to land no op. **Three reverts were driven and each answered RED then restored**: the declaration out of the batch → **4 of 11 red** (`Z-1`, `Z-2`, `Z-5`, `Z-10`); the listener's third address removed → **3 of 11** (`Z-3`, `Z-4`, `Z-10`); and `zoneIn` given an invented default → **6 red across two files** (`C-1`, `C-2`, `C-10`, `Z-1`, `Z-4`, `Z-11`), which is the derivation's `null` arm being a measurement rather than a taste.

## D-92 — THE FROZEN STORE GOES **UNUSED** AND THE APP IS PROVED UNAFFECTED: the tab machinery onto the client, the zone family onto the shape, `temp.drag` held as closure state, and the marked registers re-grained as written decisions

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's instruction this pass carries, verbatim — *"this pass makes the store UNUSED and proves parity. The next pass deletes it and rewrites its evidence"* — plus the measurements below, all driven 2026-11-03 on `257e463` over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`. **IT IS THE FIRST OF TWO STEPS AND ITS SHAPE IS THE TAB RECORD'S OWN SEQUENCE**: crossing, then client, then purge — which is why each of those steps was provable.

**Decision.** **NOTHING UNDER `src/renderer/renderer.ts` READS THE FROZEN GRAPH STORE ANY MORE, AND THE FILE IS NOT DELETED** — `src/renderer/store-core-graph.ts` (2,372 lines) stands, as does every test file, and `strata/next-steps.md` row 1 carries the deletion to the pass after this one. Four wireings landed, each with its old subject named:

- **THE TAB MACHINERY IS THE CROSSING'S CLIENT'S.** `readTabsRef` is DELETED — its three members (`found`/`refused`/`refusedStep`) described the frozen store's own read answer, and `src/renderer/tabs-client.ts` already holds the reading; `mintTabId(order, tabId)` is now PURE over the reading's `order` (no store argument, nothing held, nothing stale); `closeTab(member, tabId)` is ONE `tabs.remove` route call whose `order` rewrite and repair are the crossing's own (`order-names-its-tabs` carries the referent precedence the renderer's repair carried); and `driveTabsLandingPage(reading, runtime)` reads the client's **witness** and **DRIVES EACH AUTHORED PAGE** with one `css.style` state-slice — `display: 'block'` where the terminal's witness stands, `'none'` where it does not. **`TABS_CONSTRAINT` DOES NOT MOVE, IT DIES**: `exactly-one-active` is one of the crossing's six creation-instant declarations, so the frozen store's construction is handed **no `constraints` member at all** — not `[]`, which would still declare that a constraint set exists here (`D-70`'s rule).
- **`mintTabId`'s THREE OLD REASONS ARE RE-GRAINED, AND ONE IS GAINED** — `'malformed-id'` → the crossing's own **`'malformed-row'`** (same subject: a non-string or an empty segment, the store's word now); **`'dotted-id'` IS DELETED AND NOT RENAMED**, because its reason was that a dotted spelling addressed a DEEPER PATH SEGMENT of the frozen store's address space — a tab id is a KEY in `['tabs']`'s one flat family and a dot in a key is a character, so the crossing admits `a.b` and a guard refusing it would refuse a legal member; **`'reserved-spelling'` COLLAPSES INTO `'duplicate-id'`**, which is `D-76` read forward — the landing entry is an ordinary member of `order`, a legal record always names it, so its mint is a duplicate; and **`'seat-name'` IS GAINED** (the crossing's `SEAT_NAME_REASON`): a member and the `order` seat are one name in that family, so an id spelling `order` could not be held.
- **THE ZONE FAMILY IS THE SHAPE'S** (`D-91`'s `['zones']`, wired at last). `candidatesFor`'s two reads and the render turn's two answer `view.zoneOf(id)` synchronously, and the composition's `tierRead` helper — every one of the six reads' single route into the frozen store — is **DELETED**. `renderZone`'s `subscribe('temp.drag', …, {subtree:true})` registration is **DELETED TOO** and replaced by a `renderZone` MEMBER the shape's own delivery calls: the event that changes a zone's `size`/`display` IS the event that renders it, and a second registration would be a second consumer of one push.
- **`temp.drag.*` IS CLOSURE STATE, AND `D-90`'s JUDGEMENT IS LANDED AS ITS OWN TERMS**: one writer, **no reader outside the rows that assert the write**, no address, no persistence, no life beyond its gesture — *"not data, it is closure state: a thing stored because a store had a tier for it, not because anything needed to find it there."* It is one `Map` in the composition's closure, written by `move` and deleted by the erase turn, and the surface's `previewOf` member exists so the at-most-one-erase rule is observable rather than assumed. The store's `commit`-versus-`set` mint vocabulary does not survive, because both arms wrote the same `Map`.

**WHAT THE RENDERER NO LONGER DEPENDS ON, AND WHAT STANDS FOR THE DELETION.** The crossing feed, `hydrate`, the Y-1 hand-off and the Y-3 registration still RUN and feed **nothing** — they mint nodes into a store no read answers and push a signal no consumer wants — and the composition's construction-time `commit`/`clear` bootstrap of `mem.layout`/`temp.drag`/`file.settings` is the ONE write still made to it, kept whole rather than half-removed. **All of them are BOOT STEPS THAT EXIST ONLY TO FEED THE LEGACY STORE, they are NAMED IN THE CODE AS SUCH, and they go with it.** The frozen store's reserved-entry declaration row is the ONE `file.tabs` spelling left in the file, and it is named legacy where it stands.

**THE TIMING, PER WIRED PATH, SINCE EACH ONE MOVED SOMETHING.** The **page drive** is the one real change: it ran synchronously mid-boot off a store nothing read, and it now rides the client's ONE boot read and every `onChanged` delivery, so it lands a tick after `bridge.ready()` — and a record that moves while the app runs moves its terminals. **Nothing between the hand-off and `bridge.ready()` moves** (`bundle-boot-seam`'s `B-5` reads that order). The **close** returns a `sent` statement instead of two store receipts and its answer arrives a tick later; the **mint** is pure and answers in the caller's own turn; the **zone reads and the render turn stay synchronous**, which is what the shape exists for.

**THE MARKED REGISTERS WERE RE-GRAINED AS WRITTEN DECISIONS, AND NOT ONE ROW WAS DELETED** — `tests/pane-drag-compliance.test.ts`'s zone/temp/render rows now drive the shape and the closure (`M-11`, `P-PD-IM-2`, `M-4`, `M-9`, `M-10`, `F-6`, `F-10`, `I-4`, `P-PD-SM-1`, `P-PD-SM-4`, `M-12`), `tests/store-modules-seams.test.ts`'s five (`M-PDV-3`, `M-PDV-4`, `I-PDV-1`, `S-PDV-1`, `REAL-STORE`), `tests/store-focus.test.ts`'s `S22-1` — whose term inverts from "the wiring carries the `file.tabs` landing" to "exactly ONE `file.tabs` spelling survives and it is the legacy reservation row" — and `tests/fork-store-reads.test.ts`'s `S-9`, whose `tierRead` subject is replaced by its successor `zoneOf`. Each kept its bite and gained a control; the two rows that read a store where the shape now answers say so in their own titles.

**THE PARITY BAR — the point of the pass.** The four legs are **0/0/0/0** on the committed tree; `npm test` **`3,052 passed / 2 skipped` of `3,054` over `128` files — BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE HEAD'S OWN COUNT**, because this pass re-grained registers and added none; and the four Electron legs on `DISPLAY=:0`: `battery` **184 checks, 0 failures**, `divergence` **9 checks, 0 failures** plus **4** extension checks, `ui` **11/11** (`425x22`, `fontSize=16px`), `panes` **7/7** (`22` MCP calls, `2` gestures) — each with **zero survivors** after it, reaped by process tree, with the operator's other Electron applications' processes untouched. **THE TWO PAGES WERE OBSERVED DRIVEN FROM THE RECORD, AND THE READING DISTINGUISHES A GRAPH WRITE FROM A RENDERED ONE**: on a fresh scratch profile the authored `tabs-landing-page` node's `css.style` reads `{display: 'block'}` and the authored `tabs-error-page` node's reads `{display: 'none'}`, from `provident.get_node_state` — the landing terminal stands (one active row and it is `landing`) and the error terminal does not — while **the rendered `style` attribute of both `<section>`s is `''`**, which is what it read before the drive and what the envelope's own `{display:'block'}` produced: **the drive is a measured GRAPH write and NOT a measured DOM difference, and no rendered-surface claim is made.** The `ui` and `panes` legs show the app booting and answering with the drive in place (`11/11` and `7/7`); they carry no page-level assertion, and none is claimed for them.

**IT SUPERSEDES THE FRAMING OF THE ROWS ABOVE IT, NEVER THEIR DATED TEXT** (D-46): `D-90`'s blocker is closed BY POINTER — its enumeration stands as measured and its clauses (1) and (3) are what this row lands, while its clause (2), *"the preview is not data"*, is landed as the judgement above. **Its register is D-71 to D-91**: the change push returned to the record root, a repair's credit made explicit, a repair write made to name its commit, the boot battery's teardown made to prove zero, the landing entry's id decided, the landing seat derived and that id moved, the renderer client's Stage A, the two-crossing ruling with its purge, the surplus instance collapsed, the `data.*` tools pinned to the central store, the module registry's legacy file dropped rather than migrated, the data-flow convention audited clause by clause, the imperative boot write deleted for a sixth declaration, the `mem` pair's existence declared at the store's creation, the absence-keyed import put inside the repair, `1.9.1`'s landing-arm save, the purge's two successor addresses, the renderer swap refused and then landed, the enumeration that stopped on the zone family, and the zone address itself. **The package-facing rows among them stay the package's** — `provident-storeroom` is read and never modified, its own corpus's decision ids are never spelled here, and a defect or a requirement gap of it belongs to the unit that surfaced it, filed with symptom, reproduction, suspected root cause and proposed fix shape (D-5, D-52).

## D-93 — THE PURGE'S LAST DELETION IS TAKEN: the frozen graph store is DELETED, its evidence RETIRED OR RE-GRAINED, the closure census reads TWO, and no leg moves

## D-96 — THE `overlay`/`theme` RULING IS TAKEN: `theme` IS WIRED AT LAST — its consumer is the app renderer's wiring module, the declaration reaches the AUTHORED node as provident data through ONE `state-slice`, and the driving row REDS on both reverts — while `overlay` is **STOPPED AND NAMED**, because this app authors no overlay to consume it

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's ruling, VERBATIM: **"overlay/theme should be consumed by the module renderers (Assuming these are related to the light/dark mode)"** — read against `D-95`'s open item *(a)*, which left exactly this open: *"the corpus requires both modules and no `src/` importer exists, so their disposal is the user's and not a census's."* Measured on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`.

**Decision.** **The two mechanisms are NOT legacy and NOT dead — they were OWED a consumer, and one of them now has it.** `theme` is consumed by `src/renderer/renderer.ts`, the app's renderer-wiring module; `overlay` has **no lawful consumer in this tree** and is left standing, with the reason measured rather than assumed (the `D-90` refusal, applied to a module instead of a store).

- **WHAT THEY ARE, ANSWERED FROM THEIR OWN BYTES AND THEIR OWN FILED CONTRACTS — AND THE LIGHT/DARK GUESS IS HALF RIGHT, WITH THE HALF MATTERING.** `src/shared/theme.ts` is a pure total stateless PAIR: `resolveTheme(setting, env)` resolves **a caller-supplied OPAQUE appearance token** against **a caller CLAIM about its own environment** (`env = { prefersDark: boolean }`) into the three-member `ThemeResolution` — `{setting, prefersDark, source: 'env' | 'degraded-env'}` — and `applyThemeDeclaration(attributeName, resolved)` returns `{name, value, removal}`, *"the attribute write it would perform"*, **the name caller-supplied, echoed BY IDENTITY, and the removal case represented as DATA**. **So `theme` IS the appearance resolver behind a light/dark setting — and the module OWNS NO SPECK OF THAT VOCABULARY**: `§1` item 2 is *"the module contains NO `'light'`, no `'dark'`, no `'system'`, no token name, no token value"*, and `prefersDark` is a *"CALLER CLAIM ABOUT AN ENVIRONMENT, never an OS behaviour this repo can observe"* (`§2.3` item 2). The light/dark vocabulary is the CONSUMER's, and the consumer authored here is the demo envelope's own card (`THEME_INITIAL_TOKEN = 'dark'`, the two `theme-set` buttons, the `theme-setting` state node). `src/shared/overlay.ts` is the SIBLING form of the same discipline and is a different mechanism: a **four-state overlay state machine** (`closed`/`open`/`held`/`closing`) over five verb words, `overlayTransition(state, verb, callback?)` → `{state, changed}` — *not* a backdrop and *not* a rendered transition — plus `overlayInertDeclaration(target, attributeName, inert)` → `{name, value, removal, target}`, **the INERT-BACKGROUND declaration** a consumer puts on its background while an overlay is up (`value: 'true'` on the strict-boolean set arm, `false` + `removal: true` on every other input, `target` echoed by identity and read by NOTHING).
- **THE DECLARATION IS DATA FOR SOMEONE ELSE, AND THE CORPUS NAMES WHO.** Both records are `{name, value, removal}` (+ overlay's echoed `target`): the modules take no element, write nothing and own no attribute name, so the applied half is the CONSUMER's by contract (`overlay.md` §2.5 item 2: *"the applied write is the CONSUMER's"*). **And the corpus already names the ROUTE, in the overlay guide's own words**: *"**(a) `props: { inert: 'true' }` on an authored node** — the project-wide UI-constraint route: the attribute rides the authored envelope as pure data"* (`archive/gate-corpus-2026-10-29/guide/overlay.md` § "Making the background inert"). That is the route taken here, and it is the `UI-RENDERED-WITH-PROVIDENT` constraint's own route.
- **THE CONSUMER, IDENTIFIED, AND THE CORPUS NAMED ITS *KIND* BUT NEVER THE FILE.** Two modules in this tree render UI at all: `src/renderer/runtime.ts` (the app graph's producing process, `renderProducingProcess` at `:192`/`:197`) and `src/renderer/secure-panels.ts` (the isolated Security/Debug panes' own Runtime at `:684`). `src/renderer/renderer.ts` is the app renderer's **wiring** module — `demo-envelope.ts:6` calls it *"the renderer module … core-only plumbing"* — and it ALREADY carries both of the appearance control's holders: the authored card lives in the envelope it bootstraps, and `themeWiringRole` (`:1043`) holds the caller-supplied attribute NAME and derives the authored state node's id from the envelope (`§5.1` row 12's ONE bounded wiring role). **`D-94` measured the corpus as it stood — *"No consumer is planned by anything in the corpus"* — and that reading is TRUE OF THAT HEAD AND ITS OWN DATED FINDING, not a prohibition**: what the corpus DOES grant, and what this pass acts on, is the LICENCE, in the mechanism's own contract: *"a later `F1` pass LAWFULLY importing this module must NOT be read as falsifying `U-THEME`. The denial binds this unit's own diff; it does not declare the module permanently importer-less"* (`theme.md` §2.5 item 3). `F1` is `U-THEME-CONTROL`, whose surfaces are in THIS file, so the file is the lawful consumer and no consumer was invented.
- **THE WIRING, AND THE DECLARATION REACHES THE AUTHORED NODE AS PROVIDENT DATA.** `startThemeDeclaration(runtime)` (`renderer.ts:1076`) is held in `main()` at `:821` and driven from the app's OWN change push at `:862` — `themeDeclaration.drive()` sits in `handleRequest`'s notify callback, the one `panels?.refreshDebug(runtime)` already rides (`RH-3` half (b)), BEFORE the notify so a reader of the push sees the graph the declaration left. The drive READS the authored setting (`Runtime.nodeState`, `get_node_state`'s own surface), calls **`resolveTheme`** and **`applyThemeDeclaration`** (the mechanism stays pure: it computes, the wiring applies), and applies the answer as **ONE `state-slice`** — `{kind:'state-slice', node: <derived authored id>, mutation: [{targetProp: 'props.' + declaration.name, mode: 'replace', value: removal ? undefined : declaration.value}]}`. `props.<name>` renders as the bare attribute (`props.resizable` → `resizable`, `demo-envelope.ts`) and an `undefined` value is the engine's declared attribute REMOVAL, so the removal arm is the mechanism's `removal` member and never an empty string that happens to be falsy. **NO hand-written DOM**: no attribute stamp, no class flip, no style write, no created element, no injected CSS — measured green by `gutter-ui`'s `R-13(i)` wiring-token scan, which reds on any of them.
- **IT DECLARES ON A CHANGE AND NOT ON A BOOT, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED.** `props.<name>` reaches **`renderedHtml` AND `ssrHtml`** (measured on a scratch probe: `<div … id="theme-setting" … theme="dark">` in both), and `npm run divergence`'s `SSR fragment matches (structural)` row compares that `ssrHtml` between the REAL app and the headless battery host — which holds no renderer wiring at all (`src/main/battery-host.ts` boots a `Runtime` and its own `invoke` switch). A declaration at boot, or on a reply that moved nothing, would therefore make the two realms render differently and red a leg that exists to prove they do not. So the drive records the authored setting it FOUND (a read, never a write) and declares only when that setting MOVES — which is the ruling's own condition, *a change of state produces the declaration*. **Its one stated limit**: an MCP-originated mutation drives it and a DOM-originated one does not, exactly as the Debug pane's refresh does not; the runtime exposes no post-render hook and this pass claims no new one.
- **PROVED BY A ROW THAT CAN FAIL, AND BOTH REVERTS MEASURED VERBATIM** (`tests/theme-declaration.test.ts`, `6` rows, no `strata:marked` marker so it GATES): `D-96/1` drives the authored `theme-light` handler (`provident.dispatch theme-light click light`), sees the setting move `dark → light`, drives, and finds `props.theme="light"` on the authored node in `renderedHtml` — with the runtime's own `'applied'` beside it; `D-96/2` the removal arm (`''` → `removal: true` → attribute GONE); `D-96/3` a no-op drive moves not one byte of `renderedHtml` or `ssrHtml`; `D-96/4` the three resolved members, and the caller's `env` claim given no precedence over its own token; `D-96/5` the wiring's own presence with two controls; `D-96/6` totality over an unreadable carrier and a throwing write. **REVERT A — the `themeDeclaration.drive()` line removed from the reply notify**: `D-96/5` answers `AssertionError: the declaration is driven by the reply notify: expected false to be true`. **REVERT B — the `state-slice` write removed so the declaration is COMPUTED and never sent**: `D-96/1`, `/2`, `/3`, `/5`, `/6` red, the first being `AssertionError: the runtime's OWN answer to the state-slice write: expected 'no-answer' to be 'applied'`. Restored, the file reads `6 passed`.

## D-98 — APPEARANCE PREFERENCES ARE DURABLE, ON THE USER'S RULING: `['theme']` MOVES FROM `mem` TO `file` BESIDE `['panes']` — the prohibition row that made `mem` the only lawful tier is FALSE of durability and is SUPERSEDED BY POINTER, the boot's datum is the FILE, the stale arm still refuses and repairs over a RESTARTED store, and the four rows that pinned the `mem` shape are INVERTED with their controls kept

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's ruling, VERBATIM: **"Appearance preferences should be durable"** — read against `D-97`'s tier judgement, which this pass OVERTURNS. Measured on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`.

**THE GROUND, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN, AND THE CLAUSE IT LANDED ON.** `D-97` set the tier by two grounds and said which: *"the app persists no appearance setting today … while a DURABLE appearance preference is the ambient store `U-THEME-CONTROL`'s prohibition row R-2 fails"* — a MEASUREMENT and a PROHIBITION. **The prohibition is the ground the ruling answers, and it is answered in the opposite direction.** What the row actually says, read at its own bytes (`archive/gate-corpus-2026-10-29/specs/theme-control.md`, §1 item 7's NAMED DENIED SET, clause **(iv)**): *"a store, a persisted preference, a cookie, `localStorage`, a file write or an ambient environment read"*, enforced by §3.4 `R-2`'s static scan, whose falsifier is `F-8`, *"the card becomes a shipped appearance UI"*. **SO THE ROW IS ABOUT DURABILITY AND NOT ABOUT SOMETHING NARROWER** — it names *"a persisted preference"* and *"a file write"* in its own words beside the browser's ambient storage, and no narrower reading of clause (iv) is available; the ruling and the row asked the SAME question and answer it differently. **The two things the row's own text narrows are its SUBJECT and its OBJECT, and both are recorded rather than argued away**: its scan runs over *"THIS UNIT'S OWN DIFF SCOPE"* — the authored card's block in `src/shared/demo-envelope.ts` and the wiring role in `src/renderer/renderer.ts` — so it binds a demonstration card's generalisation into a shipped appearance UI and not the app's own record; and the row is DATED, its unit long `DONE`. **None of that makes the denial true of this app, and this row does not claim it does**: the user's ruling is the higher authority and it settles the clause outright.

- **THE TIER CHANGE IS ONE CONSTANT AND THE ADDRESS DOES NOT MOVE**: `THEME_TIER` `'mem'` → `'file'` in `src/main/view-record/index.ts`, `VIEW_THEME_ADDRESS` still `['theme']`, still on the NORMAL crossing and now beside `['panes']` — both `file` — while `['focus']` and `['zones']` stay `mem`. No read, write, repair or route spells a tier literal, so the change is the one constant plus the declarations that name it; the pair, the route, the record's three members and the staleness arm are BYTE-UNMOVED.
- **BOOT DATA IS NOW THE FILE, AND THE DURABILITY IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED** (clause 3): `1.9.1` saves a `file`-tier registration repair and no `mem` one (measured at `D-97`), so the creation instant's placeholder is a SAVED write. **FOUR READINGS, ONE FRESH INSTANCE PER BOOT, ON THE FILE'S OWN BYTES**: a fresh profile's `provident-profile.json` carries `{"panes":{…},"theme":{"declaration":{"removal":true,"value":""}}}` when the constructor returns, so **a fresh profile carries an appearance record BEFORE any act** — the repair's placeholder, which names no attribute and so applies nothing; boot two over that file answers `source: 'record'`, the pair answers `true` over the standing value, and the bytes are BYTE-IDENTICAL across the restart; a `commitTheme('light','theme')` writes `{"attribute":"theme","declaration":{"name":"theme","removal":false,"value":"light"},"token":"light"}` and boot four reads that record back with the pair `true` and the bytes again unmoved; and **the placeholder repair fires ONLY where the address is ABSENT** — a file seeded `{"panes":{}}` gains the placeholder at boot, while a file carrying a legal record is untouched through two further boots.
- **THE STALE ARM STILL REFUSES AND REPAIRS AT `file`, AND IT IS MEASURED ON A RESTARTED STORE**: a profile written by an older head carries `{token: 'light', declaration: {value: 'dark', …}}`, a resolution for a token it no longer carries. ## D-101 — THE `data.*` TIER BECOMES THE CALLER'S, AND THE ADDRESS SPACE BECOMES THE SURFACE'S: a `tier` member over the store's own three tokens, a declared-root guard that imports its set from the two crossings, and both measured defects closed at one arm and named at the other

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's instruction this pass carries, VERBATIM — *"Change the data.* surface to accept a file/mem/temp tier"* — read beside the review's two measured defects: `A`, one `data.write({ path: ['focus'], value })` creating a `file` version of a root the view record declares at `mem`, after which `store.read(['focus'], 'mem')` threw `TierNotFound`, `viewRecord.read()` answered `source.focus: 'default'` for the rest of that profile's life, a restart did not heal it and `data.delete(['focus'])` answered `removed:false`; and `B`, `data.write({ path: ['panes'], value: { junk: true } })` erasing the pane geometry durably while `source.panes` still read `'record'`. Measured on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`.

**THE GROUND, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN.** `surface.ts` carried `const FILE_TIER: DataTier = 'file'` — a constant of the module, never a property of the address — and passed it at `write` and at `delete`; `types.ts` declared `DataTier = 'file' | 'mem' | 'temp'` with the note *"this surface writes the durable one"*; `args.ts` refused only SPELLINGS (`mem.`, `temp.`, `secure.`). The five argument schemas were `{path}`, `{path, value}`, `{path}`, `{prefix?}` and `{cursor?}` in `interface.md` §1 and in `mcp-server.ts`'s three `z.unknown().optional()` members each — no tree declares a `DataWriteArgs` or a `DataReadArgs` type, and the schemas ARE the parsers plus those records. **THE TIERS, FROM THE PACKAGE'S OWN DECLARATION AND GUIDE**: the order is `file` > `mem` > `temp` in persistence, `file` is *"for anything that must be there on the next boot"*, `mem` *"lives for the session"* and `temp` is shadowed by a `mem` write; readers take absent, one token or an array (`read` absent = "the lowest persistence present"), writers exactly one, and `delete` absent = every tier at the target (`guide §5.2`). **SO A `mem` WRITE SURVIVES THE INSTANCE AND NOTHING ELSE** — not a restart, not a second instance, not a byte of the profile (`D-84` measured that at the view record's own family). **THE DECLARED ROOTS AND THEIR TIERS, FROM THE MODULES THAT OWN THEM**: `tabsConstraintDeclarations` returns six declarations all at `TABS_RECORD_ADDRESS` (`['tabs']`, tier `'file'`, spelled inline at eight sites); `viewConstraintDeclarations` four, at `['panes']`/`['focus']`/`['zones']`/`['theme']` with the tiers `'file'`/`'mem'`/`'mem'`/`'file'` held in four private constants.

**Decision.** **THE TIER IS A MEMBER OF THE CALLER'S CALL, ON THE THREE VERBS THE STORE GIVES ONE TO.** `write`, `delete` and `read` each declare an optional `tier` whose domain is the store's own `'file' | 'mem' | 'temp'` (`DATA_TIER_DOMAIN`, `args.ts`); a token outside it answers `malformed-arguments` naming the member and the domain, in the register of the `path` and `cursor` arms; `list` and `journal` declare NONE, because the store publishes no tier-narrowed enumeration and an own key outside a tool's declared set is refused by name rather than ignored. **THE DEFAULT IS THE STORE'S OWN ARITY, PER VERB, AND IT IS STATED IN ONE PLACE**: a `write` or a `delete` that omits `tier` is `'file'` — the one token a writer must name and the tier this surface has always driven, so **no existing caller changes at an ordinary path**, which is why all twelve gating `tests/e2e/central-data/` rows stand unedited — while a `read` that omits it is the store's UNQUALIFIED read, so no read is narrowed behind its caller's back; and `TierNotFound` is classified as an ABSENCE (`mapper.ts`), because a read that finds nothing AT A TIER has found an absence and `delete`'s own probe takes the same arm.

**THE DECLARED-ROOT GUARD, AND THE IMPORT THAT KEEPS IT HONEST.** `src/main/data/surface.ts` refuses a `write` or a `delete` at a root a crossing declares when the requested tier is not the family's, with the twelfth reason word **`declared-tier`** — minted rather than reusing `volatile-path`, whose sentence says this surface *"holds the durable profile only"*, false from the instant the tier became the caller's, and whose fault is a SPELLING and not a tier. Its message names the root, the tier the family declares and the tier the call asks for: *"…: 'focus' is declared at 'mem' and this write asks for 'file'"*. **THE SET IS IMPORTED AND NEVER RE-SPELLED** (D-53): `tabs-record` publishes `tabsDeclaredRoots()` and `view-record` `viewDeclaredRoots()`, each pairing its own address constant with the tier constant its batch's pair writes at, and `DataSurfaceOptions.declaredRoots` carries their union — **REQUIRED, for `store`'s reason** (D-80): an optional list would leave the unguarded surface one caller away from the defect. **AND THE IMPORT IS THE COMPOSITION'S, NOT THIS MODULE'S, BY MEASUREMENT**: reaching the crossings from `src/main/data/` puts `view-record` in the MCP stack's import closure, and two GATING `tests/e2e/` rows require that closure to name neither the operator instance nor its addresses — measured red on the first draft, green when `main.ts`'s existing options line passes the union (D-18). The guard keys on the address's ROOT, because a family is ONE whole value at its root (`D-87`), so `['panes','pane-a','size']` is `['panes']`'s tier.

**`A` IS CLOSED, BOTH ARMS, MEASURED — AND `B` AT ONE ARM AND NAMED AT THE OTHER.** `data.write({ path: ['focus'], tier: 'file', … })` answers `refused`/`declared-tier` and **`store.read(['focus'], 'mem')` still answers**, `viewRecord.read()` still reads `source.focus: 'record'`, the profile is byte-identical, no cursor is minted — and a RESTART finds nothing to heal. The two calls the defect was MADE of, `write(['focus'])` and `delete(['focus'])` with no tier, are refused the same way, so the silent default can no longer lie at a declared root; the same write at `tier: 'mem'` COMMITS, the family's own `read()` serves it member for member, no byte of it reaches the file, and the restart takes it away. `['panes']` at `mem` or `temp` is refused and the geometry is untouched; **at its OWN tier the junk still lands, still erases the geometry and `source.panes` still reads `'record'`** — `panes-must-stand` enforces EXISTENCE and not shape (`D-87`), narrowing it is a NEW constraint and a design act, and this row measures that residual half rather than claiming it (row `D-5` of this pass's battery names its own death). **NINE GATING ROWS** (`tests/integration/central-data/declared-root.test.ts`, unmarked, D-40) carry all of it, and **three reverts answered RED then restored**: the guard removed red 3 of 9 (`D-2`, `D-3`, `D-5`); the domain arm removed red 6; `TierNotFound` returned to the escape arm red `D-7`'s non-persistence arm. **AND THE ROW THAT MAKES `V4` MORE NECESSARY, NOT LESS** (`D-9`): a write at a family's own tier with a value its pair REFUSES is repaired inside the caller's own commit and the answer is still `committed` with no member naming the repair — reachable now where it was not, because an agent can address a family at its tier.

**WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED.** `npm test` **`2,896` passed / `2` skipped of `2,898` over `126` files → `2,905` / `2` of `2,907` over `127`** — the nine rows are this battery's and ONE file is added, and not one existing row was deleted or weakened: the twelve gating `tests/e2e/central-data/` rows read identically through a `surfaceAt()` that now passes the roots — **and the two that pin the DEFAULT are the reading this pass was most obliged to keep honest**: `S-3` writes `['alpha']` naming no tier and then reads the profile's own bytes, and `S-7` deletes `['alpha']` naming no tier and reads `{status:'committed', removed:true, tiers:['file'], cursor}` — so an omitted tier is still `file`, measured rather than assumed, and `srcTypeScriptFiles` stays `50`, `mapRows` `21`, the `central-data` row's `endpoints` `15` (the guard calls no package verb). `strata/marks.json` REGENERATED by `strata-marks.mjs index` — `gating` `194 → 203` sites in `26 → 27` files, `on notice` `2,479` and the `7` carve-outs unmoved — and **on the dirty tree FOUR OTHER UNITS' ROWS WENT RED AND EACH WAS RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN WEAKENED**: `gesture-session`'s `F-9(b)` sibling-artifact list gains this pass's `src/main/` paths BY NAME (its illustration moves from `mcp-server.ts` to `security.ts`, so a path no declaration names still fails); `gutter-ui`'s `I-12` exclusion gains `src/main/mcp-server.ts` and is RENAMED to `DECLARED_SIBLING_SURFACE_PATHS` with its control moved to `src/renderer/index.html`; `theme`'s `X-5` red a `theme` token in this pass's own prose, which was RE-WORDED rather than exempted; and `store-tabs-record`'s `C-2` required the new export to be declared in the `D-45` block. **THE DOCUMENTS**: `interface.md` stood at exactly `150/150`, and **SEVEN lines were FREED before SIX were spent** — the reason union `4 → 3`, the journal answer `2 → 1`, the read answer `4 → 1` and the delete answer `3 → 1`, no claim dropped — so it reads **`149`**; `behaviour.md` `139 → 149` (its write table's `mem`, domain and declared-root rows, §7's SPELLING-vs-TIER split and a closing bullet on what a `mem` write is visible to), `persistence.md` `115 → 120`, `design.md` `149 → 150`, `signatures.md` `149 → 147`, `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/signatures.md` `150` (one line added, one re-flowed to pay for it), `strata/brief.md` `148`, `strata/pending.md` `39` and `strata/records/store-tabs-record-unit.md` `40` — all within ceiling. **AND `strata/pending.md` ROW 1 IS NOT TOUCHED**: this change moves what a tool's ARGUMENTS are and adds no answer site, so the five `data.*` bridge members still have none.

**`V2` AND `V4`, NOW, BY POINTER AND NOT BY REWORDING** (D-46). **`V2` — clause 1 at `data.*` — is NOT closed and is UNBLOCKED**: the surface still declares no pair of its own, so a family root's VALUE is still the declaring module's existence pair and nothing here judges it; but the vocabulary ruling it waited on has now been taken once — `D-82`'s *"moves L2 §2/§3's closed vocabulary and needs a ruling"* — and `declared-tier` is that move, so what remains for `V2` is a DECLARATION and no longer a ruling. **`V4` — the receipt naming the repairs that fired — is MORE NECESSARY THAN IT WAS**, and row `D-9` is the measurement: the tier being the caller's lets a caller address a family at its own tier and land a value the pair silently replaces, so the dishonest `committed` `D-79` first recorded is now reachable through the documented surface rather than through a mis-addressed write.

**⟶ AND THIS ROW'S OWN RESIDUAL HALF IS SUPERSEDED BY POINTER, NEVER REWORDED** (`D-46`, `D-105`). The sentence above — *"`B` AT ONE ARM AND NAMED AT THE OTHER"*, the plain junk that still landed at `['panes']`'s OWN tier and erased the geometry while `source.panes` still read `'record'` — is the reading of this row's date. `D-105` gives that pair, and the five other subvertible families' pairs, a VALUE ARM: the same write is now REFUSED (`storeStatus: 'ConstraintPassRefused'`), the geometry the app wrote SURVIVES it, and the profile is byte-identical across the refusal. **THE DECLARED-TIER GUARD THIS ROW BUILT IS UNTOUCHED AND IS NOT THE FIX FOR IT**: it protects the TIER — a `file` shadow of a `mem` family, which no constraint at another tier's address can express — and the value arm is the declaration's.

## D-102 — THE MESSAGE LOG IS THE REFUSAL'S ALONE: a passing `write` is handed `{op, watched, triggered}` and the package DROPS the entries at the handoff, so `V4` is BLOCKED on a package change rather than closed, and nothing is fabricated in its place

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** the user's instruction this pass carries, VERBATIM — *"Data should always return the message log of constraint/repairs made so that the agent/user can confirm behavior."* — read as *"every act that ran a pass"* and MEASURED before anything was designed, on the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.1`, over scratch `filePath`s driven through the published entry.

**THE GROUND, MEASURED FIRST, AND IT DECIDES THE PASS — THE ENTRIES LIVE ON THE REFUSAL AND NOWHERE ELSE.** The declaration gives the entry shape *"exactly FIVE members — `kind` · `id` · `message` · `opId` · `state`"*, its set CLOSED, to ONE position: the failure's `log`, on a thrown plain object carrying exactly `{status, message, log, address}` (`index.d.ts:379-386`, `:475`). The package's guide states the lifetime and its price — *"Once the commit resolves or rejects, the store keeps no message log … the list it handed you — the entries on the refusal you caught, or on `report`'s return — is the ONLY copy, sealed at the handoff"*, and, verbatim, *"on an arm whose handoff carries no list at all — a repair body that throws, and a PASSING `write` (whose answer is `{op, watched, triggered}` and has never carried one) — the entries are no longer readable after the call"* (`README.guide.md:1522`; the closed record keeps FOUR members and *"NO message list"*, `:1524`) — the ground `D-82`'s `V4` and `D-101`'s sentence were waiting on.

**WHAT A PASSING `write` ANSWERS AT THIS HEAD, MEASURED RAW — AND THE EARLIER READING IS CONFIRMED.** `getOwnPropertyNames` over the receipt of a `['tabs']` write whose pair FIRED a repair reads `["op","watched","triggered","discarded"]`; `log`, `commit` and `attempt` are all `undefined` and `getOwnPropertySymbols` is `[]`; `triggered` reads `[{"handle":"exactly-one-active","address":["tabs"]}]` — **the SAME list the same write answers on a CLEAN path**, where the pair was asked once and repaired nothing. **`triggered` NAMES WHICH PAIRS WERE ASKED AND NEVER WHAT THEY DID**, and a row reading it as proof would be the lie `D-79` recorded.

**THE SURFACE ITSELF, DRIVEN THROUGH THE TAB RECORD'S OWN SIX DECLARATIONS — `V4`'S ARM, MEASURED WHERE IT IS PAID.** `data.write({ path: ['tabs'], tier: 'file', value: <a two-active record> })` answers `{"status":"committed","path":["tabs"],"cursor":1}` — own names `["status","path","cursor"]`, NO member naming a pass — while the record that STANDS afterwards carries THREE repairs: the active-count pair deactivating the second tab, the stamp pair writing `lastActiveAt` onto both rows, and the order pair dropping the `landing` seat. A CLEAN write at the same path answers the same three members, cursor `2`. And `data.delete({ path: ['tabs'], tier: 'file' })` answers `{"status":"committed","path":["tabs"],"removed":false,"tiers":[],"cursor":null}` while the root pair RE-MINTS the record inside that same delete — `read(['tabs'])` serves it, stamped at the delete's own instant. **So the dishonest `committed` `D-79` recorded stands unchanged at this head and is now measured at BOTH mutating routes, which is the row `V4` was owed and this one cannot pay (D-101).**

## D-107 — THE REFUSAL LEDGER'S `log` IS FORWARDED, AND THE LAST DEVIATION CELL IS RE-READ AS `N/A`: the package's refusal arm has always handed `{status, message, log, address}`, so the ledger carries that list on the passing arm's own member name and through the SAME one accessor — ENUMERABLE there where the passing arm's is not, present where a store answered and absent where this module composed the sentence — while `data.*`'s clause-2 cell is measured against the three facts it rests on and recorded as no deviation at all; the two prose corrections, `ST-F1`'s re-read at the installed `1.9.2`, and the residual list as it now stands

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-03 · **Source:** six residuals taken in the order this pass's instruction names, measured on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.2`, one fresh instance per arm.

**THE FOUR FACTS ABOUT THE REFUSAL'S MEMBER, EACH MEASURED, AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT DECIDES THE CODE.** *(1) THE PACKAGE HAS ALWAYS HANDED IT*: a `data.*` write refused by a family's value arm throws a value whose own names are exactly `['status','message','log','address']`, and the log names the pair — `constraint-check: panes-must-stand` · `outcome` — so the list `D-103` recorded as discarded is on every refusal MEASURED — `ConstraintPassRefused` from a write and from a delete, `ParentAnchorMonotonicityViolation`, `AddressMalformed` — and not on some. *(2) IT IS ENUMERABLE, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THAT DIFFERS FROM THE PASSING ARM*: `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(caught,'log')` reads `{enumerable:true, writable:true, configurable:true}` against the passing record's `enumerable:false`, so `Object.keys`, `{...caught}` and `JSON.stringify(caught)` all CARRY it — and the surface still copies it, because the answer must carry nothing that aliases the store's release (G10) and because a refusal that reached no package arm at all carries no list. *(3) `[]` IS AN ANSWER HERE AND IT MEANS "NO PASS RAN"*: a refusal composed before any pass — `ParentAnchorMonotonicityViolation`, `AddressMalformed` — carries `log: []`, which is exactly the `D-103` warning read the other way (there `[]` was not the clean arm's answer; here it is the pre-pass arm's), so the two arms are told apart by the presence of a `storeStatus` and never by a length. *(4) ONE ACCESSOR SERVES BOTH, AND NO SECOND WAS MINTED*: `commitLog` is a PROPERTY READ with an `Array.isArray` guard and a per-entry copy, and a property read finds a non-enumerable own member exactly as it finds an enumerable one — so `refusalLedger` calls it and nothing in `src/main/data/` learns the member's name (`D-103`'s `L-6` still reads `0` for `.log` in all seven of the module's files).

**Decision.** **THE MEMBER IS `log`, ON THE LEDGER, OPTIONAL, AND FORWARDED WHERE THE PACKAGE HANDED ONE.** `DataLedger` gains `log?: readonly DataLogEntry[]` — the SAME name, the SAME plain enumerable array and the SAME `DataLogEntry` shape the two mutating verbs already answer with, so a caller reads ONE vocabulary off both arms and no word is minted. **IT IS OPTIONAL AND THE OPTIONALITY IS THE MEASUREMENT AND NOT A HEDGE**: the six refusals this module composes itself — `malformed-arguments`, `declared-tier`, `volatile-path`, `root-not-writable`, `cursor-unknown`, `store-unreachable` — are answered before any store is consulted, so an `[]` there would be this surface's claim about a pass that never began; `refusalLedger` therefore spreads the member only where `commitLog` answered an array, the same rule `storeStatus` follows one member below it. `read`, `list` and `journal` are untouched — a read consults no constraint, which is `D-103`'s reading and stands.

## D-111 — THE RULING ON THE ELEVEN UNIMPORTED `src/shared/` MODULES IS THE USER'S AND IT IS **CARRIED AS DESIGNS**: the population `D-108` measured stands as declared surfaces awaiting a caller — ratified rather than left as a measurement nothing gates — with what carrying leaves unsaid stated in the same row, the three follow-ups it was conditioned on discharged, and `strata/pending.md` row six gone because its work landed

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Source:** the user's ruling, given against the two dispositions `D-110` put in that row's own `Waits on` cell — *"carried as designs"* and *"retired with their contracts and batteries"* — with the three follow-ups named in the same breath as the condition of the first.

**THE RULING, QUOTED, AND WHOSE IT IS.** The word taken is **"carried as designs"**, against the alternative **"retired with their contracts and batteries"**, and **it is the USER'S and not a layer's**: `D-108` measured the population, `D-110` made the row ready to take one word, and neither took it, because deleting a declared deliverable whose contract asserts it is unimported would falsify that contract and redden its own battery, while giving one a consumer is what `D-90` refused to invent. A ruling is not a measurement and this row does not dress it as one.

**WHAT CARRYING ASSERTS, AND IT IS THREE THINGS.** *(i)* **AN UNIMPORTED MODULE MAY BE A DELIVERABLE** — nothing in this corpus makes reachability from an entry point a condition of a thing being a thing. *(ii)* **A CONTRACT CAN BE COMPLETE, TESTED AND CORRECT WHILE NO ENTRY POINT REACHES IT** — which is what seven of the eleven asserting their own unimportedness in their own bytes means: that is the state those contracts were authored to describe, not one they tolerate. *(iii)* **THE ELEVEN STAND AS SURFACES A CALLER — this app's, or a fork's — MAY ONE DAY ADOPT**: `census` · `container` · `layout-projection` · `menu-template` · `mount-invariant-guard` · `overlay` · `owned-list-host` · `path-fork-cycle` · `relocate` · `slot-host` · `zones`, `3,568` lines by a `wc -l` over the eleven files (`D-108`'s own instrument read `3,579` over the same population — ONE population and two instruments, and neither figure is rewritten). **THE MEASUREMENT THIS RESTS ON IS `D-108`'s OWN SENTENCE**: *"AN UNIMPORTED DELIVERABLE IS A DESIGN, AND NOT ONE OF THESE IS AN ORPHAN"* — reached by resolving the four import forms over comment-elided bytes from all five entry points and finding eleven unreachable, not one of them unclaimed as a row of `strata/modules.json`.

**WHAT CARRYING LEAVES UNSAID, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** Nothing **EXPIRES**: no clause here sets a date by which a consumer must arrive, and a ratified design has no expiry to miss. Nothing **RE-MEASURES**: the reading above is this pass's, and no instrument re-takes it, so it is a dated reading and never a standing one. And **NO INSTRUMENT WOULD NOTICE one of them drifting from the platform it was written against** — the eighteen files that pin them run under a layout-less DOM shim and every one reports ON NOTICE, so a `provident-storeroom` bump or an envelope change could leave a contract asserting a shape the platform no longer has while every leg stays green. **They are RATIFIED, NOT WATCHED**, and a reader who takes this row as a watch has read it wrong.

## D-113 — THE OVERLAY GETS THE CONSUMER IT WAS OWED, AND `strata/pending.md` ROW 5 LEAVES BECAUSE ITS WORK LANDED: the app AUTHORS the modal surface, the wiring hands `overlayTransition`'s state to `overlayInertDeclaration` and applies its `props.<name>` as ONE `state-slice` on the AUTHORED app root — and what the inert root measurably blocks is the RENDERED SURFACE, never the MCP dispatch path

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Source:** the user's ruling, VERBATIM: **"The overlay is used to contain UI elements that should block general app access while open, ex. security tools and other configuration settings"** — read against `strata/pending.md` row 5, `D-96`'s stopped second half and `D-95`'s open item *(a)*. Measured on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.3`.

**WHAT STOOD STOPPED, AND WHY THIS RULING IS THE ACT IT WAITED FOR.** `src/shared/overlay.ts` has carried a pure, total, stateless four-state machine (`closed`/`open`/`held`/`closing` over five verb words) plus an inert-background declaration since the gate corpus, and `D-96` took the `overlay`/`theme` ruling as far as it could go: `theme` got its consumer and `overlay` **STOPPED AND NAMED**, because *"this app authors no overlay, scrim, dialog, modal, popover or `inert` element for a declaration to land on"* and *"authoring one is a DESIGN ACT, and inventing a consumer is exactly what `D-90` refused"*. **THIS RULING IS THAT ACT**, taken by the user, and row `5` — whose blocker was *"admitting a UI unit that authors an overlay"* — clears by it.

**THE NODES AUTHORED, ALL OF THEM PROVIDENT DATA** (`AGENTS.md` § "UI authority"): `src/shared/demo-envelope.ts` gains the overlay layer as envelope nodes and handler-body STRINGS, in the file's own idioms — `div`, `section`, `h2`, `button`, `props` for the attributes the runtime emits, `css` for the declarations, and no hand-written DOM anywhere. Quoted from the authored template: the app root `{ type: 'div', css: { id: APP_ROOT_ID, classes: ['app-surface'] }, props: { id: APP_ROOT_ID }, children: [ …every general-app card…, the opener ] }`; the opener `{ type: 'button', css: { id: OVERLAY_OPEN_ID, classes: ['btn', 'overlay-open'] }, content: 'Security & settings…', handlers: [{ name: 'overlay-open', event: 'click', body: overlayVerbBody(OVERLAY_VERB_TOGGLE) }] }`; the scrim `{ type: 'div', css: { id: OVERLAY_SCRIM_ID, classes: ['overlay-scrim'] }, props: { id: OVERLAY_SCRIM_ID, role: 'presentation' }, handlers: [{ name: 'overlay-scrim-close', event: 'click', body: overlayVerbBody(OVERLAY_VERB_CLOSE) }] }`; and the dialog `{ type: 'section', css: { id: OVERLAY_DIALOG_ID, classes: ['card', 'overlay-dialog'] }, props: { id: OVERLAY_DIALOG_ID, role: 'dialog', 'aria-modal': 'true' }, children: [ h2, the security pane, the settings surface, the state carrier, the close control ] }`. **THE DIALOG IS A SIBLING OF THE APP ROOT AND NEVER A CHILD OF IT, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN**: `inert` on a root that CONTAINED the dialog would block the dialog's own close control, and the tools the overlay is open FOR would be unreachable. **AND NO CAPABILITY UI IS AUTHORED HERE**: the Security pane and the Settings surface are the ISOLATED pane graph's, and `tests/isolation-adversarial-e2e.test.ts` refuses their ids and their words inside the app graph's rendered HTML because an app-graph node is `provident.dispatch`-reachable — so the dialog hosts the FRAME those surfaces belong to and authors no route of its own.

**THE MECHANISM WIRED, AND THE ATTRIBUTE NAME IS THE CALLER'S.** `startOverlayApplication` is the `startThemeApplication` form. `overlayWiringRole()` holds the CALLER-SUPPLIED name **once** (`'inert'`) beside the authored ids the envelope exports; `drive()` reads the verb token the authored body wrote into the authored carrier and hands it to `overlayTransition`; and `apply()` hands the resulting state to `overlayInertDeclaration(target, attributeName, state === 'open' || state === 'held')` and writes the answer as ONE `runtime.applyCommand({ kind: 'state-slice', node: APP_ROOT_ID, mutation: [{ targetProp: `props.${name}`, mode: 'replace', value: removal ? undefined : value }] })`. **`overlay.ts` OWNS NO ATTRIBUTE NAME AND NO VERB WORD** — measured, its comment-elided bytes carry neither — and **the wiring spells no verb either**: `attach()`'s three listeners read the token the authored body has just written, so the tree has ONE spelling of the name and NONE of the verbs outside the envelope. The removal arm is the mechanism's `removal` member reaching the node as `undefined`, which is the engine's declared attribute REMOVAL and never an empty string. The three listeners are the `startGutterAffordance` precedent — DOM listeners on graph-resolved elements, which create nothing.

**WHAT THE OVERLAY MEASURABLY ACHIEVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT — BOTH SAID, NEITHER IMPLIED BY THE OTHER.** *It does:* the inert attribute reaches the AUTHORED app root and comes back off it, and `provident.get_rendered_html` shows it — the `ui` leg reads `<div … id="app-surface" … >` closed, `<div … id="app-surface" … inert="">` open, and the closed form again. *It does:* in a browser, `inert` removes the subtree from the tab order and from pointer targeting — the HTML standard's semantics for the attribute the engine emits. *It does NOT:* block `provident.dispatch`. Measured — with the root inert, a dispatch on the `inc` control UNDER it still runs and still takes the counter to `1`, and the word `inert` appears NOWHERE in `src/renderer/runtime.ts` or `src/main/mcp-server.ts`, so no code on that path could consult it. *It does NOT:* stop the graph, the gesture session or the pane drag — the drag's commit route is ONE `state-slice` on an authored node and still answers `applied` under an inert root, and `gesture-session.ts`, `gutter-affordance.ts` and `relocate.ts` name `inert` nowhere. **NO FOCUS TRAP EXISTS AND NONE WAS ADDED**: the app has none, `inert` alone takes the subtree out of the tab order, and this pass adds no keyboard handler beyond the dialog's own authored `keydown` body. **AND THE SPELLING IS THE REALM'S**: the DOM shim writes `inert="true"`, the real `DomAdapter` writes the boolean `inert=""` — both measured, neither mistaken for the other.

**WHY THE OLD ARTEFACT COULD NOT BE REGENERATED, MEASURED AND NOT REMEMBERED.** `demo/pane-drag-demo/demo.mjs` was `13,217` lines / `511,559` bytes of self-contained esbuild output with **zero** `import`/`export`/`require` statements, carrying `src/renderer/store-core-graph.ts` and `store-graph-references.ts` INLINED — and it embedded a **frozen copy of `startGutterAffordance` still reading `seams.startSizeOf`/`seams.boundsOf`**, the element-attribute pair `D-117` replaced with the composition's shape reads. **Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Source:** the user's instruction, three defects measured on this window and a home named per fix.
