With the desktop's dark preference EMULATED (not inferred), computed styles read `html`, `body`, `header h1`, `#counter-card h2`, `#counter` and both `#group-toggles label`s at **`rgb(255, 255, 255)`** over `rgb(244, 246, 248)`/`rgb(255, 255, 255)`; the two buttons read only because the UA paints its own dark face (`rgb(255, 255, 255)` on `rgb(107, 107, 107)`) and the panes' hint and status set explicit colours, which is why the report named them as the two that read. **THE FIX IS BOTH ARMS, AND FOR TWO DIFFERENT FAILURES**: `:root` is PINNED to `color-scheme: light` — the design IS light, its backgrounds are literals, and the pin also keeps the UA's controls and scrollbar on that arm — and `body` gains an explicit `color: #1b2430` so every element that sets no colour of its own inherits a legible one even in a realm that ignores the pin. Measured after: `color-scheme` computes `light`, and those same six elements compute `rgb(27, 36, 48)` on the same backgrounds (`#inc` `rgb(0, 0, 0)` on `rgb(239, 239, 239)`). **THE COST, STATED**: a user who prefers dark gets light form controls and a light scrollbar. **2 · THE TOGGLE CHANGED DATA AND NOT APPEARANCE, AND THE HOME IS PRESENTATION KEYED ON THE AUTHORED ATTRIBUTE.** The mechanism run directly — `applyThemeDeclaration('theme', resolveTheme(s, undefined).setting)` — answers `{name: 'theme', value: 'dark', removal: false}`, `{name: 'theme', value: 'light', removal: false}` and, for the empty setting, `{name: 'theme', value: '', removal: true}`. **WHERE IT LANDS IS MEASURED AND IS NOT THE APP ROOT**: `get_rendered_html` carries `<div … id="theme-setting" … theme="light">` and then `theme="dark"` (and `ssrHtml` carries both), `get_node_state` reads `props.theme`, while `<div … id="app-surface" …>` carries NO `theme` attribute at any point — the consumer writes `props.<name>` on the AUTHORED STATE NODE (`themeWiringRole` derives it), exactly as `D-96`/`D-97` recorded. So the rules are keyed on **`[theme="dark"]`** and reach the surface above that node through `:has()`; the selector names the ATTRIBUTE and never the node id, because the attribute is the interface the graph publishes. Fourteen declarations in six rules, colours only: the page pair (`#12161c`/`#e8edf4`), the cards (`#1b222b`), the buttons, the input, the counter's value, and the panes' dim colours re-stated (`#9aa7b8`) so nothing drops to illegible. **THE TWO SCREENSHOTS ARE THE PROOF**: before the fix they were **BYTE-IDENTICAL** (`md5 0063049f0275f08410045376b8e745cd` for both), and after it they are three distinct images (`44d94635…` light, `1891dcfc…` dark) with `body` computing `rgb(18, 22, 28)`/`rgb(232, 237, 244)`, cards `rgb(27, 34, 43)`, buttons `rgb(43, 53, 66)`.

`divergence` **`9 checks, 0 failures`** plus `4` extension checks `0` — and its three `inert` extension rows (`P1`/`P2`/`P3`) read set-equal on BOTH realms, which is the leg the envelope change had to leave exactly as it stood; `panes` `7/7` over `22` MCP calls and `2` gestures; `crossings` `31/31` over `88` MCP calls (`84` the driver's, `4` envelope-settle polls), `22` acts and `21` observation dumps. `strata/marks.json` is REGENERATED by `strata-marks.mjs index` — the four rows join two files that were already INDEXED, so `gating` moves `263 → 267` sites in the SAME `36` files (`on notice` `2,476` and the `9` carve-outs unmoved), and `strata-marks.mjs check` is green — `strata-walkthrough.mjs refs` resolves every `D-n` over `120` rows, `strata/brief.md`'s §6 figure and its mark census are re-written IN PLACE and the file holds at `148` of `150`, and `strata/modules.json` is UNTOUCHED because the map already claims this pass's one new write path — `renderer-wiring` carried `src/renderer/index.html`, and the `chrome` row claiming it too was a DOUBLE CLAIM `strata-lint` refused (measured: `path "src/renderer/index.html" claimed by "renderer-wiring" and "chrome"`), so `mapRows` stays `21` and no `endpoints` figure moves. `strata-lint` reads `119` PASS / `1` FAIL / `4` INFO at exit `1` BEFORE and AFTER this pass — run on a detached worktree of `bb9efea` and on this tree — the FAIL being the standing over-long register rows (`D-68`, `D-70`, `D-71`, `D-73`, `D-74`, `D-75`, `D-76`) this instrument ACCEPTS and does not chase, and `D-120` is not among them at `11` lines.

## D-121 — THE USER TAKES **B**: THE WINDOW GOES FRAMELESS AND THE WINDOW CONTROLS ARE AUTHORED INTO THE TAB BAR — the option object measured on Linux, the control channel set and its bridge member, the sender guard a privileged channel owes, and the drag region measured IN THE AUTHORED DATA, with the readings it does not move stated beside the one it does

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-07 · **Source (user, verbatim):** "**B — go frameless and author the window controls into the tab bar.**" It is the FIRST of the four decisions a study left open and the only one this row takes (D-47: user-sourced, and the answer quoted rather than paraphrased).

**WHAT IT SETTLES, AND ONLY THIS.** The OS stops drawing this app's chrome: `src/main/main.ts`'s one `BrowserWindow` construction is created unframed, the window's top edge becomes the authored surface beginning at `y=0`, and minimizing, maximizing and closing become the app's own to draw and to wire. It settles the FRAMING and the controls' ORIGIN. It designs no tab bar, names no node, class, id or layer's write, and **no file under `src/` or `tests/` moves in this pass** — a ruling is recorded and the landing pass that acts on it is a separate unit (`D-6` and `D-119` are the register for who may change the shell: the merge permission that row reserved was exercised by the user's own words, the freeze is lifted, nothing is pushed, and neither clause is reworked here).

**THE OPTION OBJECT, MEASURED ON THIS PLATFORM** (Electron `44.4.5`, this host, a `980x720` construction — the app's own numbers — under `--ozone-platform=x11` as every leg spawns it; `getBounds()` and `getContentBounds()` read from the main process, `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` from the page): default frame — bounds `980x720`, content **`980x692` at `y+28`**, a 28-pixel GTK title bar; `frame: false` — content **`980x720` at `y+0`**; `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` — content `980x720` at `y+0`, IDENTICAL to `frame: false`; `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` with `titleBarOverlay: true` — the same content geometry, with the OS painting its own controls over the page. **THE ONE MEMBER B ADDS IS `frame: false`, AND NOTHING ELSE**, and each other member of the family is refused by name: the shipped declaration states it plainly — *"Specify `false` to create a frameless window. Default is `true`."* (`node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts`) — while **`titleBarOverlay`** has the OS draw the very controls B hands to the app and carries `color`/`symbolColor` annotated `@platform win32,linux`; **`trafficLightPosition`** is annotated `@platform darwin` ("Set a custom position for the traffic light buttons in frameless windows"), as are `setWindowButtonVisibility` and `setWindowButtonPosition`, so all three are no-ops on this platform and `main.ts` sets none; **`roundedCorners`** defaults `true` and the same declaration bounds it — *"On Linux, rounded corners are only drawn when the desktop environment supports client-side decorations"* — so it is left at its default rather than asserted; and **`titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`**, which measures the same here, is refused because its own documentation defines the Linux case only *"when combined with `titleBarOverlay: true`"* and says that *"otherwise no window controls will be shown"* — a value whose meaning is a version's, where `frame: false` is the documented frameless switch itself. **THE PREMISE IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN ADOPTED**: the shipped `44.4.5` declaration tags `titleBarStyle` with NO `@platform` at all, so "macOS/Windows-specific" is not what this install says, and Electron's current documentation's `hidden` row names **Windows and Linux** for its overlay branch; what is true on this host is what the four arms measured, and it is what this row commits to. **ONE PLATFORM CAVEAT IS NAMED, NOT SOLVED**: that documentation adds *"On Wayland (Linux), frameless windows have GTK drop shadows and extended resize boundaries by default"*, with `hasShadow: false` as the further member for a fully undecorated window — this host's session is Wayland while the legs spawn X11, so that arm is a measurement the landing pass owes and this row does not claim.

**THE CONTROL CHANNEL SET, AND THE INVENTORY IT JOINS.** At this head the app registers **18 `ipcMain.handle` sites and 3 `ipcMain.on` sites, every one of them in `src/main/main.ts`** — no other file under `src/` registers an IPC handler — over **26 channel-name constants** (`15` in `src/shared/types.ts`, `4` in `src/shared/tabs-channels.ts`, `6` in `src/shared/view-channels.ts`, `1` in `src/main/store-channels.ts`), and `src/main/preload.ts` exposes **9 top-level members carrying 22 routes**. **B ADDS A TENTH MEMBER, `window`, WITH FIVE ROUTES OVER FIVE CHANNELS** in a new `src/shared/window-channels.ts` (`tabs-channels.ts`'s and `view-channels.ts`'s own precedent): `minimize()`, `toggleMaximize()`, `close()` and `onChanged(handler)` over `provident:window:{minimize,toggle-maximize,close,changed}`, and `state()` over `provident:window:state` — four `ipcMain.handle` sites and no `ipcMain.on`. **WHY THESE AND NOT A PAIR PER VERB**: the button is ONE control, so ONE toggle channel with `win.isMaximized()` deciding the direction on the main side and the answer stating the state it left — a `maximize`/`unmaximize` pair would let the renderer compose the very bit it is asking about (`D-112`'s one-site-per-channel rule read on three verbs); the state READ serves the boot's first paint and every change the WM makes without the app, and the change push then carries NOTHING — no verb, no state — exactly as the tab record's, the view record's, the app-state rows' and the security record's four carry nothing (`D-63`, `D-87`, `D-104`, `D-106`). **THE LOCKSTEP THE NEW MEMBER JOINS IS FIVE SITES**: `src/main/preload.ts`'s `ProvidentBridge` and `src/renderer/secure-panels.ts`'s `declare global` (a half-declaration fails), plus the three censuses that assert the member set by EQUALITY — the two `BRIDGE_MEMBERS` constant arrays in the two `security-store-storeroom/isolation` files and the same set spelled inline in `settings-carrier-retirement`'s `ISO-4` — so a tenth member added to the bridge alone reds all three.

**THE PERMISSION MODEL A PRIVILEGED CHANNEL OWES, AND WHERE ITS GUARD MAY LIVE.** No handler in this file checks its sender today: `permitted(` and `senderFrame` occur nowhere under `src/`, 14 of the 18 `handle` sites discard `_event` and the other four take no event at all, and `BR-10` asserts both absences over comment-elided code as a MEASUREMENT of the siblings rather than as an opinion about a new site. **A window-control channel is a different privilege class**: every sibling reaches a store row, while `close()` ends the process and the two others reach the OS window the user is looking at — and the same tree makes every authored control `dispatch`-reachable, so which party may press that button is the chrome-versus-data question below. B therefore commits this group to the ONE guard the rest of the file does not have: a request is refused unless the invoking event's sender is THIS window's own `webContents` and the frame it arrived on is that webContents' main frame, and the refusal is a VALUE in the crossings' own vocabulary, never a throw (`D-101`'s refusal shape read on a channel that owns no store). **AND ITS HOME IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN**: `BR-10` reads `src/main/main.ts` with comments elided and reddens on `permitted(`, on `senderFrame` and on a bare `event` token, so the guard belongs in the main-side module that owns the four verbs with `main.ts`'s handler forwarding `_event` in one expression — or that gating row's own sentence is re-grained in the landing pass, and either way it is re-read there rather than assumed.

**THE DRAG REGION, DRIVEN IN THE RUNNING RENDERER.** Three declarations were authored into an envelope and read back through `provident.load` → `provident.dispatch` → `provident.get_rendered_html` on the built bundle under a fresh scratch profile, the observation taken in the renderer realm (an `HTMLDivElement` element and a `CSSStyleDeclaration`, so a real DOM and not the shim): **(a)** `css: {'-webkit-app-region': 'drag'}` — a css MEMBER — renders as the unknown ATTRIBUTE `-webkit-app-region="drag"` with NO `style` attribute and a computed `webkitAppRegion` of `none`, because the engine routes every `css.<key>` through `setAttribute` and only `id`, `classes`, `style` and `cssDef` are special (`node_modules/provident-ssr/dist/core/adapters.js`); **(b)** `css: {style: {'-webkit-app-region': 'drag'}}` — the authored style OBJECT — renders `style="app-region: drag;"`, reads `drag` back from `getPropertyValue('-webkit-app-region')` and COMPUTES `drag`, because `serializeStyle` emits `key: value;` for every pair and Chromium's parser then canonicalises the vendor name to `app-region`; **(c)** the controls — `{color: 'rgb(1, 2, 3)'}` renders verbatim, and `{'-webkit-app-region': 'no-drag'}` and `{'app-region': 'no-drag'}` both render `app-region: no-drag;` and compute `no-drag`. **SO THE RUNTIME FILTERS NOTHING AND THE DRAG REGION IS AUTHORABLE DATA** — through the style OBJECT and never through a bare css key — the bar's `drag` and its interactive children's `no-drag` being declarable in the envelope. **WHAT THAT DECIDES**: "the runtime cannot carry it" is struck as an argument for the shell's page CSS. **WHAT IT DOES NOT**: who authors the bar — and a row that later asserts the RENDERED tag must assert `app-region: drag`, the spelling the attribute actually carries, while the authored object may carry either name.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE.** The study's **decisions 2, 3 and 4**, each recorded here as OPEN and untouched by this row, which takes B alone and re-words none of them; and **the chrome-versus-data question** — whether the tab bar and its three controls are authored provident nodes, visible to `provident.dispatch`, `get_rendered_html` and `get_markdown` and therefore pressable by an agent, or the shell's own chrome, the one kind of element the UI-authority rule leaves outside the graph (`AGENTS.md` § "UI authority"). **THE TWO ARE ONE QUESTION FROM OPPOSITE ENDS** and neither is answered here: what this row fixes is that the bar EXISTS and is the window's top edge.

**WHAT IT COSTS, EACH AS MEASURED OR AS READ OFF THE TREE.** *(a) The page begins at `y=0`*: the content area gains the 28 pixels the title bar occupied (`980x692` → `980x720` on this host), so every y-origin moves and no box size does. *(b) The printed readings, checked rather than assumed*: the `ui` leg's `425x22` at `fontSize=16px` and the `panes` leg's `P-3` box are both BOX readings — a line box and a row box — and the same arms measure the probe's `948x22` at `(16,16)` identically framed and unframed, so both stand, as does the `ui` leg's overlay row, whose fragment sizes are the envelope's and not the viewport's; `D-120`'s measured `965x692` scrim over a `980x692` window becomes `965x720` over `980x720`, and its two screenshots are re-taken rather than byte-compared. *(c) A frameless window with no drag region yet cannot be MOVED*: the region and the framing must land in the same pass, or `frame: false` ships a window a user can never move. *(d) The map and the figures beside it*: a new `src/shared/window-channels.ts` joins the `app-shell` row's `paths` and moves that row's `endpoints` `7` → `8`, so the harness cap `strata-lint` prints for it reads `120` → `130`, while `mapRows` stays `21`; `pins`' `srcTypeScriptFiles` moves `50` → `51`, and `strata/brief.md` §2 carries that figure as prose.

## D-122 — THE USER SETTLES ALL FOUR: the tab bar is AUTHORED PROVIDENT DATA, the `menu-template` pane's open state BLOCKS THE PORTS with the agent locked out, the ZONE-AS-CONTAINER-FOR-REPOSITIONING use case is ARCHIVED and regenerable, and this template carries the RECORD AND THE REFERENCE while the app data display and its renderer are the APP'S OWN

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-05 (the host's own reading — `git log` dates the commit that carries `D-121` `2026-11-05 03:15 -0600` while that row's `Date:` cell reads `2026-11-07`; the cell stands as filed, `D-46`) · **Source (user, verbatim, four rulings in one answer):** **(1)** "provident" — the tab bar is **authored provident data**. **(2)** "menu-template (note: prevent the dispatch read by blocking the ports while the pane is open, the agent should be locked out while agent settings are configurable)". **(3)** "This is a covered use case already, regenerate from archives if it has been dropped. **Zones are containers for repositioning panes.**" **(4)** "Record that will be referenced by the app data display, which will use app-specific renderer". **This pass RESEARCHES, DESIGNS AND RECORDS and builds none of the four** — no tab bar, no menu, no layout — so no file under `src/` or `tests/` moves and `git status --short` is empty at it: `D-121`'s own shape and its own limit.

**WHAT EACH RULING SETTLES, AND ONLY THIS.** **(1)** THE TAB BAR'S AUTHORITY IS SETTLED: it is envelope data driven through the producing graph, so its nodes answer `provident.dispatch`, `get_rendered_html` and `get_markdown`; the chrome-versus-data question `D-121` recorded OPEN is answered on the DATA side for the bar, while the three window controls stay the shell's own — the one element class `AGENTS.md` § "UI authority" leaves outside the graph — and `D-121`'s measured drag-region recipe (the authored STYLE OBJECT `css: {style: {'-webkit-app-region': 'drag'}}` renders `style="app-region: drag;"` and computes `drag`, while a bare `css.<key>` renders an unknown ATTRIBUTE and computes `none`) is the authored form the bar's own drag region takes. **(2)** THE `menu-template` PANE'S LOCKOUT IS RULED AND ITS DESIGN IS THIS ROW'S OWN (§ the lockout below); the pane is where AGENT SETTINGS are configurable, and while it is open the ports are blocked. **(3)** THE ZONE FAMILY'S SEMANTIC IS NAMED — a zone is a CONTAINER FOR REPOSITIONING PANES, not a width, a track or a resize handle — and the archived use case stands (`D-2`: it is read, never re-pointed) or is regenerated by its own layer (§ regeneration below). **(4)** A SCOPE BOUNDARY IS DRAWN: this template EXPOSES THE RECORD AND THE REFERENCE and the app data display is APP-SPECIFIC, rendered by THAT APP'S OWN renderer; **THE TEMPLATE MUST NOT GROW A RENDERER OF ITS OWN** — `docs/L1/central-data-management.md` §6 `ASM-12` already leaves the rendered data pane owed to a later unit that "must owe provident-authored UI", and this ruling puts that unit in the APP, not here.

**THE ZONE USE CASE IS IN THE ARCHIVE — MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE RETIRED CORPUS, AND IT IS A MECHANISM PLUS A POLICY SHELL PLUS A NAME SET, NEVER ONE PAGE.** `grep -rn "reposition"` answers **ZERO** across `archive/`, `docs/`, `src/` and `strata/`, and so do "between zones", "one zone to another" and "moves the pane" — the corpus never spells the PROPOSITION the ruling states — but the thing the proposition is about is stated, in five places, and these are their operative clauses. *(a) A ZONE **IS** A CONTAINER AND MOVING A PANE BETWEEN ZONES IS THE MECHANISM'S OWN WRITE — `specs/slothost.md` §1: "**a host that maps caller-declared opaque keys to containers holding caller-created nodes, orders and attributes them by caller-supplied policy, owns exactly the nodes it placed, and refuses an undeclared key with a typed refusal instead of creating anything**", and its complete write list (§1 item 4, amended 2026-09-27): "it obtains one container per declared key from the factory; it projects those containers onto the injected `container`; **it places a caller-created node into that key's container; it MOVES A NODE BETWEEN TWO DECLARED CONTAINERS**; it removes a node it placed". The zones are the keys, the panes are the caller-created nodes, and the move is `setNode(newKey, node)` — reference-identical (`§3.1 M-5`/`M-7`, `I-3`), `order`/`setOrder` ordering the CONTAINERS by the caller's `orderOf` policy with **no ordering policy invented** (`M-4`, prohibition 3), and no ordering WITHIN a container existing anywhere in the corpus; `specs/slot-host-envelope-authored-container-source-review.md` §3.3 names the consumer outright — "**the fork's per-zone boxes must be supplied as nodes**, or this is not the right mechanism for that surface (V-5)" — and `FORKER.md` §4 carries the fork-facing form, "for the zone/sidebar case, the `owned-list-host` divergence: one `mount`, no per-key container — supply those boxes as **nodes**". *(b) THE DROP DECISION IS A POLICY SHELL OVER THAT MECHANISM — `specs/relocate.md`/`guide/relocate.md` (`U-RELOCATE`, composed on the frozen gesture session): the caller supplies `candidatesFor` (the candidate set), `resolveTarget`, `onReveal`, `commit` and `threshold`, and "**Two moves across two different zones read as a retarget — one presentation write carrying both the old and the new candidate, and still exactly one reveal at the terminal**". *(c) THE STORED NAMES ARE ENUMERATED AND `slot`/`distance` ARE THE LOCATION'S TWO HALVES — `specs/pane-drag-compliance.md` §2.4 names 3/4: `mem.layout.zone.<id>.slot` "OPAQUE — returned as-is, never interpreted by the store, never interpreted by the family's bytes" and `mem.layout.zone.<id>.distance` "a CALLER-MEASURED scalar — the caller measures it; the store merely stores what the caller wrote; **the family computes no distance**", both "each observed move", while name **7** `mem.layout.pane.<id>.location` is "the pane location member (queued contract clause 1: *"pane locations are STORED values"*) — read by the placement/resolve logic"; and `specs/data-ownership-model-plan.md`'s `ZQ-4` rules the referent: "**A "LOCATION" IS TWO CALLER VALUES — AN OPAQUE SLOT KEY AND A CALLER-MEASURED DISTANCE — NEVER A COORDINATE**". *(d) A MINIMIZED ZONE IS STILL A DROP TARGET — `decisions/ACTIVE-projection-and-store-facility.md`'s `ZONE-SIZE-DOMAIN-IS-CONSUMER-CARRIED-AND-THE-MINIMUM-CLAMP-IS-FAMILY-SIDE`, clause (3) quoting the architect *"The minimized zone should still broadcast a location for the proximity detection to expand back to its configured size and host the pane"*: "A MINIMIZED ZONE KEEPS ITS LOCATION. Minimizing changes the **extent**, never the **position** … **So a minimized member is a drop target that is reachable by proximity, not a member that has been removed**". *(e) THE PANES BELONG TO THE ZONE THEY STAND IN, AND THE GESTURE'S ENTRY AND TERMINAL STATES ARE THE SESSION'S — `guide/zones.md`: "a minimized zone **WITH panes retains a TAB-STRIP list** of its panes (no frames — the tabs are drag sources too); a pane drag **READS THE STORE's EXPANDED size** (`mem.layout.zone.<id>.size`; `canPlace = size >= min`) to decide placement … and **TEMPORARILY EXPANDS** a minimized target to host the ghost, restored on release/abandon"; `specs/live-demo-retrospective.md` D-15: "After committing a pane into the minimized zone, its frame lives in a `display:none` stack … The pane is represented by its TAB", with `T-12`'s row "a `.zone-tab` is a drag source carrying the pane id" driving "**I can move a pane out of its minimized zone by its tab**"; and `pending.md` §Q records "the pane-drag → zone compliance item **ADMITTED AND LANDED**". **AND THE CORPUS OWNS NO ZONE VOCABULARY IN ANY MECHANISM** — `H-r17`: "a dashboard/toolbar use case changes NO zone/track contract … **with no zone vocabulary anywhere**" — which is why `specs/zones.md` and `specs/census.md`, the two pages whose subject is the word "zone", say nothing about repositioning at all.

**WHETHER IT WAS DROPPED: THE READ SIDE SURVIVES, THE TWO HALVES THE RULING NAMES DO NOT.** Alive: `['zones']` at `mem` is a declared family under `zones-must-stand` beside the tab record's six and the module's two in the boot's ONE `createProfileStore` batch (nine declarations, one construction), with a route (`commitZones`), a client read (`zoneOf`) and a composition that READS it — `src/renderer/renderer.ts`'s `candidatesFor` answers "the candidate carries the zone's OPAQUE `slot` and its caller-measured `distance`" off `view.zoneOf(id)`, and its `renderZone` reads `zoneOf('zone-1')` for the layout call. **Dropped, each measured: (i) THE WRITE SIDE HAS NO CALLER** — `grep -rn "commitZones" src/` answers `15` hits and every one is a declaration, an implementation or the `IPC_VIEW_ZONES_COMMIT` handler, never a UI act, so nothing in the running app ever moves a pane and the container relation has no writer; **(i-bis) THE DROP HALF OF THE COMPOSITION IS UNREACHED** — `createPaneDrag` IS live (`const drag = createPaneDrag({ view: getViewClient() }, source)`) and the live gesture takes exactly three members off it, `drag.startSizeOf`, `drag.boundsOf` and `drag.release` (the RESIZE half), while `candidatesFor`, `renderZone`, `move`, `rightClick`, `cancel` and `previewOf` are returned at the surface's own object literal and **called by nothing in the tree** — the zone reads are wired and never invoked; **(ii) `mem.layout.pane.<id>.location` HAS NO SUCCESSOR** — `['panes']` carries `{ size, bounds }` and no location member (`docs/L2/view-record/interface.md` §2's address table), so the REPOSITION half went out with the frozen store; **(iii) THERE IS ONE ZONE ID AND NO MEMBERSHIP** — `renderZone` and `candidatesFor` both fall back to the literal `'zone-1'` and no authored node declares a zone (`src/shared/demo-envelope.ts` authors the pane `gutter-pane` and the word `zone` occurs `0` times in it), so no zone→panes relation exists anywhere in the tree; **(iv) THE DEMO IS A RESIZE DEMO** — `D-117` wired the live gesture onto `['panes']` and `D-118`'s rebuild drives one pane with `zoneOf` answering `null`. **`src/shared/zones.ts` IS NOT THE USE CASE AND NEVER WAS**: it is `U-ZONES`, "a **pure, total two-function mechanism**" (`isEmpty`, `trackFor`, `TrackSpec`), which "carries **no zone/pane/tab vocabulary**" and "ships **no CSS**" — the token-arithmetic half, consumed in-repo only by `census.ts`, itself imported by nothing — and `candidatesFor`'s `[{candidate: slot, distance}]` is `U-RELOCATE`'s `CandidateFor` ("the opaque candidate + its caller-supplied `distance`"), produced by the composition's closure, the pure `withinProximity` having no call site here (`D-111`). **THE LINEAGE, IN ONE LINE EACH WAY:** `SCH-4`/`SCH-7`/`SCH-9`/`SCH-10` → `U-ZONES`/`U-CENSUS`/`U-RELOCATE`/`U-SLOTHOST`/`U-PANE-DRAG-COMPLIANCE` → §Q's queued nine stored names → `D-87`/`D-91`'s `['zones']` → `D-92`'s wired reader → `D-93`'s deletion of the frozen store. **So the CONTAINER relation and the REPOSITION verb were never a landed contract in THIS tree: they were `slot-host`'s mechanism (a fork's per-zone boxes) and the demo's and the fork's own behaviour.**

**WHAT "REGENERATE" MEANS UNDER `D-2`, AND WHAT IT CANNOT MEAN.** `D-2`'s rule is that the archive **"is gitignored and is the retrieval mechanism"** and is cited by one prefix mapping — "`docs/<x>` resolves at `archive/gate-corpus-2026-10-29/<x>`" — and `D-52` refused to archive a unit's record because "archiving a unit's record would put it where `archive.md` §2 says nothing may be treated as authority". **So regeneration is a COPY FORWARD, never a re-adoption**: the archived pages stay exactly where they are and are READ and CITED BY THEIR ARCHIVE PATH; no live file may carry their bytes, and no live cite is re-pointed INTO them as authority. What `D-2`'s three bullets permit is the third alone — "`docs/` stays live and is where the layers write: `docs/L1/`, `docs/L2/<module>/`, `docs/L3/<module>/`" — plus the first, "a superseded document is **replaced**, never annotated". **The re-issued document is therefore a NEW `docs/L1/panes-layout.md`, written by the `panes-layout` row's L1 layer, under the class maximum every L1 scope in this tree declares (`docs/L1/central-data-management.md`'s header: "**Ceiling:** 150 lines (class max)"), stating the use case as THIS tree's own — a zone is a container holding panes, a reposition is one `setNode`-shaped move between two declared containers composed at the crossing, `slot` is the zone's opaque key and `distance` the caller's own measure, and the entry state is the session's `pointerdown` with the terminal a release, reset or right-click — with `docs/L2/panes-layout/interface.md` and `docs/L3/panes-layout/design.md` following at their own declared ceilings (`120` and `130` at the sibling `store-view-record` scope). `panes-layout` is the right row: `strata/modules.json` claims the four mechanisms there (`zones.ts`, `census.ts`, `layout-projection.ts`, `container.ts`, `endpoints: 10`, harness cap `150`), and `strata/modules.md` §3's "L1 files the map as its first act of a unit, and no design is admitted before it (D-7)" is what makes the L1 scope the first re-issued document. **AND NO LAYER HERE MAY WRITE IT**: `D-78`'s and `D-90`'s rule that no layer judges its own design makes the regeneration `panes-layout`'s own spec gate, and this row records the path, the layer and the ceiling rather than the act.

**THE LOCKOUT — WHAT EXISTS, MEASURED FIRST (this pass's own drives, throwaway probes bundled from `src/main/` and deleted, zero surviving processes).** *(i) HOW THE SERVER STARTS AND STOPS.* The transport is chosen once at the composition site — `--mcp-transport=` / `PROVIDENT_MCP_TRANSPORT`, `--mcp-port=` / `PROVIDENT_MCP_PORT`, `default port 3787` (`src/main/main.ts:66-87`) — and `start()` creates the listener: `this.httpServer = createServer((req, res) => { void this.handleHttp(req, res) })` then `await new Promise<void>((resolve) => this.httpServer!.listen(this.port, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve()))`; `close()` already exists and DOES stop it — `await Promise.allSettled([...this.httpServers].map((s) => s.close())); this.httpServers.clear(); … if (this.httpServer) { await new Promise<void>((resolve) => this.httpServer!.close(() => resolve())); this.httpServer = null }`. **DRIVEN: after `close()` a POST to `127.0.0.1:4791/mcp` answers `ECONNREFUSED`, and `start()` called again re-listens on the SAME port and serves — the pair is RE-ENTRANT, and a second `close()` closes again.** On `stdio` there is nothing to stop that way: `start()` builds one long-lived server and `await server.connect(new StdioServerTransport())`, and `close()` closes THAT server — which is the client's own pipe, not a port. *(ii) WHAT THE EXCLUSION ACTUALLY BLOCKS, DRIVEN BOTH WAYS.* The state is not an MCP tool pair: it is the secure crossing's `mem` record, written from the renderer's Settings surface over `IPC_SECURITY_EXCLUSION` ("`provident:security:exclusion`") into `settingsSurface.transition(state)`, delivered by the instance's one subscription and re-patched onto the gate by `applyExclusion`, whose enforcement is `exclusionTurn` at the ONE REGISTRATION BOUNDARY (`const guarded = <H …>(handler: H): H => (async (...a: never[]) => exclusionTurn(liveGate) ?? (await (handler …)(...a)))`) so every `registerTool` and every resource read is wrapped. **DRIVEN on the HTTP transport: with the gate at `'mcp-disabled'` ALL EIGHT probes — `initialize`, `tools/list`, `ping`, `tools/call provident.dispatch`, `tools/call provident.load`, `tools/call provident.data.read`, `resources/list`, `resources/read mcp://provident/app` — answer `http=503` with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32003,"message":"exclusion-closed"},"id":null}`, and the backend's invocation counter reads `0` across the whole pass (it read `3` when enabled). DRIVEN on the STDIO transport: `ping`, `tools/list` and `resources/list` still ANSWER IN FULL — the tool and resource census is still legible — while every `tools/call` and the `resources/read` answer the refusal as an ordinary result, `{"status":"refused","reason":"exclusion-closed","message":"…"}`, and the backend's invocation counter holds at `4` before and after: **no call is refused at the transport and no invocation reaches the renderer.** So the exclusion covers EVERY METHOD's invocation, and on HTTP every METHOD at all; on stdio the protocol's own methods are untouched. *(iii) THE OVERLAY'S OPEN STATE REACHES NOTHING ON THIS PATH.* `D-113` measured it: "**with the root inert, a dispatch on the `inc` control UNDER it still runs and still takes the counter to `1`, and the word `inert` appears NOWHERE in `src/renderer/runtime.ts` or `src/main/mcp-server.ts`, so no code on that path could consult it**" — so `START_OVERLAY_APPLICATION`'s `inert` product is a BROWSER block and the ports (or the exclusion) are the only real wall.

**THE THREE CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, WITH THEIR COSTS, AND THE ONE THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS.** **(a) CLOSE THE HTTP LISTENER while the pane is open and re-open on close.** Blocks everything at the connection — measured `ECONNREFUSED` — and leaks nothing over the port; an IN-FLIGHT POST is not abandoned, `httpServer.close()` stops accepting and waits for the open connections to drain, so a straddling request completes under whatever state it entered; the STDIO ARM HAS NO PORT AT ALL and forcing this there is measured FATAL — after `server.close()` on stdio the client's next `ping` never returns and never throws (it hung for the whole 25 s window) while `main.ts`'s own stdin handler is `void mcp.close().finally(() => app.exit(0))`, i.e. it exits the app; and the CLIENT SEES a dead socket, which cannot be told from a quit app — the prebuild baseline's own debugging-exposure goal pays for that. **(b) REFUSE AT THE TRANSPORT** with a gate answering every request with a refusal: this is ALREADY the landed shape on HTTP (`503 -32003` before the body is read, measured) and needs no new mechanism; it leaks the STATE, which `specs/secure-exclusion.md` `§0A` item 7(b) DECLARES rather than hides ("an AUTHORIZED caller NOW learns the state FROM THE MESSAGE … and an UNAUTHORIZED caller still cannot"); an in-flight request is refused by `exclusionTurn`; stdio works with no transport change; the client sees a machine-readable refusal, never a throw. **(c) SET THE EXCLUSION AND WIDEN IT TO COVER EVERY METHOD.** Blocks every invocation on both transports (measured, `0` renderer invocations) and on HTTP every method at arrival; it can leak the tool/resource NAMES on stdio (measured); in-flight work is invalidated whole by `backend.abandonPendingForExclusion(EXCLUSION_CLOSED)`, which "rejects EVERY pending entry and returns the count (so a call dispatched under the old state can never deliver a renderer value after the transition)"; stdio is untouched and re-armable; the client sees the declared refusal with its cause and remedy. **WHAT IS REFUSED, BY NAME**: **(b) as a NEW mechanism** — it would duplicate `exclusionTurn`, which `specs/secure-exclusion.md` `§2.3` item 2 already pins at the landed 401-then-503 order; **(a) ON STDIO** — measured fatal (the request hangs, or the app exits), and the corpus already refuses it for the exclusion: "the exclusion does NOT close the stdio transport: closing it would destroy the operator's ability to re-enable (the session is spawn-local) and would make the disabled state observable as a disconnect"; **(a) ALONE** — a socket state machine is not an invariant: it fails open the moment the closing edge is skipped, and it says nothing about a method that never needed the port.

**THE DESIGN CHOSEN, IN PROSE AND NOT IN CODE.** **THE TRIGGER IS ONE AUTHORED STATE AND THERE IS NO SECOND PATH.** `src/shared/overlay.ts`'s machine already answers `closed`/`open`/`held`/`closing`, and `startOverlayApplication`'s `apply()` already computes the one predicate the inert declaration rides — `state === 'open' || state === 'held'` — so the lockout's edge is that same predicate, evaluated at that same site, and it drives the EXISTING `security.exclusion` verb over the EXISTING `IPC_SECURITY_EXCLUSION` channel: one transition site, one channel, no new vocabulary, no second writer (`D-112`'s one-site-per-channel rule). **THE EXCLUSION IS SET FIRST AND THE PORT DROPS SECOND, IN THAT ORDER AND IN THE SAME TURN**, because the exclusion is the invariant that survives a failed close and the port is the belt: the handler's answer already carries `{applied, state}`, so the port arm is a CONSEQUENCE of the state the transition answered, run after it, and its own failure is recorded as a VALUE on that answer and never thrown into the IPC reply. **THE BLOCK IS BOTH, AND NEITHER IS A WIDENING**: every method already refuses under the exclusion (measured), so nothing is added there; the port close adds only the connection-level refusal on `http` — and it is skipped entirely on `stdio`, where the exclusion alone is the whole block and the transport is never closed. **IN-FLIGHT**: the transition's epoch bump runs `abandonPendingForExclusion`, which rejects every pending renderer entry with the one channel token; a POST already accepted by the listener is not killed mid-body (`httpServer.close()` drains it), and its own turn then refuses at the registration boundary if it has not yet dispatched — measured, nothing reaches the renderer either way. **THE STDIO ARM** is therefore the exclusion alone: the transport stays CONNECTED and re-armable, the refusal is a result value, and the census (`tools/list`) stays legible — a stated cost, not an oversight. **THE RE-OPEN PATH** is the mirror edge: the overlay leaving `open`/`held` sets `'mcp-enabled'` through the same channel and re-listens on the SAME port with the SAME `start()`, which is measured re-entrant; the re-open is attempted on EVERY closing edge, not only the first, so a dropped edge heals at the next one, and a boot always calls `start()` so a restart heals it absolutely. **AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NAMED, BOTH WAYS, WITH NO CLAIM BEYOND THE MEASUREMENT.** *The app crashes with the pane open and the port closed*: the kernel releases the socket, so no stale block survives, and the next boot's `start()` binds normally — but the EXCLUSION is not persisted either (`D-19`: "the flag is NOT persisted"), so that boot comes up `mcp-enabled` and re-admits the agent; **the port block inherits exactly that property and no stronger one**, which is the safe-by-availability direction and the unsafe-by-confidentiality one, and it is stated rather than mitigated here. *The re-open throws* (a foreign process took 3787, or a TIME_WAIT collision): the exclusion is still `'mcp-disabled'`, so the agent is still locked out — the failure is in the wrong direction for usability and the right one for the ruling — and it must be answered as a recorded value and retried on the next edge and at the next boot, never swallowed. **NO BINDER AND NO IPC ROUTE IS BUILT BY THIS ROW** (the act is a landing pass's), and no `src/` or `tests/` byte moves for it.

**⟶ ITS LOCKOUT DESIGN IS SUPERSEDED BY POINTER AND NOT ONE WORD OF THIS ROW IS REWORDED (`D-46`).** The user's instruction of 2026-11-05 replaced the sequence with an INVARIANT at `D-123`: the pane's open state is the secure crossing's fourth `mem` address, one declaration at the store's root refuses `paneOpen && portsOpen` whatever route reaches it, its repair settles the ports, and the socket follows the exclusion's delivery (`http` only, `stdio` never). The imperative edges this row designed — the predicate driving the transition, the exclusion-first ordering, and the mirror re-open — are READ THROUGH that row; the one piece of the design that row does NOT build is the auto re-enable, because an invariant is not a toggle.

## D-123 — THE INVARIANT REPLACES `D-122`'S SEQUENCE: the security pane and the MCP ports cannot both be open, and the STORE refuses to hold the pair — one declaration at the store's root judges two addresses, its repair settles the PORTS, and the socket follows the exclusion's delivery on `http` and is never touched on `stdio`

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Use the constraint engine in the storeroom / Enforce that the security pane cannot be open while the MCP ports are open"*; plus the measurements below, all driven 2026-11-05 on this head over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.3`.

**THE GROUND, MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS WRITTEN.** *(i) The secure crossing's families and their repairs.* `declarationsFor` rides ONE `storeCreate` with three pairs — `['operator-settings']` `file` (`operator-record-must-stand`, repair `mintRecord` = the import performed and `toStored(imported ?? FIRST_RUN)` written whole), `['operator-app-state']` `file` (`operator-app-state-must-stand`, repair `mintAppState` = the import and `{rows, legacy, unrepresentable}`), `['operator-exclusion']` `mem` (`operator-exclusion-must-stand`, repair `mintExclusion` = `SAFE_PAIR.exclusion` whole, because a `mem` address can never come from a file) — and the first caller-visible receipt was `cursor: 4`, one op per repair. *(ii) The exclusion's shape and delivery.* `{exclusion:'mcp-enabled'|'mcp-disabled'}` stored, `tier4` derived at the read; written by `write`'s exclusion arm over `IPC_SECURITY_EXCLUSION` → `settingsSurface.transition` → one `mem` write; delivered by the instance's one subscription to `settings-surface`'s `onDelivery`, whose exclusion branch patches the gate (`applyExclusion`, epoch bump + `abandonPendingForExclusion`) and, since `D-117`, writes no holder at all. *(iii) The overlay's state.* `startOverlayApplication` holds `closed`/`open`/`held`/`closing` in closure, seeded from the AUTHORED carrier (`OVERLAY_STATE_ID`), driven by the authored verb token (`overlayVerbToken`), and its `apply()` computes `const up = state === 'open' || state === 'held'` — the predicate the `inert` declaration rides. *(iv) The MCP lifecycle.* `start()` creates the listener and `close()` stops it, measured RE-ENTRANT at `D-122` (`ECONNREFUSED` after close, `start()` re-listens on the SAME port); on `stdio` `close()` closes the CLIENT'S PIPE and the next `ping` never returns — measured fatal there. *(v) A new family's write.* The renderer's `apply()` turn is the user's act (clause 4), and nothing in the tree could write a pane's state: no channel, no verb, no address.

**THE DESIGN, AND WHY IT BEATS `D-122`'S SEQUENCE.** `D-122` made the lockout a PROCEDURE — a renderer predicate set `security.exclusion`, the port dropped as a consequence of that call — and said at its own bytes that "(a) ALONE — a socket state machine is not an invariant: it fails open the moment the closing edge is skipped". **THE INVARIANT IS NOW THE STORE'S**: the pane's open state is the crossing's FOURTH address, `['operator-pane']` on `mem`, shape `{open: boolean}` — **`mem` because a pane is not a durable fact** (the four-state machine is the renderer's and is re-seeded from the authored carrier at every boot; a persisted `open` would be a second authority over a surface that no longer exists) — and ONE declaration, `no-open-pane-over-open-ports`, refuses a store holding `paneOpen && portsOpen` whatever route reached it. **IT STANDS AT THE STORE'S ROOT `[]`, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES THE PASS**: a pair is asked only where an act touches its address (`guide §7.6`; `D-56`/`D-66`), so a pair at either half's address is asked for that half's landing op and NOT for the other's (measured, both ways) — at `[]` every act of this instance is at or below the pair, so ONE body catches BOTH edges. **ITS REPAIR SETTLES THE PORTS AND NEVER THE PANE** — closing the ports is the safe direction, the pane is what the operator is doing, and it is expressible: the crossing's answer is `{applied, state}` and the realm paints it — through ONE function, `writeExclusion`, which routes the registration instant through the handed `write` and the landing instant through `store.write(address,'mem',value,context)` — **supplying `write`'s FOURTH position, which this module supplied nowhere until this pass** (`guide §7.6`'s worked example; `D-103`: a repair that omits the commit is unsupported). **AND THE SOCKET IS NOT A CONSTRAINT'S ACT**: a repair writes a value and returns the op it landed, so the port is a LISTENER'S consequence (`D-82` clause 2) — the exclusion's delivery reaches a third callback, `onExclusionChanged`, and `ProvidentMcpServer.followExclusion` reconciles an `http` listener (`close()`/`start()`, idempotent, serialised) and returns immediately on `stdio`, where the transport is the client's pipe. **WHY IT CANNOT BE ONE REPAIR THAT REACHES A SOCKET, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A DEFECT**: the record is under the constraint engine's restart budget and applied-repair marker and the socket under none (`D-70`); so the design is a CONSTRAINT for the record and a LISTENER for the socket, each measured where it lives.

**THE BUILD, AND WHAT MOVED.** `writePane(open)` is the fourth address's one verb (one `mem` write of `{open}`, the sibling receipt; a non-boolean refused as a value before any store verb); the surface gains `pane(open)` and the callback; `IPC_SECURITY_PANE` is the channel (`store-channels.ts`'s census `1 → 2`); the preload and `secure-panels.ts` gain `setPane` in lockstep (the `security` member set `4 → 5`); the renderer's `overlayApplication.apply()` reports `up` on a MOVE over that member; and `main.ts` supplies `onExclusionChanged: (state) => { mcp.followExclusion(state) }` beside the pane's handler. **THE PANE'S BODY READS ITS OWN ADDRESS AT A LANDING INSTANT**, and that is measured rather than chosen: a re-run hands every pair the value the repair's op LANDED, so a body trusting `context.value` refused its own repair and the write crossed `ConstraintPassRefused` as *"violated a re-run"*.

**THE ROWS, AND WHAT EACH REVERT PRODUCES — MEASURED, EACH ON THE REAL SUITES.** `CD-13` EDGE ONE (the pane opens and the pair closes in the SAME write), `CD-14` EDGE TWO (an enable under an open pane still reads `mcp-disabled`), `CD-15` WHICH HALF (the pane's act stands, the enable is the discriminator that proves the pane was never settled, and an ordinary exclusion change with the pane closed repairs nothing — the control), `CD-16` ONE BODY AT BOTH LANDING ADDRESSES, `CD-17` the pane family's two arms; `PF-1` the HTTP listener's two directions, `PF-2` the stdio arm untouched, `PF-3` the follow's idempotence and serial order, `PF-4` the delivery that drives it. **Reversion 1 — the invariant's declaration removed from the batch: `8` rows red** (`CD-1`, `CD-3`, `CD-6`, `CD-13`, `CD-14`, `CD-15`, `CD-16`, `PF-4`) and green restored. **Reversion 2 — `followExclusion`'s `close()`/`start()` removed: `PF-1` and `PF-3` red** (`PF-1`: `expected true to be false` — the port still answers). **Reversion 3 — the `transport !== 'http'` guard removed: `PF-2` red** (`sent` froze at `1`, so the client's own pipes stopped carrying). **Reversion 4 — the pane's existence pair removed: `6` red** (`CD-1`, `CD-3`, `CD-5`, `CD-6`, `CD-10`, `CD-17`). **Reversion 5 — `onExclusionChanged` not called: `PF-4` red. Reversion 6 — the exclusion's existence pair removed (the control's own subject): `6` red** (`CD-1`…`CD-6`).

**THE MEASUREMENTS.** Four legs `0/0/0/0`: `npm test` **`2,975 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,977` over `135` files** (nine rows and one file more than `D-122`'s `2,966` of `2,968` over `134`), `typecheck`, `typecheck:tests`, `build`. ## D-124 — THE INVARIANT'S ROOT PAIR WAS COMPENSATING FOR NOTHING: a constraint body READS the half its own address does not carry, so the ONE pair at the store's root `[]` becomes TWO — one at `['operator-pane']` and one at `['operator-exclusion']` — each judging its own half and READING the other, the repair still settling the PORTS, and NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGING: this is a COUPLING fix and not a defect repair

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"You can call read() from inside of a constraint body, you don't need direct visibility"* — the correction of `D-123`, and every figure below is driven 2026-11-05 over the installed `provident-storeroom@1.9.3` through this module's own batch.

**WHAT THE PREMISE GOT WRONG, NAMED.** `D-123` put ONE pair at the store's root `[]` because it held that *"a pair at either half's address is asked for that half's landing op only, so only the root catches both edges with one body."* The FIRST clause is true and measured (`guide §7.6`'s membership rule; `D-56`/`D-66`); the SECOND is the error — a body asked for its own half can READ the other half, so "only the root" was false. **So the root pair was an UNNECESSARY COUPLING**: asked on EVERY write to the whole store, and existing solely to compensate for a visibility limitation that does not exist.

**THE CAPABILITY, MEASURED.** *(i) AT A LANDING INSTANT* a body's `store.read(<other address>, 'mem')` answers the other half — the pane's seat read `{exclusion:'mcp-disabled'}` while the act was the pane's own. *(ii) IT OPENS NO ATTEMPT*: the count at the body's entry and after its read are the SAME (`1`, the write's own), `attempt-opened` fires `0` times for it, and `0` listener deliveries cross a read of a listened address — *"a read inside a body runs INSIDE the attempt's window, opens nothing, and disturbs nothing"* (`guide §7.6`, measured there 2026-10-28 and re-measured here). *(iii) AT THE REGISTRATION INSTANT* the handle does not exist (`standing()` is `null` until `storeCreate` returns, and still `null` on that instant's own re-run though its `tier` IS set), so a body reads NOTHING there; what it does read is `context.value`, which at that instant IS the value at ITS OWN address — so the split is OWN half from `context.value` where no handle stands, BOTH halves from the store where one does. *(iv) AFTER A REPAIR LANDS* the re-run hands a pair `{address: <the pair's own address>, value: <the repair's last landing>}` — measured: a pane-address pair was handed `{exclusion:'mcp-disabled'}` — so the address and the value DISAGREE and **a body READS rather than trusting `context['value']`**.

**THE TRIGGER ANSWER, MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — AND IT IS TWO PAIRS.** This module's batch, adopted by a real store with every constraint wrapped in a counter: `write(['operator-exclusion'])` asked `["operator-exclusion-must-stand"]` before and `["operator-exclusion-must-stand","no-open-ports-under-an-open-pane"]` after, and the PANE's seat was in NEITHER; `write(['operator-pane'])` asked `["operator-pane-must-stand"]` / `["operator-pane-must-stand","no-open-pane-over-open-ports"]`, and the PORTS' seat was in neither; each record's own `triggered` set carried ONE address (`[["operator-exclusion"],…]`, `[["operator-pane"],…]`); and a control write at a third address asked nothing of either. **SIBLINGS DO NOT TRIGGER**, so the honest shape is TWO pairs and the `[]` pair — the only one asked for both — is REMOVED.

**THE SHAPE NOW, AND THE CLAUSE THAT LICENSES THE READ.** SIX declarations in ONE `createProfileStore` call (measured: one construction hands the package exactly ONE configuration): the four existence pairs, then `no-open-pane-over-open-ports` at `['operator-pane']` and `no-open-ports-under-an-open-pane` at `['operator-exclusion']` — two ids, because a batch may not name one handle twice and the construction refuses it (measured). Each seat judges the half its own address carries and reads the other; each refuses when both stand open and repairs by settling **the PORTS**, unchanged — `D-123`'s direction, through the module's one repair-write path `writeExclusion`, the credited arm, so `D-72`/`D-73` are intact. **THE LICENSING CLAUSE IS `guide §7.6`'s OWN, IN ITS OWN TERMS:** *"If a constraint needs to look for the data at a given location, it can read()"* (`D-50`), because *"the body is your code, it closes over the store handle you already hold, and `store.read(address)` is a published verb."* **AND THE READ IS NOT A WRITE PATH, NOT A DELIVERY AND NOT A CHECK**: it writes no byte, fires no listener, runs no pass and is no verdict — and it is taken ONLY where `context['value']` cannot answer, which at a registration instant is nowhere.

**NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED, AND THAT IS THIS ROW'S CLAIM RATHER THAN ITS AFTERTHOUGHT.** The invariant held at BOTH edges before this pass and holds after it: the pane cannot be opened over open ports, the ports cannot be enabled under an open pane, the repair settles the ports and leaves the pane alone, and the socket still follows the exclusion's delivery on `http` while `stdio` is untouched. **What moved is the ADDRESS and the COUPLING it was paying for.**

**THE ROWS, AND WHAT EACH REVERT PRODUCES — MEASURED, ON THE REAL SUITES.** `CD-16` IS RE-DERIVED AND ITS ROOT-ADDRESS CENSUS INVERTED (`D-46`): it asserted the invariant stands at `[]` and now measures that NO batch element stands at the root, that each seat stands at its own half, the two `triggered` lists above, ONE configuration per construction, and both edges through the module's verbs. Two rows are NEW: `CD-18` (each seat reads both halves and follows the store, driven with a value at the seat's own address that the store does not hold — a trusting body faults there and this one passes) and `CD-19` (one act, one repair: a repaired act lands EXACTLY two ops and delivers on the two handles its writes fired, an ordinary act one, and ten alternating faulting acts all commit so the restart budget is never reached). `VA-14`'s census moves `5 → 6` / `15 → 16` and now DRIVES the pane family's existence pair, which it declared for a pass and never drove. **Reversion 1 — BOTH seats removed: `11` rows red over `3` files** (`CD-1`, `CD-3`, `CD-6`, `CD-13`…`CD-16`, `CD-18`, `CD-19`, `PF-4`, `VA-14`). **Reversion 2 — the PANE's seat removed: `9` red, `CD-13` among them** (`CD-1`, `CD-3`, `CD-6`, `CD-16`, `CD-18`, `CD-19`, `PF-4`, `VA-14`), while EDGE TWO STILL HOLDS. **Reversion 3 — the PORTS' seat removed: `9` red, `CD-14` among them** (`CD-1`, `CD-3`, `CD-6`, `CD-15`, `CD-16`, `CD-18`, `CD-19`, `VA-14`), while EDGE ONE STILL HOLDS — so BOTH seats are load-bearing and neither is the other's understudy. **Reversion 4 — the PANE half taken from `context['value']` instead of read: `CD-14`, `CD-15`, `CD-16`, `CD-18`, `CD-19` red**, because the ports' seat then cannot see the pane at all — and **`CD-13` stays GREEN there, which is the whole of `D-123`'s error in one figure**: an absent or mismatched port half is judged as OPEN by the predicate, so the pane edge looked caught while the same fault was hiding. **Reversion 5 — the PORTS half taken from `context['value']`: `0` rows red, MEASURED AND STATED RATHER THAN CLAIMED AWAY** — at every landing instant this instance reaches, the value at a seat's own address IS the ports half (the pane's act carries the pane; a re-run carries the repair's landing, whose `exclusion` word is the ports' own), so no act distinguishes that read; it is kept because a body must not depend on a value the pass may substitute, and the absence of a red is the honest figure.

## D-125 — THE STORE IS THE STATE MACHINE AND THE RENDERED PANE IS A LISTENER'S PRODUCT: the operator's act writes `['operator-pane']` directly, the constraint's repair settles the ports and the panel carries the intent it preserved, the renderer renders the store's DELIVERY — and the pair gains `wanted` so the close edge has an intent to read, which is the datum `D-123`'s repair was destroying

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-05 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Following the pattern of the renderer listening to the stores, the user action to open the security pane should directly flip the state in the store. This will then cascade into the repair, then fire the listeners that render the pane and close the MCP. On close, it then deactivates the security pane, the constraint checks if the MCP settings are enabled, and then re-opens the MCP ports if so. Listeners then fire to open the ports and close the rendered pane. This ensures at the state machine level that the rendered-pane and MCP-open states are incompatible."*

**WHAT THE PREVIOUS DIRECTION GOT WRONG, AND IT IS A DIRECTION AND NOT A DEFECT.** `D-124` had `startOverlayApplication` hold the four-state machine in closure, seeded from the authored carrier, moving on the authored verb token, and REPORTING the predicate it computed over `IPC_SECURITY_PANE` — so **the renderer was the machine and the store followed it**, and the incompatibility was enforced by a SEQUENCE (the wiring's own transition, then its report, then the crossing's repair) rather than by the state machine the store holds. A sequence fails open the moment a turn is skipped, and it leaves the recorded state a projection of a local one. **THIS ROW INVERTS IT.**

**THE INTENT QUESTION, ASKED BEFORE ANY DESIGN AND ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT.** *(i) `['operator-exclusion']` carried `{exclusion}` ALONE* — `tier4` is DERIVED at the read (`tier4 === (exclusion === 'mcp-disabled')`) and is refused by the value arm as a member, so nothing but the two words was ever stored (measured: `exclusionAdmitsAt`'s closed member set; `CD-1`/`CD-2`'s `Object.keys` reading). *Its writers were two*: `IPC_SECURITY_EXCLUSION` → `settingsSurface.transition` → `settings.write`, and the invariant's repair `writeExclusion(…, PORTS_CLOSED)` — **and that second writer OVERWROTE the first**, so after a pane opened, *"were the ports supposed to be open?"* was unanswerable: the only datum that could have said so had been replaced by the word the repair settled to. *Its readers* are the gate (`applyExclusion`), `followExclusion` and the seats themselves. *(ii) `['operator-settings']` carries `{token, enabled, maxJournalLength, entries}`, and its `enabled` IS THE CAPABILITY GROUPS, MEASURED AND NOT ASSUMED*: `VALID_GROUPS` is `read`/`dispatch`/`graph`/`code`/`module`/`data`, `admitGroups` filters to exactly those, and `patchOf` hands the list to the gate as `groups` — so *"the MCP settings are enabled"* cannot mean that member. *(iii) NO DESIRED/EFFECTIVE SPLIT EXISTED ANYWHERE*: `grep` answers no `desired`/`intent`/`effective`/`requested` field in `src/`, and the gate has one state and one reader. **SO THE CLOSE PATH COULD NOT RESTORE THE INTENT WITHOUT A NEW DATUM, AND THAT IS SAID HERE BEFORE IT WAS BUILT.**

**THE TWO LAWFUL SHAPES, THEIR COSTS, AND THE ONE TAKEN.** **(A) DERIVED EFFECTIVE STATE** — the pair keeps the operator's intent and the ports obey `intent ∧ ¬paneOpen`, derived: no state can hold both, the store never holds an incompatible pair, and "re-open on close" is automatic. **It costs the user's own second sentence**: with nothing for the constraint to refuse, *"this will then cascade into the repair"* has no repair to cascade into, and `CD-13`…`CD-19`'s measured two-op edges become a derivation no act can observe. **(B) INTENT STORED, EFFECTIVE WRITTEN BY THE REPAIR** — a second datum records the intent and the repair settles the pair on BOTH edges: **taken**, because the correction names a repair, a constraint that CHECKS, and listeners that fire in consequence, and because it keeps the measured invariant (the pane's half is a factor of the settled word, so the pair can never hold both open) while giving the close edge something to settle to. **WHERE THE DATUM LIVES, AND THE SHAPE REJECTED FOR ITS COST**: `wanted` is the PAIR'S OWN SECOND MEMBER — `{exclusion, wanted}`, one value, one write, no tear, and the operator's transition states both words so an ordinary act is still ONE op. A FIFTH `mem` ADDRESS was lawful and rejected: it would need its own existence pair, its own creation repair and its own seat, would move the batch `6 → 8` and the first caller ordinal `5 → 6`, and would put the intent where a write could separate it from the state it qualifies. `wanted` is ADMITTED BUT NOT REQUIRED, and a pair naming none states that what stands is what was asked.

**THE INVERSION, QUOTED.** The user's act reaches ONE write: `startOverlayApplication`'s `act()` composes no state, holds no machine and writes the crossing — `crossing.write(asked)` — where the boolean comes from the MECHANISM handed **the store's own last delivered word**: `overlayTransition(before === true ? 'open' : 'closed', verb, …)`. A verb that asks for the state the store already reports is no write (`changed:false`), which is `D-82` clause 4's rule kept. **THE RENDERER IS A LISTENER**: the realm's ONE security subscription — `startSecurityShape`'s, the same delivery the record's re-read rides, and **no second registration is taken for the pane** (`D-90`'s one-consumer rule, measured: the module takes four subscriptions, one per crossing) — calls `overlayApplication.render()`, which reads the crossing's word and applies `overlayInertDeclaration`'s `{name, value, removal}` as ONE `state-slice` on the AUTHORED app root. **THE FOUR STATES**: `open` and `closed` are DERIVED from the store and nothing else; `closing` is the wiring's own transient, held while a close's write is in flight (a pane up and on its way out — the mechanism's own meaning), cleared by the delivery that answers it, and it **renders nothing** because the render predicate is the store's word alone; `held` is a member of the mechanism's closed set with **no producer in this app**, since a pane is up when the store says so and "up but unconfirmed" names no state left. A transient may stay local under `D-90`'s judgement — one writer in one realm, no persistence, no crossing, no second reader, outliving no delivery — the terms the drag preview was judged by.

**THE CASCADE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, DRIVEN AT THE PROCESS-SHAPED SURFACE.** **OPEN**: one write at `['operator-pane']` `{open:true}` → the pane's seat reads `wanted` enabled and the pane it just landed → the repair writes `{exclusion:'mcp-disabled', wanted:'mcp-enabled'}` → the exclusion's delivery patches the gate, reaches `onExclusionChanged` and drops the `http` socket (`stdio` untouched, measured fatal to close) → the pane's own delivery renders the pane. **CLOSE**: `{open:false}` → the same seat reads the intent the open edge PRESERVED → the repair writes `{exclusion:'mcp-enabled', wanted:'mcp-enabled'}` → the exclusion's delivery re-patches and RE-OPENS the socket → the pane's delivery un-renders it. **THE SECOND SEAT STAYS**: a write at `['operator-exclusion']` under an open pane is still settled closed, because siblings do not trigger (`D-124` measured), and its repair now writes back the intent it READ rather than the word it settled to.

## D-126 — THE RENDERED SURFACE AUDITED AGAINST ITS OWN PATTERN: eleven violations of *the store is the state machine and the rendered value is a listener's product* found, ONE of them an ABSENCE rather than a drift — the appearance act never reached the store on the human's path — and it is landed; the two findings that need a seat other than the wiring's are NAMED and not absorbed, together with a defect no unit owns yet

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Review the rest of the rendered surface for similar pattern violations"* — asked of the surface `D-125` had just corrected at one node, so that the correction is a RULE applied to the tree and not a single repair.

**THE PATTERN, AS THE MEASURE.** `D-125`'s ruling generalises to four tests: (1) an operator's act writes the STORE first; (2) a constraint repairs; (3) a listener RENDERS the delivery; (4) a local transient is lawful only with one writer, no persistence, no crossing, no second reader, and no outliving of the delivery that answers it. The census the audit walked: FOUR write sites under `src/` (the reply path's three acts and the drag sink), THIRTY-EIGHT authored nodes, and the renderer's DOM-originated turns.

**THE ONE ABSENCE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A DRIFT.** `#theme-dark`/`#theme-light`'s authored handlers wrote the AUTHORED CARRIER and the crossing was reached from exactly ONE call site — `replyRoute`'s notify, gated on a MUTATING reply — so **a human's click wrote the carrier and reached the store NEVER**, and no delivery could reconcile the two surfaces because no delivery was ever caused. Measured, and worse than inert: a real click forwards `String(target.value)` (`src/renderer/runtime.ts`), `HTMLButtonElement.value` is `''` unless the control authors one, so the click wrote the **EMPTY SETTING** — absence — into the carrier. Two instrument classes were structurally blind: `npm run divergence` compares the realms BEFORE any act, and every unit row dispatched, which is the agent's path. **THE FIX TAKES BOTH HALVES AND THE SECOND IS AN ENVELOPE ACT**: the handlers may not substitute a token (`theme-control.md` §2.3 item 2 fails exactly that, and `''` is a token outside the closed block §2.2(D)), so the token must come from the CALLER, and on the DOM path the caller is the BROWSER — the two controls now author `props: { value: THEME_DARK_TOKEN | THEME_LIGHT_TOKEN }`, declared once beside `THEME_INITIAL_TOKEN` and REFERENCED in the card so that §3.4 R-6 and §3.2 F-1's read of the card's QUOTED literals stays exactly the two handler bodies', the closed block still closed at two. `startThemeApplication` gains `attach()`, which resolves the two controls through `themeControlIds()` — derived from the authored card, never spelled — and hands the event's token to the SAME turn the reply path calls, split out as `commitSetting` so ONE body serves both causes. **AND THE LISTENER READS THE EVENT AND NOT THE CARRIER, WHICH IS MEASURED RATHER THAN PREFERRED**: the authored handler's write lands on a LATER turn (synchronously after the dispatch the carrier still held the previous token; it moved on the first microtask), so a listener reading the carrier would act on the value the click was REPLACING and would send nothing at all on a session's first act.

**THE TEN DRIFTS, EACH WITH ITS CLASS AND ITS MEASUREMENT** — none absorbed, none silently fixed: `#overlay-state`'s repeated verb is DROPPED by `lastCarried` (a second `toggle` measures `{verb:null,asked:null,wrote:false}` with the store still `true`), and the carrier cannot express a repeat act at all because the authored handler writes the same WORD — **an envelope act, not a wiring one**; `#gutter-status`'s `content` is written by the sink at release and by nothing else, while `['panes']` is `file`, so a second boot's read-out disagrees with the restored size (they agree today only because the authored `100` IS the crossing's default); `SecurePanels.cfg` paints `FIRST_RUN` BEFORE any delivery and re-spells the crossing's own placeholder; `lastApplied`/`lastCarried` swallow a record the surface no longer holds, so a graph-touching reply rebuilds the node and no re-apply happens; the `closing` transient outlives its delivery when the write is refused, because a refusal delivers nothing; `driveTabsLandingPage` hides BOTH tab terminals on any non-`committed` reading including a transport fault, which is clause 3 inverted; `renderZone`, `move`, `candidatesFor`, `previewOf` and `defaultSizeFor` have **no caller** under `src/`, contradicting `D-92`'s own claim that the shape's delivery calls `renderZone`; `writeOutcome()` has no `src/` reader, regrowing the class `D-117` deleted and being the reason the three divergences above are invisible; and `#gutter-pane`'s authored `size`/`min`/`max` are read by nothing since `D-117`. **THE LAWFUL NEAR-MISSES ARE NAMED SO NOBODY "FIXES" THEM**: the counter and the echo sit outside `D-82`'s six-family enumeration; the overlay's contents and the panes column's `resizable` are authored data; `applyPreview`/`applyCursor` are DECLARED transient DOM writes whose satisfying alternative is the corpus's own named hazard (a preview-by-dispatch re-renders the graph mid-gesture); and `panels.refreshDebug` has no address to be delivered from, the app graph being a rendering engine and not a store (`D-78` ruling 3).

**THE DEFECT NO UNIT OWNS YET, FOUND BY THE AUDIT AND FILED RATHER THAN FIXED — A DOM-ORIGINATED `state-slice` RENDERS ONE WRITE LATE.** `applyCommand` compiles the dirtied node immediately after `supervisor.apply` (`src/renderer/runtime.ts`), before that op's flush has settled; a `state-slice` issued while a flush is in flight therefore reaches the producing graph and never reaches `domPrevMap`, so `get_node_state` carries it while `get_rendered_html` does not. Measured on this tree: the click-driven delivery's `props.theme` present from microtask 3 and absent from `renderedHtml` through microtask 10, the same write repeated rendering at once, and the agent's path unaffected because `dispatch` awaits `flush()` first. **This is why `tests/theme-act.test.ts` asserts the GRAPH and not the serialization**: a row that asserted the attribute would either be red or, worse, would have to call the gap correct. It reaches the pane too — `startOverlayApplication`'s `renderTurn` writes `props.inert` from a delivery, and a human's toggle starts the same flush.

**THE MEASUREMENTS.** Four legs `0/0/0/0`: `npm test` **`2,987 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,989` over `136` files** (four rows and one file, `tests/theme-act.test.ts`'s `A-1`…`A-4`: the control's authored token, the dispatched click reaching the crossing and returning as a delivery, the `changed` guard surviving the click, and totality with the derivation of the ids), `typecheck`, `typecheck:tests`, `build`. `strata-marks.mjs index` moves `gating.sites` `284 → 288` in `37 → 38` files, `onNotice.sites` `2,476` unmoved. `demo/pane-drag-demo/demo.mjs` is REBUILT, its `--check` green. **THE REVERTS, STATED AS THE SHAPE OF THE CLAIM**: delete `attach()` and `A-2`/`A-3` red while `A-1` stands, which is what makes the two rows about the ACT; drop `props.value` and `A-1`, `A-2` and `A-3` red together, which is what makes the envelope half load-bearing rather than decorative. **THE BOUNDARY ROW NAMES ONE NEW PATH AND STOPS**: `tests/theme-act.test.ts` joins `DECLARED_SCOPE`; `src/renderer/renderer.ts` and `src/shared/demo-envelope.ts` are already declared, and `src/shared/dom-shim.ts` is deliberately ABSENT — `engine-pin` §2.2.4 closes the shim's member set and three other units' rows assert this pass never touches it, so the platform's `value` REFLECTION is supplied by the battery's own click, and that bound is stated in the row rather than paid for by growing a pinned harness.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-125`** as prose and never as a bare `D-n`: the change push; the repair's credit and its commit; the boot battery's teardown; the landing entry's id; the tab client in Stage A; the two-crossing ruling; the surplus instance collapsed with `data.*` pinned; the module registry's legacy file dropped; the data-flow convention audited clause by clause; the imperative boot write deleted; the `mem` pair's existence; the absence-keyed import inside the repair; `1.9.1`'s landing save; the purge's two successor addresses; the renderer swap refused and then landed; the zone family's enumeration, address and delivery; the frozen store deleted; the crossings given a leg; the view record's live leg; the appearance mechanism's consumer and its durability; the corpus made honest; the archive made checkout-visible; the `data` tier and the message log; `1.9.2`'s commit log; the app-state rows; `1.9.3`'s refusals; the refusal ledger; the registration instant; the five `data.*` routes; the declaration produced in a repair; the overlay's consumer; the instrument over the records; the handover's ceiling; the tab bar and the window controls; the three defects the window measured; the pane's open state as a fourth address and then the root pair taken away; and the inversion that makes the STORE the machine. **This row applies that inversion to the appearance family, records the whole surface's compliance against it, and refuses to absorb two findings whose seats are not the wiring's.**

## D-127 — A FAILED READ IS NOT A STATE: the tab terminals were driven from `absent`/`unread`/`refused` readings as though they were records, so a realm with no bridge and a single transport blip each BLANKED both authored pages — closed by taking the drive on `committed` alone, with `witness` made nullable so that "no record" stops being reported as "does not stand"

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Continue with the rest of the pattern violations"* — the follow-on to `D-126`, whose audit filed eleven findings and closed one; this row closes the second.

**THE DEFECT, MEASURED — `D-126`'s finding `F7`, and it is clause 3 INVERTED.** `driveTabsLandingPage` derived its witness as `reading.status === 'committed' ? reading.witness : null` and then drove BOTH authored pages from the resulting booleans, so every arm that was **not** a record — `absent` (a route that answered *there is no such member*), `unread` (a transport fault or a throw) and `refused` (the store declining to answer) — wrote `css.style: {display:'none'}` to `#tabs-landing-page` and `#tabs-error-page`. `D-82` clause 3 admits boot data "from file or constraint repairs"; this was boot data from a **failure**. Two consequences, both user-visible and neither measured by any row: on a realm with **no bridge at all** (a plain page, which `main()` explicitly supports — `if (!bridge) { … return }`) both sections the envelope authors `display: "block"` were hidden for the life of the page; and a single blip hid both until the next successful read, since a fault delivers no correction. **The instrument that would have caught it did not exist**: no row under `tests/` drives this role.

**THE FIX, AND THE ONE DECISION INSIDE IT.** The drive is taken on `committed` alone: every other arm issues **no write at all** and reports `status: null`, so the surface keeps the envelope's authored `display: "block"` or the last record's word, and the reading still REPORTS what it could not read instead of converting it into a state. **AND `TabsPageDrive.witness` BECOMES `boolean | null`**, because the old `false` was two different claims wearing one word: *the record says this terminal does not stand* and *there is no record*. A reader — and `describeTabsPages`'s own line, which now prints `witness=none` — can tell them apart, and the drive keys on the first. This is the same rule the appearance family took at `D-126`: a realm that has heard nothing renders nothing it was not authored with.

**THE ROWS ARE THE AUDIT'S OWN BATTERY** — `tests/renderer-delivery-compliance.test.ts`, new and gating, where each of `D-126`'s findings lands as it is closed: `DC-1` **no record, no drive** across all five non-committed arms (`absent` ×2, `unread` ×2, `refused`) with zero writes and `[witness,status,driven] = [null,null,false]`, and the control that the same instrument DOES record a real drive; `DC-2` **the record still drives, per terminal and in both directions** across the four combinations, so closing the no-record arm did not make the drive inert, each write being `css.style` on its own page; `DC-3` **a fault after a record changes nothing** — the sequence, not one reading, which is the arm that made a blip blank both pages; `DC-4` **totality** — a refused `state-slice` carries the runtime's own word with `driven: false` and is never converted into a success, a throwing runtime answers `threw`, and a `null` runtime answers no status. **THE REVERTS**: restore the old ternary and `DC-1` reds on all five arms and `DC-3` reds on its second turn; return `witness` to a `boolean` and `DC-1` reds on the reporting half while `DC-2` stands, which is what keeps the two halves distinct claims.

**THE MEASUREMENTS.** Four legs `0/0/0/0`: `npm test` **`2,991 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,993` over `137` files** (four rows and one file), `typecheck`, `typecheck:tests`, `build`. `strata-marks.mjs index` moves `gating.sites` `288 → 292` in `38 → 39` files, `onNotice.sites` `2,476` unmoved; `demo/pane-drag-demo/demo.mjs` is REBUILT, its `--check` green. **NO DOCUMENT MOVES**: `docs/L2/store-tabs-record/interface.md` declares the module's read answer and this is the WIRING's role, so no declared shape changes and none is restated.

**WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS `D-126`'S LIST AND NOT A SILENT ONE** — its findings `F2` (the overlay's carrier cannot express a REPEAT act, an envelope act), `F3` (the gutter read-out is written by the sink alone while `['panes']` is `file`), `F4` (the panes column paints the crossing's `FIRST_RUN` before any delivery), `F5`/`F9` (two guards swallowing a record the surface no longer holds), `F6` (a `closing` transient outliving a refused write), `F8`/`F10`/`F11` (five members with no caller, a `writeOutcome()` with no reader, and three authored props read by nothing), together with the render-lag defect `D-126` filed against the producing runtime. `strata/next-steps.md` row `4` is narrowed to those and row `3` stands.

**AND ONE FINDING WAS ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED BY MEASUREMENT — `F6`, THE `closing` TRANSIENT OUTLIVING A REFUSED WRITE.** The obvious fix is to clear the transient on any turn that READS the store's word, since a `closing` window means *the store has not answered yet*. It reds `OV-7` at once, which asserts the transient is REPORTED while a close's write is in flight: after the act the store still reads `open` because it has **not yet processed** the write, and a refused write leaves it reading `open` for the opposite reason. **THE TWO ARMS ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE BY READING THE STORE**, so no read can clear the transient and the only honest signal is the WRITE'S OWN ANSWER — which `startOverlayApplication` discards today (`void bridge?.security?.setPane(open)`). `F6` therefore waits on a wiring change to read that answer's refusal arm, and not on a cleverer guard.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-126`** as prose: the change push; the repair's credit and its commit; the boot battery's teardown; the landing entry's id; the tab client in Stage A; the two-crossing ruling; the surplus instance collapsed; the module registry's file dropped; the data-flow convention audited; the imperative boot write deleted; the `mem` pair's existence; the import inside the repair; `1.9.1`'s landing save; the two successor addresses; the renderer swap; the zone family; the frozen store deleted; the crossings' leg; the view record's live leg; the appearance mechanism's consumer and durability; the corpus made honest; the archive made checkout-visible; the `data` tier and the message log; `1.9.2`'s commit log; the app-state rows; `1.9.3`'s refusals; the refusal ledger; the registration instant; the five `data.*` routes; the declaration produced in a repair; the overlay's consumer; the instrument over the records; the handover's ceiling; the tab bar and the window controls; the three defects the window measured; the pane's fourth address and the root pair withdrawn; the inversion that makes the STORE the machine; the appearance act driven by a human's click; and the audit that measures the whole surface against them. **This row closes the audit's first wiring finding and starts the battery that will hold the rest.**
