## D-155 — `composeRecord` IS **KEPT**, AND THE REASON IS THAT A SPLIT WOULD NOT REMOVE IT: three of its five call sites are REPAIRS, the creation split is only lawful because its intermediate row is INVISIBLE, the removal needs the OPPOSITE order — and `D-139`'s test is thereby named NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and must be applied to the ACT and not to the function's name

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `pending.md` row `2`'s last item — the one `D-139` filed under *"NEED A DECISION THIS ROW DOES NOT TAKE"* — settled by `store-tabs-record`'s L3 and re-read against the tree by L0.

**THE VERDICT IS KEPT, AND IT IS NOT A SHRUG.** `pending.md` row `2`'s own closure condition is *"each composer is either deleted with its ancestry enforced and its battery re-grained, or kept with the reason recorded beside it; **none is left unjudged**"*. This item is now **judged**, and the reason lives at `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/design.md` §10. **`composeRecord`, `writeJoined` and `TabsCommitCarrier` all stay; no hunk is owed to L4 and no battery row is re-grained.** The verdict is earned by three independent grounds, and the strongest of them is not about invariants at all.

**GROUND (1) — A SPLIT WOULD NOT REMOVE THE COMPOSER.** `composeRecord` has **five** call sites, and **three of them are REPAIRS** — `healRecord`'s (`:771`), `mintRecord`'s (`:935`) and `repairOrderSeat`'s (`:1045`) — against **two acts** (`commit` at `:1175`, `remove` at `:1220`). **`D-83` measured that a repair must write the rows it names**, and `D-139` itself classes the repairs' values as must-stay. So splitting the two act sites would leave `composeRecord` **standing for the class this corpus has already ruled must stay**: the "deletion" would delete nothing and cost two commits. **A composer whose call sites fall into two classes must be judged twice**, and `D-139` judged it once by name.

**GROUND (2) — THE CREATION SPLIT IS LAWFUL ONLY BECAUSE ITS INTERMEDIATE STATE IS INVISIBLE, AND IT WOULD MAKE EVERY CLEAN CREATION ANSWER `repaired: true`.** `orderNamesItsTabs` loops over `seat` alone, so a member the seat does not yet name passes its arm — and `viewFrom` builds `entries` **from `order`** (`for (const id of seated) … entries[id] = row`), so the row written first is **unreadable by every constraint and every view**. The intermediate is a **hole, not a violation**. But at the seat write two rows then read active, `exactly-one-active` refuses, `written` resolves to the new id, and `healRecord` keeps it — so **every clean creation would report a repair the split caused on purpose**, turning `D-70`'s `repaired` answer (the member that says whether the ENGINE repaired) into noise about the pass's own sequencing. **And a repair landing between the two writes files `composeRecord(order, rows)` without the unseated row — erasing the creation outright**, after which the seat write wears the seat-naming refusal.

**GROUND (3) — THE TWO ACTS NEED OPPOSITE SEQUENCES, AND THE REMOVAL'S REPAIR USES THE WRONG DISCIPLINE.** Creation can write member-then-seat; removal **cannot**, because `order` naming a member the record no longer holds is precisely the seat arm's sentence. So removal must write **seat-then-member** — and the body that answers a seat fault is `repairOrderSeat`, whose `NO_HINTS` resolves the survivor by the **seat's own order** (arm iii) where the removal's discipline is the **removed entry's pre-position** (arm ii), carried by `exactly-one-active`'s hints. **A split does not merely reorder writes; it changes which repair reasons about the act.** One write is what makes the act's order-dependence irrelevant — that is `composeRecord`'s reason, in one sentence.

**AND THE ANCESTRY WAS NEVER THE MISSING THING, WHICH IS THE CORRECTION THE CORPUS NEEDS.** Unlike the two composers already removed, `tabs-must-stand` **does** enforce the root and `viewOf`'s fallback **does** read `['tabs', id]`, so `D-139`'s stated precondition was **MET here** — and the composer was still required. **So the precondition is not what decided any of the three cases.** What decided them is one question `D-139` never asked: **is the ACT expressible as a leaf write?** For panes and zones it was, once their id domains closed; **for the tab record it is not, because a tab id is MINTED AT RUNTIME** (`newTab: true`, `mintTabId`) — and that is also why the two closed domains cannot be re-used as a device here: **closing the tab-id set would delete the feature.**

**`writeJoined` AND `TabsCommitCarrier` ARE NOT COMPOSERS AT ALL, AND `D-139`'s INVENTORY MIS-FILED THEM.** They appear at the same sites, but the carrier is `write`'s **fourth position at ANY address** — so a leaf write would name its commit just as well — and `D-73`'s ruling is that a repair write naming neither is a **compile error**: *"Repairs that do not pass the commit are unsupported."* **They are an ARITY DEVICE enforcing the user's own ruling, and they are separable from the composer in principle and kept independently in fact.** An inventory that classifies by site rather than by role put a type-level safeguard of `D-73` in a list of formatting devices; the row says so rather than letting the filing stand.

**THE METHOD CORRECTION, STATED SO THE NEXT INVENTORY DOES NOT REPEAT IT.** `D-138`'s test — *is the write a LEAF of an enforced structure?* — is **necessary and not sufficient**. Applied to the **function's name** it asked "can a leaf write destroy a sibling?" and answered for all nine composers alike; applied to the **ACT** it asks "is what this entry point does expressible as leaves?", which is what actually differs between the three families. **`D-139` was right about the test and wrong about two separate preconditions** — the ancestry (which was met for tabs and unsatisfied for panes and zones) and the act's expressibility (which was the real discriminator all along). Its *"removable once the ancestry is enforced"* set is now **EMPTY**, its *"need a decision"* set is **SETTLED**, and its *"not removable"* set stands unchanged.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD.** `npm test` **`2,931 passed / 1 failed`** on the first reading and **`2,932 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,934`** over **`141`** files on the re-run, exit `0` — the failure being `tests/e2e/tier-readout/`'s `T-1` on `MCP error -32000: Connection closed`, the boot casualty class this corpus has carried since `D-147` and which reads **8/8 alone**; `tests/integration/store-tabs-record/` and `tests/unit/store-tabs-record/` **`52/52`** green, which is the re-grain's own check. Three pages moved and every one is at or under its ceiling: `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/design.md` **`121`/`150`** (rev 13, new §10), `docs/L2/store-tabs-record/interface.md` **`150`/`150`** (rev 6), `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/signatures.md` **`150`/`150`** (rev 5, transcribed — pinned by `signatures.test.ts` `C-7`).

## D-156 — THE TAB REMOVAL STOPS COMPOSING: `order` BECOMES A BIJECTION WITH THE ROWS, THE ACT BECOMES ONE `delete`, AND THE WORK SPLITS BETWEEN TWO REPAIRS THAT OWN DIFFERENT FAULTS — the user's ruling, and the three faults the measurement found behind it

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"This doesn't need a compose to remove a record. It needs a repair that reassigns the active tab (if the active tab is deleted - this already exists) and a repair that drops that tab from the order array (There should be a constraint that forces the order array to exactly contain the available tab ids)"*

**THE RULING IS RIGHT, AND THE MECHANISM IS MEASURED ON THE LIVE `1.10.0`.** A constraint registered at `['tabs']`, one record standing: **`delete(['tabs','tab-1'], 'mem')` asks the pair at `['tabs']` (one ask, `ctx.address` `['tabs','tab-1']`, `ctx.value` `undefined`) and leaves `order: ['landing','tab-1']` naming a row that is GONE**; **`write(['tabs','tab-9'], row)` asks the same pair and leaves a row the `order` does not name.** So both directions are open, both reach the parent's pairs, and the two violations are mirror images — which is precisely the structure a bijection plus a repair closes.

**AND THE CONSTRAINT IS CURRENTLY HALF A BIJECTION, WHICH IS THE DEFECT THE RULING NAMES.** `orderNamesItsTabs` loops over `seat` only: every id IN `order` must have a plain member, and **nothing requires every member to be IN `order`**. So `order ⊆ rows` is enforced and `order ≡ rows` is not — and `rows ⊄ order` is not merely legal, it is **invisible**: `viewFrom` builds `entries` by walking `order`, so a row outside the seat is unreadable by every body and every view. **That hole is also what made `D-155`'s creation-split argument work at all**, so closing it changes the ground under that row: **`D-155`'s ground (1) — that a split would leave the composer serving the three repair sites — STANDS and is now the whole licence; its ground (3) is SUPERSEDED IN FACT** (the opposite-sequence asymmetry ceases to exist once the constraint settles membership in either direction); **its ground (2) stands**, which is why no creation-side hunk is taken.

**THE DESIGN, AS SETTLED, IN FOUR DECISIONS.** **(1) THE PAIR IS EXTENDED, NOT MULTIPLIED.** One fault — the seat disagrees with the rows — takes one id and one repair; a seventh pair would give one state two sentences and buy a second whole-record repair inside one attempt. Its sentence re-grains to *"…carries no sequence of exactly its own tabs, once each"* and it gains exactly one clause: **an own key other than `order` that the seat does not name**. **THE WIDENING IS A CONTRACT CHANGE AND IS STATED AS ONE** — no id, `reason`, address, tier or route moves, but a record that passes today refuses at the next write. **(2) THE TWO REPAIRS OWN DIFFERENT FAULTS**, which the ruling's own wording requires: `repairOrderSeat` owns **membership** and `healRecord` owns **activeness**. `healedFamily` gains a required `scope` — `'seat'` seats what the record holds, drops stray keys, fills the three defaults and **preserves every `active` flag**; `'family'` does all that *and* §7's precedence. **CONVERGENCE IS MEASURED, NOT HOPED**: the pass asks one refusal at a time and re-runs from the top, the batch order is contractual, so the seat repair lands first and `exactly-one-active` is asked on the record it left. **And the alternative fails in this tree**: a full-heal seat repair resolves arm (iii), its write leaves one active, and the re-run passes — so the activeness pair is never asked and **removing the active tab would silently re-seat the seat's first row instead of the pre-position**. **(3) THE ACT IS ONE `delete`.** Shape arms and `namesASeat` refuse before any store verb as they do now; the act takes the PRE view, refreshes `lastView`, answers already-absent without a store act, performs `delete(['tabs', id], TABS_RECORD_TIER)` — **no composition, no value** — refreshes `lastView` again, and answers from `standsAsIntended` against the **delete-only expectation** (`order` and rows minus the id, flags untouched). **(4) `commit` STAYS COMPOSED IN THIS PASS AND ITS ROW-WRITE IS OWED**, because a composed intent satisfies the bijection by construction — so the two acts cannot disagree about the record's shape while only one of them moves.

**`repaired` KEEPS ITS MEANING ON THE THREE CASES, AND THAT IS WHY THE EXPECTATION IS THE DELETE-ONLY ONE.** Removing a **non-active** tab → bare `committed` (the seat repair ran and left exactly what the removal meant). Removing the **active** tab with a survivor → `committed` **with `repaired: true`** (the successor is the engine's choosing, and predicting it would be a second copy of §7's precedence). Removing the **last** tab → `repaired: true` (the floor differs from the empty expectation). **A removal whose successor is the pre-position therefore cannot answer a bare `committed`** — which is exactly `D-70`'s signal working rather than being suppressed.

**THREE FAULTS THE MEASUREMENT FOUND BEHIND THE RULING, EACH OF WHICH WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AS SILENT DAMAGE.** **(a)** Under the six pairs a **descendant delete hands `tabsMustStand` `value: undefined`**, so it mints the floor and **erases the siblings** (measured) — the act cannot delete a row while that body reads the act's value. **(b)** A **leaf row write hands the seat pair the ROW**, so a repair taking its view from the act's value **replaces the family** (measured: two tab rows both erased). **(c)** The empty-view floor must survive **at the registration instant** or `storeCreate` throws. **So both bodies judge the record at the CONTEXT's address** — root or registration hands the value, anything deeper reads the store raw — **and the seat repair parses the record by its own keys, so it SEATS as well as drops.** None of the three is in the ruling; all three follow from taking it, and they are the reason a design pass exists between a right instruction and a landing.

**`composeRecord`'S FATE, RESTATED WITHOUT OVERCLAIMING.** It **survives**, for the repairs and for `commit`'s intent. **What changes is that the REMOVAL ACT no longer composes**: its site keeps the name and loses the write, and its product is the comparator's expectation rather than a written value. **No deletion of the composer happens here and this row does not claim one** (`D-155`'s ground 1 is the reason it could not have).

**THE GATE, AND IT IS THIS ROW'S FIRST DUTY.** The design pages record that **H1–H8 must not land on their word alone** — the ruling must be registered before a hunk lands. **This row is that registration**, so `store-tabs-record`'s L4 may now take H1–H8: the sentence, the address-discriminated body with its sixth clause, `repairOrderSeat`'s own-key parse with the `'seat'` scope, `healedFamily`'s required `scope`, `tabsMustStand`'s root-only absence, `remove`'s two `lastView` refreshes plus the delete plus the comparator, and eight docblocks replaced in place. **Its battery is the landing pass's** (`D-3`): five new `crossing.test.ts` rows and **two re-grains with their reasons** — the `repaired`-on-`remove` gloss, and the creation row seeding `{tab-1: row}` with no seat, which must now **seat** it rather than take the floor.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-155`'S** — nothing in this row moves a byte: the design pages are its whole product and they sit at `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/design.md` **`126`/150** (rev 14), `docs/L2/store-tabs-record/interface.md` **`149`/150** (rev 7) and `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/signatures.md` **`150`/150** (rev 6, `C-7` pin satisfied). **The `1.10.0` probes were taken in `/tmp` and deleted; the package was never modified.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-155`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a ruling that turned a whole-record rewrite into one delete, the half-open constraint that made it necessary, a repair-ownership split whose alternative silently re-seats the wrong tab, three faults that only measurement surfaced, and the gate that says a hunk may not land before its ruling is filed.**

## D-157 — `D-156` LANDS: THE TAB REMOVAL IS **ONE DELETE**, `order` IS A BIJECTION WITH THE ROWS, AND THE TWO REPAIRS OWN DIFFERENT FAULTS — and the battery's own instrument had to move because **every clause of the seat pair has a REPAIR**, so a repaired fault could never measure a REFUSED write

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-156`'s eight hunks, landed in `src/main/tabs-record/index.ts` alone, with its battery re-grained by the pass that owns it (`D-3`).

**WHAT LANDED.** `orderNamesItsTabs` gained its **sixth clause** — *an own key other than `order` the seat does not name* — so the pair now enforces `order ≡ rows` and not merely `order ⊆ rows`; **a row outside the seat is no longer legal, which matters because it was never merely legal but INVISIBLE** (`viewFrom` walks `order`). Its sentence re-grains to *"…carries no sequence of exactly its own tabs, once each"*. `healedFamily` takes a **required `scope`**: `'seat'` seats what the record holds, drops stray keys, fills the three field defaults and **preserves every `active` flag**; `'family'` does all that **and** §7's successor precedence — so `repairOrderSeat` owns **membership** and `healRecord` owns **activeness**, each by construction rather than by hope. `tabsMustStand`'s absence arm is **root-only**. **And `remove` performs ONE `delete(['tabs', id], TABS_RECORD_TIER)`**: shape arms and `namesASeat` refuse before any store verb, the act takes the PRE view and hands it to the observation, answers an already-absent tab **without a store act**, composes the **delete-only expectation and never writes it**, refreshes `lastView` on both arms, and answers from the comparator.

**THE ADDRESS RULE IS THE LANDING'S LOAD-BEARING HUNK, AND BOTH BODIES NOW OBEY IT.** `deeperThanRecord(address)` — an array strictly longer than `['tabs']` and prefixed by it — reads the record **raw through the handle**; the root (a registration ask, a root write, a hand-driven context) judges **the value the act hands**. Without it, `D-156`'s measured faults land as silent damage: **a leaf row write hands the seat pair the ROW** (two tab rows erased in the measurement) and **a descendant delete hands `tabsMustStand` `value: undefined`** (the floor minted over the siblings).

**THREE THINGS THE LANDING PASS MEASURED THAT THE DESIGN COULD NOT PREDICT.** **(i)** At `1.10.0` the **registration repair context carries BOTH `write` and `pending`**, so `isCommitCarrier` cannot discriminate the instant — `repairOrderSeat` branches on `typeof context.write === 'function'`, which is the `write`-member rule `D-73` states. **(ii)** **`delete(['tabs','never-was'])` throws `AddressNotFound`** rather than succeeding emptily, so the already-absent arm must precede every store verb — the ordering is not stylistic. **(iii)** The three `repaired` cases were each measured rather than reasoned: non-active → bare `committed`; active with a survivor → `committed, repaired: true` (the successor deliberately not predicted); last tab → `repaired: true` with the minted floor standing.

**THE BATTERY, AND THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT IT EXPOSED.** `crossing.test.ts` went **31 → 36 rows**: five new ones state what the change now **rests on** and nothing measured before — *a leaf row write SEATS* (`tab-9` lands in both the record and the seat), *a stray key is DROPPED*, *the LEAF-WRITE HAZARD CONTROL* (a row write must not wipe its siblings — the guard for the erasure measured above), *a descendant delete must NOT mint*, and *the delete direction* with its three `repaired` cases. One row was re-grained (the creation row seeding `{tab-1: row}` now **SEATS** it instead of taking the floor, per H3's own-key parse) and one gloss was re-grained (the `repaired`-on-`remove` description, from the composed intent to the delete-only expectation). **NO TOMBSTONE WAS NEEDED — no row's subject left**, which is the difference between this landing and the two composers before it.

**AND THE ROW THAT MEASURES ZERO DELIVERY HAD TO CHANGE ITS INSTRUMENT, WHICH IS A FINDING ABOUT THE CONSTRAINT SET.** That row asserts *a write a pair REFUSES delivers NOTHING*, and its refusing instrument was a **stray own key** on the record — which the new sixth clause now **repairs and drops**, so the pair passed on the re-run and no refusal occurred. **THE REASON IS THAT EVERY ONE OF THE SEAT PAIR'S SIX CLAUSES HAS A REPAIR**: a fault the module can name is repaired inside the caller's commit and the re-run passes, so **a repairable fault can never produce a refused write**. The instrument moved to a row's **`label`** — a member `healedFamily` copies through untouched, so the marker survives every repair and the write refuses again on the re-run — and the claim is now measured against an **unrepairable** fault, with a second half asserting the refused title landed nowhere. **A battery row whose instrument the module learns to repair is a row that silently stops measuring**, and only running it said so.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD.** `npm test` **`2,937 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,939`** over **`141`** files, exit `0` — **up five rows and no file**, which is the whole battery move; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **exit `0`** with the index REGENERATED at **`328` gating sites in `44` files** (`323` at `D-146`'s regen — the five new rows); `refs` resolves **`157`** rows; the demo bundle current at **39 inputs**. `tests/integration/store-tabs-record/` and `tests/integration/central-data/` **`111/111`** over `10` files.

**WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT DO.** **`commit` still composes** — its intent satisfies the bijection by construction, so the two acts cannot disagree about the record's shape while only one moves — and **its row-write is OWED**, with the same delete-shaped argument already available to it. **`composeRecord` survives**, for the repairs and for `commit`'s intent and comparator; **nothing here claims its deletion**, and `D-155`'s ground (1) is why there was nothing to claim. **The audit's remaining seven of eleven still stand as `pending.md` row `1`.**

**ONE FRAGILITY WORTH NAMING FOR WHOEVER COMES NEXT.** With `D-155`'s judgement and this landing together, **`crossing.test.ts`'s pre-position row is now the ONLY place §7's successor precedence arm (ii) is measured** — so it must not be retired later without a replacement, and a future pass that finds it "duplicated" should read that sentence first.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-156`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a whole-record rewrite becoming one delete, a constraint that became a bijection, two repairs that now own different faults by construction, three behaviours only a probe could establish, and a battery instrument that had to be made unrepairable before it could measure a refusal.**

## D-158 — CREATING A TAB IS ONE ROW WRITE AND THE SEAT REPAIR APPENDS IT: the mirror of `D-156`, and the two things creation does not share with removal — the APPEND POSITION stops being the act's to promise, and the PRE refresh becomes LOAD-BEARING because a stale observation would deactivate the tab the caller just opened

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Creating a new tab should be doable as a write, with the repair appending it to the order"* — `D-157`'s owed item, and the creation side of `D-156`'s ruling.

**THE MECHANISM WAS ALREADY PROVEN, SO NOTHING HERE IS SPECULATIVE.** `order` is a bijection with the rows (`D-157`), `repairOrderSeat` heals with `scope: 'seat'` — seating what the record holds by parsing it by its **own keys** and preserving every `active` flag — and a battery row landed at `D-157` already measures that `store.write(['tabs','tab-9'], 'file', row)` leaves the row **and** the seat naming it. **So the act is the only thing that changes**: `commit` stops composing and writing a whole record and writes **one row**.

**SETTLED QUESTION (1) — THE APPEND POSITION CONFIRMED FOR THE ACT'S OWN CASE, AND REFUTED AS A LAW.** A leaf write leaves exactly **one** stray key, and the seat parse's tail is `Object.keys` minus the seat key, so the new id lands **last** — the same position the composed act spelled with `[...order, row.id]`. Measured at the route shape: `['landing','tab-9']`, and the control `['landing','tab-1','tab-2','tab-9']`. **BUT WITH TWO OR MORE STRAYS THE TAIL IS THE STORE'S KEY-ORDERED IMAGE AND NOT INSERTION ORDER** — `profile-file.test.ts`'s boot row reads root keys `['panes','tabs','theme']`, `D-97` measured `{value, removal}` → `{removal, value}`, and JS own-key enumeration puts an index-like id first. **So the act's semantics do not change, and the position simply stops being the act's to promise**: a reader may rely on the **seat's array sequence**, never on having predicted where an append lands. That sentence belongs in the pages, because a caller who assumes insertion order will be right today and wrong the first time two strays appear.

**SETTLED QUESTION (2) — THE EVALUATION TRACE, VERIFIED, WITH TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF'S READING.** For a new row written `active: true` beside a standing active row: **the seat pair refuses, the `'seat'` repair appends and preserves both flags, the re-run now has two actives, `exactly-one-active` refuses, `healRecord` keeps the written referent, and a third evaluation passes — one delivery, and the answer is `committed, repaired: true`.** The corrections: **(a)** `exactly-one-active` cannot speak first for a **stronger** reason than ask order — **an unseated row is INVISIBLE to `viewOf`**, whose entries are built from `order`, so to that pair the record reads exactly as it stood and would **pass**; the batch order and restart-from-top merely make its first ask land on the seated record. **(b)** `written` resolving to the new id does **not** depend on which refresh the act makes — every handle-side view lacks it, pre- or post-write — **but the PRE refresh is still OWED and load-bearing**: a **stale** `lastView` (a bypassing `data.write` never refreshes it) that carries that id's row makes `before !== undefined`, so `written` falls to `null` and `healedFamily`'s default `keep = standing[0]` **deactivates the tab the caller just created**. A refresh whose absence is invisible in the happy path is exactly the kind of line this corpus has learned to keep.

**THE COMPARATOR AND THE THREE CASES.** Expectation = `composeRecord(pre.order.includes(row.id) ? pre.order : [...pre.order, row.id], {...pre.entries, [row.id]: row})`, compared through `standsAsIntended` and **never written**. **(i) an UPDATE** — a row for an id the record already seats: no stray key, the bijection holds, no repair runs, **bare `committed`**. **(ii) a NEW row with `active: false`** — the seat repair runs and leaves exactly the expectation, so **bare `committed`**; the member changes only where a field default was filled, which is the row's own fault and is how the act answers today. **(iii) a NEW row with `active: true` beside an active row** — **`committed, repaired: true`**, the new tab the survivor. **A stray the act did not name is also `repaired: true`** — reported rather than hidden.

**THE GUARDS, AND ONE THAT IS NOW LOAD-BEARING ON ITS OWN.** `malformed-row` and `namesASeat` are unchanged and stay before any store verb — and **`namesASeat` is now the ONLY guard there, which makes it structural rather than tidy**: a leaf write at `['tabs','order']` would replace the seat, the pair would refuse (the seat is no longer an array), and `seatViewFrom` **skips the seat key** — so the repair would **drop the row the caller wrote** and keep everything else. The act must not refuse an otherwise-legal unseated row: **that write IS the creation**, the pair refuses inside the commit, and its repair seats it.

**WHAT THE ACT OWES AROUND THE WRITE.** `lastView` exactly as `remove` owes it — **pre** (one read, two uses: the comparator and the observation) and **post on both arms** — with the pre refresh load-bearing per the correction above. **FIELD DEFAULTS: nothing.** `healedFamily` fills `label`/`target`/`lastActiveAt` in **both** scopes, so the seat repair already lands them, and pre-filling them in the act would be a second authority — and would **suppress `repaired`**, which is the signal the renderer needs.

**`composeRecord`'S FATE, AGAIN WITHOUT OVERCLAIM.** It **stays**, for the three repairs **and for both comparators** — `remove`'s delete-only expectation and `commit`'s creation expectation — compared and never written (`D-155` ground 1). **`D-155`'s ground (2) is DISCHARGED and not waived**: a clean creation answers a bare `committed`, which is the honesty that ground was protecting.

**THE GATE, AND THIS ROW IS IT.** The design pages record that H9–H11 await a register row of their own, because `D-157` books this instruction as **OWED**. **This row is that registration**, so `store-tabs-record`'s L4 may now take: **H9** the act — pre `viewOf` read → `lastView` → **one leaf write** → post refresh on both arms → the creation expectation through `standsAsIntended`, with **five composition statements deleted**; **H10** five docblocks and headers replaced in place (the file header, `TabsRecord`'s `commit`, two in `composeRecord`, `createTabsRecord`'s); **H11** nothing else moves — no exported name, no surface, no channel, no type, and `signatures.md` byte-unmoved but for its rev token (`C-7`). **Its battery is the landing pass's** (`D-3`): **four new rows** — the creation through the route (seat appended, row admitted, one active, derived `landing`, **ONE delivery**); the `active: false` new row answered **bare `committed`** (a case nothing states today); **the stale-observation control**, which reds on H9 with its pre refresh removed — and the append position at the route (three creations in creation order; a re-`commit` does not move a seated id) — plus **three re-grains**: the two leaf-write rows' false gloss that *"`commit` is not changed in this pass"*, the section prose around them, and `repaired`-on-`commit`'s gloss to the creation expectation.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-157`'S** — nothing in this row moves a byte; its product is the design pages, at `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/design.md` **`128`/150** (rev 15), `docs/L2/store-tabs-record/interface.md` **`149`/150** (rev 8) and `docs/L3/store-tabs-record/signatures.md` **`150`/150** (rev 7, `C-7` satisfied).

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-157`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records the creation side of a ruling that already had its removal side, an append position that is right once and ungoverned after, a stale observation whose absence would deactivate the tab just created, and a guard that became structural the moment the seat could be written by address.**

## D-159 — `D-158` LANDS: CREATION IS **ONE ROW WRITE** AND THE SEAT REPAIR APPENDS — and the row must CORRECT ITS OWN PREDECESSOR, because the pre refresh it called LOAD-BEARING is **not observably so**: the activeness pair refreshes its own capture on every ask, so the design's owed control could not fail and the battery had to measure the invariant instead

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-158`'s three hunks, landed in `src/main/tabs-record/index.ts` alone, with its battery re-grained and its residual docblocks closed by the passes that own them.

A caller who assumes insertion order is right today and wrong the first time two strays appear, and the row says so.

```ts
export function rowForSeat(seat: ActedSeat): TabsRecordRow {
  const lastActiveAt = new Date().toISOString()          // the clock, read ONCE, at the call
  return seat.kind === 'open'
    ? { id: seat.id, target: seat.target, active: true, lastActiveAt }
    : { ...seat.row, active: true, lastActiveAt }
}
```

## D-164 — `F3`'S SECOND AUTHORITY AND `F5`/`F9` LAND, AND THE STATE CHECK HAD TO BE REFUTED AND CORRECTED BEFORE IT COULD SHIP: a props read cannot tell *not yet rendered* from *already absent*, so an absence-keyed skip is unsound and a **removal always paints**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-163`'s eight hunks and its two-guard replacement, landed in `src/renderer/renderer.ts`, with the state check failing its own battery and amended at `docs/L3/renderer-wiring/design.md` rev 13.

**WHAT LANDED.** `startGutterAffordance`'s `write` closure — the ONE `applyCommand` `state-slice` that wrote the clamped figure into `#gutter-status` beside `['panes']` at `file` — is **deleted**, and the same closure returns `renderPaneSize`, which `startViewShape` takes as a **third parameter** and calls **third in its ONE subscription body** (no second subscription, `D-90`). **`lastApplied` is deleted at both application sites**, the overlay's seed with it, and each paint now decides by reading the node its own write would land on, through a total `authoredPropOf`. **Eighty-nine lines left the file** and `lastCarried` at both sites, the overlay's `derived`, and `release`'s `R3`→`R4`→`R5` order all survive. **`F3`'s skip is a PRESENCE comparison** (`authored.setting === value`, a never-`undefined` string, no removal arm) and is untouched.

**AND THE RULE `D-163` SHIPPED WITH WAS WRONG — REFUTED BY ITS OWN BATTERY BEFORE IT COULD STAND.** The skip was `held === wanted`, justified as *"not owed means the write would be a no-op by construction"*. **For a REMOVAL that is false**: after the store drops the prop, `nodeState`'s `states[0].props[name]` reports it **absent while the render has not yet applied the removal** — so `held === undefined === wanted`, the paint is **skipped**, and the DOM keeps the attribute. Measured: **`OV-12`** read `close: the removal arm lands` as **`false`**, and **`OV-14`** found the tag **still carrying `inert="true"`** after a delivery that should have removed it. **The rendered pane was closed and the DOM said otherwise.**

**THE CORRECTION, AND ITS RULE STATED ONCE.** A skip now requires a **POSITIVE SETTLED MATCH** — `wanted !== undefined && held.readable && held.held === wanted` — with **the operands ordered so a removal is decided before any read**, so **a removal delivery takes NO `nodeState` read and always paints**, paying one redundant idempotent `state-slice`. **THE GENERAL RULE, RECORDED AS `OV-7`'s SIBLING** (the store read cannot tell *not yet processed* from *refused*; a props read cannot tell *not yet rendered* from *already absent*): **a read of a surface cannot establish that a write is unnecessary when the write is a REMOVAL, because absence-before-render and absence-after-render are indistinguishable — an absence-keyed skip is always unsound and only a presence-keyed match may skip.** That is `D-163`'s defect turned into a rule, and it is the third time this series has found that a *skip* is where the damage hides.

**`F3`'S NAMED SYMPTOM STILL DOES NOT CLOSE, AND `pending.md` ROW `1` NOW SAYS SO.** A delivery is the paint's only trigger, so **a second boot that receives none leaves the read-out as the envelope authors it** — the write that disagreed is gone, the disagreement is not. Both closes stay **routed**: a boot paint (refused by `D-96`/`T-4`) and the envelope's authored `content` (`app-envelope`'s `D-129` row). **`F5`/`F9` DO close**, and the row is re-grained from seven findings to **five**.

**THE BATTERY MOVED, AND EVERY NEW ROW WAS PROVED ABLE TO FAIL.** `PS-3` reads **`0`** `applyCommand`s where it read `1`, its flag property carried by `commitPane`/`clearDrag` so the zero cannot come from an unreached release. **`OV-14(b)`**'s `idle.written` moves **`false` → `true`** — the redundant idempotent removal write is the price of never skipping an owed paint — and **`T-5`**'s arity **`2` → `3`**. **`RS-1`…`RS-5` are NEW and GATING** in `tests/unit/renderer-wiring/state-checked-paint.test.ts`: the family arm (`'default'` with an available figure paints **nothing**), the positive settled match, **`RS-3` the removal that always paints even where `held` already reads `undefined`** — **the row that would have caught `OV-12`/`OV-14`** — unreadable-fails-open, and the **read counts** (one per positive-wanted site, **zero** on a removal). **`RS-3` and `RS-5` were proved to red on the pre-correction predicate at EACH SITE SEPARATELY**, with the source restored byte-identically, and the file's path claimed on `renderer-wiring`'s `modules.json` entry and in the worktree boundary's `DECLARED_SCOPE` in the same pass (`D-146`'s precedent).

**ONE CONTRADICTION IS LEFT OWED AND IS NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED.** `docs/L3/renderer-wiring/design.md` §8 still enumerates **four** `RS` rows with different content from the **five** that were built, and `D-163`'s own sentence says *"`RS-1`…`RS-4`"*. **The pages and that row are superseded in fact** — a five-row grain is what landed, and `RS-3`'s absence-keyed clause is the one the pass exists for — and the design page's §8 re-grain is **owed to its next rev**, not smuggled in here (`D-46`).

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD.** `npm test` **`2,950 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,952`** over **`142`** files (`+1` file for the new gating battery); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **exit `0`** at **`341` gating sites in `45` files** (`336`/`44` at `D-161` — exactly `+5` rows, `+1` file); `refs` resolves **`164`** rows; the demo bundle rebuilt to **39 inputs**. One intermediate reading failed `tests/e2e/focus-retirement/`'s `F-1` on the boot-casualty class the corpus has carried since `D-147` — **5/5 alone**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-163`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a sink's write deleted and painted from the delivery, two change-guards replaced by a state check, that state check refuted by its own battery and corrected into a rule, a removal that now always paints, five new gating rows with two proved red at each site, and a symptom that survives its own fix and is said so in the queue.**

## D-165 — THE BOOT CASUALTY IS NOT ONE FILE'S AND THE SUITE IS NOT RELIABLY GREEN ON A CLEAN TREE: the same `-32000: Connection closed` fell on `focus-retirement`'s `F-1` twice, `pane-drag-temp`'s `P-1` twice and `tier-readout`'s `T-1` three times in one session, each passing alone, and the brief's "no failures on a clean tree" was therefore a claim the instrument cannot always honour

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** the readings taken across `D-152`–`D-164`, each full-suite run recorded, and the transcription error that reading produced twice.

**THE CENSUS, FROM ONE SESSION'S RUNS AND NOT FROM IMPRESSION.** The full suite was run repeatedly on a tree whose `git status` was empty. **Seven runs carried exactly one failure, and it was a different file each time**: `tests/e2e/focus-retirement/`'s `F-1` **twice**, `tests/e2e/pane-drag-temp/`'s `P-1` **twice**, `tests/e2e/tier-readout/`'s `T-1` **three times**. **Every one failed with `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` (or, once, `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` on `dist/renderer/index.html`), every one passed when run ALONE, and every one is a booting `tests/e2e/` file.** The immediately following run of the same clean tree read **`2,950 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,952`** with zero failures.

**WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE BRIEF'S OWN CLAIM, WHICH SAID *"no failures on a clean tree"*.** **It is a claim the instrument cannot always honour**, so it is re-worded to *"no failures on a CASUALTY-FREE run"* with the flake named, and it now requires that **a reading names both figures and never only one**. The `brief.md` §6 cell for `npm test` is a floor every pass quotes; a floor that is true two runs in three is a floor that will eventually be quoted falsely — **and it was: this seat transcribed the dirty figure into a decision row twice (`D-159`, `D-164`)**, both times because a run carrying the casualty reads one lower and looks like a reading.

**AND THE PREVIOUS ATTRIBUTION WAS TOO NARROW.** The corpus has described this as *"tier-readout's e2e is the known boot casualty"* since `D-147`. **Measured, the identity ROTATES across every booting e2e file** — three of them in one session — so it is a class about **spawning Electron under parallel harness load**, not a property of one battery. **A row that names one file is a row that will be read as "that file is flaky"**, which is why this one names the census instead.

**WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED.** No cause is established and none is guessed: the two shapes observed — `-32000: Connection closed`, and one `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` on a `dist/renderer/index.html` that existed before and after — are consistent with a spawn/mount race under parallel load and are **not** evidence of a product defect, since each file passes alone and the `dist` file was measured present outside the run. **A pass that wants the cause will have to instrument the spawn**; this row does not pretend otherwise.

**WHAT IT COSTS, STATED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT.** A single full-suite run is a **probabilistic** instrument — roughly one run in two carried the casualty here. **So a green reading needs a re-run**, and a reading with the casualty in it must never be transcribed as the head's. That is now written in `brief.md` §6's own cell rather than in a decision row nobody re-reads.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-164`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a census rather than an anecdote, a brief claim corrected because the instrument will not always honour it, a narrower attribution widened, and the two transcription errors this seat made from readings that were one row short.**

## D-166 — `F6` IS DESIGNED AND IT IS UNBLOCKED: a refused close leaves `closing` standing because the ONE signal that could clear it is `void`-ed, the seam is the member's own declared answer, and a refused close is a state **NOTHING MEASURES** — which is the row the pass has to add

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `pending.md` row `1`'s `F6`, the one finding of the five remaining whose own *"waits on"* cell **names no foreign owner**.

**WHY IT IS UNBLOCKED, SINCE THE ROW LEFT IT UNNAMED RATHER THAN CLEARED.** `D-128`'s own sentence puts the fix inside this module — *"`F6` needs the write's own answer, which `void bridge?.security?.setPane(open)` discards"* — and `D-127` calls it *"a wiring change"*, not another unit's row; `src/renderer/renderer.ts` is `renderer-wiring`'s. **No row anywhere pins the `void` or pins a refusal**, so the worst reading is that the cell is incomplete rather than that a blocker exists. The design pass says so plainly rather than treating an omission as a permission it did not check.

**THE DEFECT, MEASURED.** `renderer.ts:1039` is `write: (open) => { void bridge?.security?.setPane(open) }`, and `setPane`'s declared answer is **`Promise<{status:'committed'} | {status:'refused'; reason; message}>`** — **the `void` discards exactly the signal the finding names.** The act then sets the transient **synchronously** on a close write (`if (wrote && !asked) transient = 'closing'`), and `renderTurn`'s **`if (clear) transient = null`** is the transient's **only** clearing site — **reached by a delivery and by nothing else.** **So a refused close leaves the pane down, the store unmoved, and the wiring believing it is still on its way out**, with no delivery coming to correct it.

**THE SEAM IS THE MEMBER'S OWN ANSWER, WIDENED — NOTHING NEW.** `OverlayPaneCrossing.write` goes from `(open) => void` to **`(open) => Promise<unknown> | void`**; `main()`'s site **drops the `void`** and returns the promise; and the act keeps it in **one `settle(ordinal, answer)`** that reuses `renderTurn`'s existing clearing path. **No new member, no new route, no new address, no fifth word, and no new register** — the cost is one promise continuation inside a closure that already holds the transient, and one ordinal so a superseded answer cannot clear a newer act (`G1`'s discipline).

**WHAT A REFUSED CLOSE LEAVES: THE STORE'S WORD.** `derived` has exactly one assignment (`storedOpen()`), so clearing the transient falls back to **`open`** — the pane is up and the wiring now says so. **`D-125`'s render predicate is untouched** (the render reads the store alone) and **`D-82` clause 4 holds** (the write is the external cause and the refusal is its answer). **TWO ALTERNATIVES ARE REFUSED IN WRITING**: a failure word of the wiring's own, because the four-state set is the **mechanism's** and closed and `held` already has no producer here; and keeping the transient with a recorded reason, because it would **outlive the very answer that settles it** — the one term `D-90`'s judgement set.

**A REFUSAL IS REPORTED, AND SILENCE WOULD BE THE CLASS `D-117` DELETED.** `console.error` for a `refused` answer and `console.warn` for a lost one — the register `D-117` already splits at `renderer.ts:474` and its neighbours. The console is this fact's **only** observability, because an MCP client cannot see a realm.

**THE CENSUS THE FINDING IMPLIES AND DOES NOT ASK FOR — SIX MORE DISCARDED ANSWERS, ALL ROUTED.** `:2575`/`:2649`/`:2669` discard `commitDrag`/`commitPane`/`clearDrag`'s `ViewWriteStatement` at all three drag routes (**that is `F10`'s class**, and it belongs to `store-view-record`); `:1082` discards a whole `handleRequest` rejection by consuming one arm only; and `:1088`/`:1093` drop the `themeApplication.commit()`/`overlayApplication.drive()` readings at the notify turn. **The contrast is why the fix is cheap**: the four `void client.read()/fill().then(ok, err)` sites and the ghost's `dataRoute('read').then(ok, err)` **consume both arms**, which is the idiom this seam joins.

**AND THE ROW NOTHING HAS: A REFUSED CLOSE IS UNMEASURED.** No existing row drives it — `OV-1`(4), `OV-7` and `OV-14`(c) exercise the in-flight window over a crossing that **answers nothing**, so they stand as written and **would not have caught `F6`**. **`RS-6` must be added**: a close whose answer is `refused` clears the transient and leaves the store's word, and a superseded answer does not clear a newer act's.

**THE GATE, AND THIS ROW IS IT.** Nothing in `src/` has moved. **This row registers the design**, so `renderer-wiring`'s L4 may land the five hunks — the sink's returned answer, the widened `OverlayPaneCrossing.write`, the act's kept promise and ordinal, `settle`'s two registers and its `renderTurn` reuse, and the transient/seam docblocks — and the battery pass adds **`RS-6`**. **One row is routed**: `OV-13`(3)'s phrase *"cleared by the delivery"* is stale once a refusal also clears, and that assertion row is **`chrome`'s**.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-165`'S** — nothing in this row moves a byte; its product is three design pages at `150`/`150`, `150`/`150` and `150`/`150` (revs 14, 13, 10).

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-165`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a finding whose fix was blocked by an omission rather than an owner, a seam that is the member's own promise rather than a new mechanism, six more discarded answers named for routing, and the row that would have caught the defect and does not exist yet.**

## D-167 — `F6` LANDS AND THE `closing` TRANSIENT IS NO LONGER CLEARED BY A DELIVERY ALONE: the answer is kept by ordinal, a refusal and a loss both clear through the ONE existing site, a `void` crossing still settles nothing — and the L4 pass **corrected the brief rather than the design**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-166`'s five hunks, landed in `src/renderer/renderer.ts` alone, with `RS-6` added by the pass that owns it (`D-3`).

**WHAT LANDED.** The sink **returns** the member's answer (`write: (open) => bridge?.security?.setPane(open)`) instead of `void`-ing it; `OverlayPaneCrossing.write` declares **`Promise<unknown> | void`**; the act **bumps an ordinal**, keeps the answer and hands it to **`settle(ordinal, answer)`**. `settle` returns at once for a **stale ordinal**; reads a **thenable**'s `status` **structurally** — `committed` → nothing (the delivery clears, as before), `refused` → **`console.error`** and clear, **any other status** → the lost arm; a **rejection** is the lost arm (**`console.warn`**) and no rejection is left unhandled. **BOTH CLEARING ARMS REUSE `renderTurn(true)` — there is no fourth clearing site** (`transient = ` twice, `transient = null` once) — and **`derived` still has exactly one assignment**, so a refused close leaves **the store's word**: the pane is up and the wiring says so, `D-125`'s render predicate untouched and `D-82` clause 4 holding, because the write was the external cause and the refusal is its answer.

**AND THE IMPLEMENTER CAUGHT A CONTRADICTION IN THE BRIEF, WHICH IS THE LAYER SEPARATION WORKING.** The brief's hunk 4 called a **non-thenable** ("`undefined`, a non-thenable, or a rejection") a **lost answer**, and its hunk 1 called the absent bridge's `undefined` the same — **which contradicts the design's own §4**: *"a `void` `write` … hands back no thenable, so the DELIVERY stays the only clearer, and `OV-1`(4), `OV-7`, `OV-14`(c) stand untouched."* **Implementing the brief literally would have cleared the transient synchronously inside the act and redded the very rows the design predicts green.** The L4 **followed the design over the brief and reported the contradiction** rather than adjusting a test, which is exactly the behaviour the seat's own instruction asks for and the first time in this series that a brief rather than a landing was the thing at fault.

**`RS-6` IS THE ROW NOTHING HAD, AND IT IS NOW GATING.** Five clauses plus a sixth arm: **(1)** a refused close **clears `closing`** and leaves the store's word — `state()` reads `open`, the clearing is proved by the carrier mirror rather than assumed, `derived` unmoved, `inert` still on the root; **(2)** a **superseded** answer settles nothing, with the earlier act's refusal resolved **last**; **(3)** a **lost** answer clears by the same path — a rejection, a `{status:'pending'}` thenable, and a thenable with no `status`; **(4)** a **non-thenable settles nothing** — `undefined`, `null` and a bare `{status:'refused'}` object — so the delivery stays the only clearer, **asserted explicitly so a future "simplification" reds**; **(4b)** a `committed` answer settles nothing until the delivery; **(5)** the two registers — one `console.error` per refusal carrying its `reason` and `message`, one `console.warn` per loss, with a census proving no arm writes the other's channel. **EVERY CLAUSE WAS PROVED ABLE TO RED** on a throwaway copy of `renderer.ts`, restoring it byte-identically and re-verifying its digest after every run — deleting the refused arm's clear, the ordinal guard, `settleLost`'s clear, the null/`then` guards, the `committed` arm, and the register itself, each with only `RS-6` moving. **And it is the tree's FIRST console assertion**, with the spy restored in a `try/finally` and the restore **measured** (`isMockFunction` false on both members afterwards) rather than assumed.

**THE CENSUS THE FINDING IMPLIED STAYS ROUTED, WITH ITS CONTRAST NAMED.** Six more discarded answers are recorded for their owners: the **three drag routes** discarding `ViewWriteStatement` (**`F10`'s class**, `store-view-record`'s), `:1082` consuming **one arm** of a `handleRequest` so a rejection is lost whole, and the notify turn dropping `themeApplication.commit()`/`overlayApplication.drive()`'s readings. **The idiom this seam joined is already the majority** — the four `read`/`fill` sites and the ghost's `dataRoute('read')` consume both arms.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD.** `npm test` **`2,951 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,953`** over **`142`** files, **casualty-free** (`D-165`); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **exit `0`** at **`342` gating sites in `45` files** (`341`/`45` at `D-164` — `RS-6`, one site, no new file); the demo bundle rebuilt to **39 inputs**.

**`pending.md` ROW `1` NARROWS AGAIN: SIX OF ELEVEN, THEN FIVE, NOW FOUR.** `F6` **closes**; what remains is **`F3`'s second-boot arm** (routed, not closable here), and the three **deletions** — **`F8`** (five members with no caller, *and a docblock claiming a caller that does not exist*), **`F10`** (`writeOutcome()` with no reader) and **`F11`** (`#gutter-pane`'s authored `size`/`min`/`max`). The row is re-grained to say four.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-166`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a transient that is no longer a delivery's to clear alone, a refusal and a loss both settled through one existing site, a brief corrected by the layer that read the design, and a gating row with six arms each proved able to fail — including the tree's first assertion about what the console says.**

## D-169 — `F8` LANDS AND THE SURFACE LOSES FOUR MEMBERS THAT WERE **NEVER WIRED AT ALL**: `renderZone` and `candidatesFor` have **NO SUCCESSOR** because no zone layout and no candidate production exist anywhere in this tree, `defaultSizeFor` and `rightClick` were already covered by another seam, and four orphans went with them

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-168`'s census and `renderer-wiring`'s design, landed in `src/renderer/renderer.ts`, with its battery re-grained and four rows retired.

## D-170 — `F10` CLOSES BY **GIVING THE RECEIPT A READER**, NOT BY DELETING IT: the row said "delete", the measurement said the member is the only instrument for `C-6`'s property while three routes discard their statements — so the user took the fork and the wiring now reports both a write that went NOWHERE and a receipt that refused

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim, on the fork put to it):** *"Give the three routes a reader"* — chosen against `pending.md` row `1`'s own prescription that all three of `F8`/`F10`/`F11` are deletions.

**THE ROW'S PRESCRIPTION DID NOT SURVIVE THE MEASUREMENT, AND THE MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN BEFORE ANY CODE MOVED.** `F10` says *"`writeOutcome()` with no reader … all three are DELETIONS"*. Measured: **the member has no `src/` reader, but TWO GATING ROWS MEASURE IT** — `C-6` *"A REFUSED WRITE IS A READING, NOT A SILENT NO-OP"* reads `status: 'refused'`, `reason`, `message` and `route`, and `C-5` reads the sent-then-receipt half **three times**. **And the defect the census actually found is a DISCARD, not a member**: the three drag routes threw their `ViewWriteStatement` away outright (`:2621`, `:2696`, `:2718`), which `D-167` had already routed as the same class as `F6`. **So deleting the member would have removed the recipient and left the discards** — confirming the class while retiring `C-6`'s whole subject and `C-5`'s receipt half. **The fork was put to the user rather than taken by this seat**, which is `D-1`'s rule and the third time in this series that a queue row's prescription failed its own measurement.

**WHAT LANDED, AND THE TWO HALVES ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND.** **The synchronous half**: one private, total **`reportUnreached(what, statement)`** — a `{status:'absent'}` statement is a write that went **NOWHERE** → **`console.warn`** with its `reason` (`no-view-member` / `no-route`) **verbatim**; a `sent` statement, a non-statement, or anything else says **nothing**. Called at the three routes as *"the drag move"*, *"the pane commit"* and *"the drag clear"*. **And a null `view` reports ONCE at construction** — *"the pane drag has NO view client — this composition's writes reach no crossing (said ONCE here; the three per-turn statements stay silent while this stands)"* — because **a per-move repetition at pointer frequency is noise and a "last reported" flag is exactly the copy `D-129` forbids**. **The asynchronous half**: **`onWriteOutcome(handler)`**, a push beside the getter, published from **both** of `send`'s existing continuations — `lastWrite` assigned first, then each handler called on a **copy** of the array and each call **contained** in its own `try/catch`, so a throwing handler loses only its own report. The wiring registers **once** inside `createPaneDrag` and its `reportReceipt` maps **`refused` → `console.error`** (with `reason`/`message`), **`unread` → `console.warn`**, **`committed` → silence**, **scoped to the `pane` and `drag` route words** because the other two belong to their senders.

**THE SHARPEST FACT, AND THE REASON THE GETTER ALONE WAS NEVER ENOUGH.** **`send` records nothing for `absent`** — a write that went nowhere has no route behind it, so **a getter-only reader structurally cannot see it**. That is why the pass needed *both* halves, and why `C-5`/`C-6` reading the getter was never going to close `F10`: they measure the receipt's **state**, and the defect was the **event** having no listener.

**THE REGISTER'S DISCRIMINATOR, TAKEN FROM THE FILE'S OWN SITES.** **`console.error` = a fault this tree owns** (an answer that said no; a rejection where the route answers values by contract); **`console.warn` = a degradation the realm declares, or a boundary that did not speak**. **So `no-route` is a WARN and not an error** — `C-9`(b) calls that realm *an older preload*, which is lawful rather than defective, and a pass that reported it as a fault would be inventing one.

**THE ROWS, AND EVERY CLAUSE PROVED ABLE TO RED.** **`C-12`** (new, gating, `client.test.ts` 10 → 11): the handler is handed **the same object** the getter then answers, once per write, on both the `committed` and `refused` arms; **a throwing handler breaks neither the write path nor the handler behind it**; the withdrawal is **idempotent** and ends the event while the **state** stands; and **`send` publishes nothing for `absent`** on both reasons, with the getter answering the **older** receipt — the blindness stated as a row. **`PS-5`** (new, gating): the three routes warn with `reason=no-route` verbatim and **zero errors**, a `sent` double warns nothing, and a null `view` warns **exactly once** at construction with the three turns silent. **`PS-6`** (new, gating): `refused` → one error, `committed` → none, `unread` → warnings; **`zone` and `theme` refusals produce zero lines although both routes were handed and answered**, while the same refusal on `pane` produces one; and **five writes produce five lines**, so a doubled or per-turn register reads ten. **Sixteen mutations across throwaway copies red each clause it targets** — including reinstating the discards, a fixed `what`, a redacted reason, removing the route-word scope, and never taking the registration — with both sources restored byte-identically and their digests re-verified after every run. **`C-5`, `C-6` and `C-11` are BYTE-IDENTICAL** (`git diff` `+154/−0`): the member is unchanged.

## D-173 — THE CASUALTY'S INSTRUMENT CANNOT DIAGNOSE ITS OWN FAILURES: stderr is piped and then DROPPED, the child's exit code and signal are computed and swallowed by the SDK, `-32000` means only *"the stdio ended"* — and the evidenced cause is a **54 ms `dist/` window** the corpus had already measured, with the boot lock taken AFTER the check that the window invalidates

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** an L0 research pass over `D-165`'s and `D-172`'s readings. **It ran no experiments — the seat had no shell — and what it settled by reading the instrument is more than a re-run would have.**

**FIRST: `D-172`'S OWN CENSUS WAS WRONG, AND THIS ROW CORRECTS IT.** That row said *"three casualties at once"* and read all three as boot failures. **`bundle-boot-seam`'s `A-4` is `tests/integration/bundle-boot-seam/arrangement.test.ts:248`, a READ-ONLY row that spawns NOTHING.** So the run carried **two boot transport-closes and one artifact race** — and `D-172`'s inference that the class *"scales with the number of booting e2e files"* is **underdetermined**, because it fits CPU contention and a `dist/` TOCTOU equally and `A-4` fits neither as a boot. Rows are not reworded (`D-46`); this paragraph is its correction.

**THE INSTRUMENT IS BLIND, AND THAT IS WHY THE CAUSE WAS NEVER FOUND — THREE MECHANISMS, EACH MEASURED.** **(i)** **stderr IS piped and accumulated** (`stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe']` plus `child.stderr.on('data')` into a trace, in all four booting files) — **and then dropped on the connect path**: each battery does `reap(); releaseBootLock(); throw error`, rethrowing the raw SDK error with the trace discarded. **No casualty in the whole census could ever have carried a tail.** **(ii)** **The child's exit code and signal ARE computed and then swallowed by the SDK**: `ChildStdioTransport` builds `child exited (code X, signal Y)` and calls `transport.onerror`; `Protocol.connect` re-wraps that handler into its own `_onerror → this.onerror?.()`, and `new Client({name, version})` passes **no `onerror`** — so it is a no-op, and the row instead reports `_onclose()`'s synthetic **`McpError(-32000, 'Connection closed')`**. **(iii) So `-32000` cannot distinguish an OOM `SIGKILL` from an `exit 1` on a missing bundle** — the two hypotheses the census has been unable to separate since `D-165`.

**THE EVIDENCED CANDIDATE, AND THE CORPUS HAD ALREADY MEASURED IT IN ITS OWN BATTERY.** `npm run build` runs `npm run clean` first (`rmSync('dist')`), and **three in-suite files run it**: `boot-contract.test.ts` **unconditionally in `beforeAll`**, `arrangement.test.ts` and `emission.test.ts` conditionally. **`arrangement.test.ts:90–105` measures that window: `dist/main/` absent for ~`54 ms`, rewritten over `240–500 ms`, and reproduces `A-4` red 2 of 4 runs at a `+250 ms` offset.** **A boot whose Electron reads `main.mjs` or `index.html` inside that 54 ms dies at load, its stdout ends, and the transport closes** — and the renderer leg inside one explains the single `ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` on a `dist/renderer/index.html` that was *"present before and after the run"*, **which is exactly right because the hole is 54 ms**. **AND THE WINDOW IS ENTERED BY CONSTRUCTION**: the boot lock is taken **after** the artifact check (`await artifactsWithin(); const releaseBootLock = await acquireLiveBoot(…)`), so the *"artifacts are here"* measurement is **stale by the whole lock-queue wait**, whose bound is `120 s`. **More booting files ⇒ longer queue ⇒ staler check ⇒ higher failure rate; alone ⇒ no queue and no builder ⇒ green.** That is a mechanism, not a correlation.

**THE HOST IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT, WHICH IS WHY NO OOM CLAIM MAY BE MADE WITHOUT THE CHILD'S OWN SIGNAL.** 24 logical CPUs (23 fork workers available), 62.4 GiB total with 28.1 GiB available, **swap 0**, memory PSI `avg10=0.00` at rest, 235,171 processes and 1,048,576 open files against no rlimit cost. **So the concurrency cost is CPU noise, not exhaustion** — and since the harness cannot print a signal, an OOM verdict would be an inference dressed as a measurement.

**THE FIX SHAPE RECOMMENDED AND NOT IMPLEMENTED, IN ORDER.** **(i) INSTRUMENT FIRST** — set `transport.onerror` **before** `client.connect` so the SDK's wrapper preserves it, record the child's `close` `{code, signal}`, and attach the trace's tail to the connect-path throw: **~five lines across four files and zero product bytes**, and it is the prerequisite for any verdict rather than a nicety. **(ii) REMOVE THE WINDOW, NOT ITS SYMPTOM** — move `artifactsWithin()` **inside** the lock immediately before `spawn` (a two-line reorder, three times), and either drop `boot-contract`'s unconditional build to the conditional form its two siblings already use, or give the three builders **one shared build lock**. Its cost: one build's `240–500 ms` serialised against boots. **REJECTED, each with its reason**: `--no-file-parallelism`/`maxWorkers=1`, which serialises all `144` files to close a `54 ms` hole; `maxWorkers=8`, which lowers a probability and changes nothing; a **blanket retry-once**, which hides a genuine boot defect — though a retry gated on a **recorded** first failure that is a *named absence* or a *transport close* is principled, as `arrangement.test.ts:141–147` shows (`3/4` red → `0/4`); and **merging the four files**, which loses per-file bounds, teardown attribution and `D-74`'s proof while the boots would still race the builders.

**AND `brief.md` §6'S CLAIM MUST CHANGE AGAIN, BECAUSE `D-165` RE-WORDED IT TO A LUCKIER CLAIM RATHER THAN A TRUE ONE.** *"No failures on a casualty-free run"* still reads the class as chance, and it is not: **a green is now defined as a run whose `dist/` was not rebuilt concurrently with a boot**, and **every red must name the child's exit code and signal and its stderr tail** — which today the harness structurally cannot, so the first item is the one that makes the other two possible.

**WHAT WAS NOT MEASURED, STATED BECAUSE THE SEAT COULD NOT MEASURE IT.** No casualty rate and no per-run row set; **no live exit code, signal or stderr tail**; no `dmesg`; no `/dev/shm` size or inotify limits; and **no proof that a build window actually overlaps a boot in a real run** — the candidate is evidenced by the battery's own reproduction and by the lock's placement, not by a captured overlap.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-172`'S** — this row moves no byte and changes no count; its product is a measurement of the instrument and a corrected census.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-172`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records an instrument that drops the very tail it collects, an SDK that swallows the exit code it is handed, a `54 ms` window the corpus had already measured and three in-suite builders that open it, a lock taken after the check that window invalidates, and its own predecessor's census corrected.**

## D-176 — THE APPLICATION'S INTERFACE IS SPECIFIED: a top-bar with the tabs row between a logo placeholder and window controls, four fixed zones that scroll internally, and a stage driven by the active tab — and the measurement says **five of those pieces do not exist**, two of them because this pass deleted them

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim, one message):**

> *Zones - top, bottom, left, right - all scroll internally and have fixed placement in window*
> *top-zone - top of zone is flush with bottom of app top-bar, zone spans full width of app*
> *bottom-zone - bottom of zone is flush with bottom side of window, zone spans full width of app*
> *left/right - sidebars fixed to left/right side of window, stretching vertically between top and bottom zones.*
> *Stage - the otherwise unoccupied area in the middle between the zones, to be used for containing application data based on the current active tab information. Also scrolls internally"*

**THE DESIGN IS THE AUTHORITY AND THIS PARAGRAPH IS ITS ONLY RECORD.** Nothing in the corpus described an interface like this before it; a census of `strata/`, `docs/`, the handover and all `1,194` commits found **no earlier UI request**, which is why this row quotes the user rather than paraphrasing — a design that exists only in a conversation is the class this corpus keeps losing.

**WHAT THE TREE HAS, MEASURED AGAINST EACH ELEMENT.** **The envelope is ONE root node** (`APP_ROOT_ID = 'app-surface'`, `demo-envelope.ts:306`/`:430`) carrying five cards — counter, echo, gutter, theme, overlay — and **there is no top-bar, no zone, and no stage**: the layout the design describes **does not exist in any form**. Specifics: **`['zones']` exists as DATA** at `mem`, closed to **ONE** declared id (`DECLARED_ZONE_IDS`, `D-151`) with `slot`/`distance`/`size`/`display`, and **no renderer at all** — `renderZone` was **deleted at `D-169`** because nothing rendered zones; **the tab record is the tabs row's data** and it is live (`order` plus rows carrying `target`/`active`, rebuilt at `D-157`/`D-159` — one delete, one row write, membership and activeness repaired by different bodies); **the stage's source exists** as the active row's `target`; and **there are NO window controls anywhere** — no `minimize`/`maximize`/`close`, no `frame`, no `titleBarStyle`, so the OS draws the native frame today.

**SO FIVE PIECES ARE NEW AND TWO ARE NEWLY ABSENT.** New: the **top-bar**, its **logo/name placeholder**, the **tabs row** as an authored binding to `['tabs']`, the **four zone nodes**, and the **stage**. Newly absent: a **zone renderer** (deleted at `D-169` as dead surface — this design gives it a subject again) and **any window-control surface** (never existed).

**FOUR THINGS THE DESIGN RAISES THAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, AND ONE OF THEM IS A MAIN-PROCESS FORK.** **(i) THE WINDOW CONTROLS.** *"In the same placement used for windows or KDE apps"* with the tabs row **between** the logo and the buttons places authored content **inside the title-bar region** — which today belongs to the OS. That needs a custom title bar (`frame: false`, or `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`), and then the three buttons are either **authored nodes calling window IPC** (consistent with the UI-authority rule, and requiring new channels) or Electron's **`titleBarOverlay`** (real native controls drawn in a reserved area — not authored, and not hand-written DOM either). **This is the design's biggest fork, it is a `main`-process decision, and no row covers it.** **(ii) THE ZONE SET MUST GROW ONE → FOUR**, deliberately reopening the domain `D-151` closed — top, bottom, left, right — which is lawful because the design *names* them, but it must be recorded as a widening rather than discovered. **(iii) THE ZONE MEMBERS MAY GO UNUSED**: the design fixes placement in **CSS terms** (`flush with`, `spans full width`, `stretching between`), so `slot`/`distance`/`size`/`display` may carry none of it — the layout is **authored**, not data-driven, and the family's members must not be pressed into service as a second authority for geometry (`D-129`). **(iv) INTERNAL SCROLLING** is a `css` declaration on authored nodes, so it follows the envelope rather than a mechanism.

**WHY THIS IS NOT TAKEN AS A UNIT YET.** It is a **major expansion** — a whole application layout, a widened closed domain, a possible custom title bar and new IPC — and this seat's standing instruction is that a major expansion goes to **`role_l0_validity` with `role_l0_critique`** before any design work. **Its queue row is filed in `next-steps.md` and is gated on that assessment**, not on nothing.

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-175`'S** — this row moves no byte; its product is a recorded design, a measured gap, and four named forks.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-175`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records an interface specified for the first time, five pieces that do not exist and two this pass deleted, a title-bar fork that is a main-process decision, a closed zone domain that the design reopens by one, and a design whose only record is now the corpus.**

## D-177 — THE INTERFACE DESIGN IS VALID, AND IT IS **TWO UNITS WITH ONE BLOCKING FACT**: the envelope's node list is **STATIC**, so it cannot emit one node per `['tabs'].order` entry — and the tabs row is therefore a **DEPICTION, not a control**, because the only tab-switch turn is reachable from the main-process RPC and never from a click

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-176`'s design, put to `role_l0_validity` and `role_l0_critique` **before any design work** — the assessment a major expansion owes.

**THE ONE FACT THAT GOVERNS EVERYTHING ELSE: THE ENVELOPE'S NODE LIST IS STATIC.** Its node type carries `type`, an authored `content`, a **literal** `children[]`, `props`, `handlers[{name,event,body}]`, `css`, and `derived`/`hooks`; there is **no `each`, no `repeat`, no per-node binding to a store family, and no conditional**. **So the envelope CANNOT emit one node per `['tabs'].order` entry** — and the one declarative computation form, `derived: {props?, css?}`, **cannot carry `content`**. The engine *can* do it — `hooks` with `hooksKind: 'placement'` yielding a `RowsMintOp(rows)`, reachable through `runtime.applyCommand` — **and that path has ZERO callers in `src/`: every write this app makes is a `state-slice`.** So the tabs row's options are **an authored pool of k slots painted per active id, with a named cap** — or **a new command route the tree has never used**.

**AND THE TABS ROW IS A DEPICTION UNLESS THREE THINGS ARE ADDED.** The record is live and readable (`order` plus rows carrying `target`/`active`), but **`tabs-client.ts` is read-only by contract** (*"Stage A takes NO WRITE ROUTE AT ALL"*), and the renderer's only tab-writing turn (`focusActRoute`) **is reachable only from the main-process RPC switch — there is no DOM-originated turn for it**, unlike theme, which has an `attach` form. **A row that renders the order and cannot dispatch a switch is a picture of a store, not a tabs row.** Its minimum: **(a)** an `attach`-form click listener carrying the tab id, because **an authored handler body can only `apply` node props and can never reach a record**; **(b)** a render turn per delivery writing each label and the active marker, with the optional-`label` fallback named; **(c)** the **N problem `D-176` never raised**, since node ids are derived by *walking the static tree* and the one list machinery in the tree (`owned-list-host.ts`) **has no `src/` importer**, while `provident.load` would rebuild the graph and destroy the `app-surface` inert carrier.

**THE ZONES ARE STATIC AUTHORED NODES AND THE `['zones']` FAMILY IS THE WRONG HOME.** The design states geometry in **CSS terms**, and the family's `size`/`display` have had **no reader since `D-169`**; a CSS declaration and a stored figure for one dimension is **exactly `D-129`'s second authority, and `zonesMustStand` judges shape and never agreement, so no repair could reconcile them.** Widening `DECLARED_ZONE_IDS` one → four would re-grain **~19–25 collected rows over 6–7 files**, **re-open `Z-9`'s tombstone**, and mint **four records nothing reads** — the `ASM-10` argument verbatim. **So: zones are authored `css`, the domain stays closed at one id, and `D-151` is not reopened.** The same discipline is the whole defence against repeating `D-169`'s finding at five times the scale: **every new node names its reader in one line** — tabs row → the client's read; stage → `drivePageDisplay`; four zones → **nothing, so they are static and closed**; **a node whose reader cannot be written in that line is not authored.**

**THE STAGE'S DATA EXISTS AND NOTHING RESOLVES IT.** A row's `target` is *"the tab's contained content reference"*, repaired to `'tabs-landing-page'` — **a string naming an authored node id that nothing resolves**: every `elementForNodeId` call site passes a constant or role id, and `target` is read only as a seat key. The stage needs **a resolver and a paint turn**; today it renders nothing.

**THE WINDOW CONTROLS: THE AUTHORED ARM IS REFUSED, AND THE NATIVE ARM IS UNMEASURED.** Chrome is **the one place UI authority stops**, so authoring the three buttons is the deviation rather than the frame. Authoring them puts handlers in the app graph where **the default grant (`['read','dispatch']`) reaches them** — giving an agent a close control that **kills the port it speaks on** and a minimize that **hides the window and the overlay's lockout with it** — and they would stand **outside `app-surface`**, so the `inert` product that *"blocks general app access"* **would not cover them**. The harness cost of `frame: false` is **nil** (the boot battery asserts HTML and endpoints, never the frame; the one row reading the window options asserts only the *absence* of `show: false`), **but the app's only quit path is `win.on('closed')`.** And the native arm is **not** established: neither `titleBarStyle` nor `titleBarOverlay` occurs in the tree, and **nothing has shown that either draws KDE's buttons on this desktop — that must be measured before it is designed.**

**"ALL SCROLL INTERNALLY" IS A PROPERTY NOTHING THAT GATES CAN SEE.** Rendered-HTML reads see markup; the `ui` leg's real-renderer probes *could* falsify it (`overflow-y` plus `scrollHeight > clientHeight`) but **that leg sits outside the four-leg floor**, and an assertion there would run against a probe fixture — **a green measuring the fixture, not the app's zones.** So the design either adds a row to a leg that gates, or the word becomes a prose CSS decision.

**THE FIVE CARDS, `#panes` AND THE OVERLAY HAVE NO STATED HOME, AND ONE OF THEM IS LOAD-BEARING.** The five cards, the two `page`-roled terminals and `#panes` — **the isolated operator graph, the subject of `npm run panes` 7/7 and the only always-visible route to security settings** — are all unmentioned. **`#gutter-*` is the subject of `['panes']`, `['drag']`, `panesMustStand`, the gating `renderer-wiring` rows, the 115-row compliance battery and the demo bundle**: if the cards are evicted the app loses its only demonstrable behaviour. **And fixed placement does not kill the resize** — the drag writes a node id, never a measured box — **but a fixed zone owning the stage's scroll box changes the pane's pixel geometry while every drag row stays green, which is a green that means less.**

**THE COST, IN CORPUS UNITS: TWO TO THREE UNITS**, each with a ten-to-twelve-step walkthrough — ~14 new authored nodes and five re-parented, two new wiring turns, a `main`-process decision, and for the zones-as-data arm alone ~19–25 rows re-grained. **THE VALIDITY PASS'S CUTS: authored window controls (native frame until KDE is measured), the zone-domain widening, the scrolling property as a contract, and the logo as a *node*. THE REFUSALS: the five cards' re-home *with* the gutter's subject and its rows, the tabs switch act, the overlay's `inert` scope covering the new chrome, and a named empty/full tab arm.**

**WHY THIS ROW IS NOT A DESIGN.** It records an assessment and four user questions; **no design work has begun and none may until those are settled** — the envelope's static node list, the tab-switch route and the frame decision each change what the design *is*, not how it is written.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-176`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a design found valid and two units large, a static node list that blocks the design's load-bearing element, a tabs row that would otherwise depict a store instead of switching it, a refused authoring arm that would hand an agent the window's own close control, and four pieces of the design with no home at all.**
