## D-195 — `app-shell`'S L3 LANDS AND HITS ONE BLOCKER WITH A CLEAN RESOLUTION: **`X-5` BANS `Menu`/`setApplicationMenu` IN `src/**`** WHILE `S-10` REQUIRES THE CALL — and the row's subject is a menu being **AUTHORED**, which `setApplicationMenu(null)` is not

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `app-shell`'s L3 pass (`docs/L3/app-shell/design.md` **rev 5, 149 lines**; `docs/L3/app-shell/signatures.md` **created, rev 1, 93 lines**) and a reading of `tests/menu-template.test.ts`'s `X-5`.

**THE BLOCKER, MEASURED.** `X-5` is a **`src/**`-wide census** whose claim is *"`src/**` contains NO menu, picker, dialog or accelerator surface"* — six specs, one named exemption (`dialog` in `demo-envelope.ts`, granted at `D-113`). **The design requires `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)` in `src/main/main.ts`** (`D-181`: the native menu must go, because a pane now *contains* the menus). **That call reds `X-5` on two specs at once — `Menu` and `setApplicationMenu` — so `S-10` cannot land green.**

**AND THE RESOLUTION IS THE ROW'S OWN SUBJECT RATHER THAN A NEGOTIATION.** `X-5` exists to keep **a menu surface out of `src/`** — it is the row that says *this app does not author a menubar*. **`setApplicationMenu(null)` authors nothing; it REMOVES.** So the exemption is **the null form, by name and by shape**: **`main.ts` may import `Menu` and call `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)` exactly once, and the ban on `MenuItem`, on `picker`, on `'darwin'` and on a NON-NULL `setApplicationMenu` stands unmoved.** **`chrome` owes that re-grain** (the row is `tests/menu-template.test.ts`'s), and it is the same shape as `D-113`'s `dialog` exemption — a named path gaining a named token with the reason stated, and the controls proving both halves.

**THE PASS ALSO CORRECTED L2'S WORD, WHICH IS THE KIND OF THING THAT BECOMES A BUG.** The route answers **`admitted`, not `applied`**: **no arm executes a role**, so a click on `Copy` admits and changes nothing. **`applied` would have claimed an execution nothing performs**, and the L2 page said `applied`. **That is `OWED-1` in the pass's own list — what an admitted role actually DOES — and it is a real gap**: the route delivers the role to `main` and **`main` admits it without acting**, because the acting is Chromium's own menu machinery which has just been removed. **A role that is admitted and not executed is a receipt, not an action** — and the page now says so.

**THE COST IS USER-VISIBLE AND IS STATED AS SUCH.** `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)` takes **ten accelerators** with it — `Ctrl+Q`, `Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+R`, `Shift+Ctrl+R`, `Ctrl+Shift+I`, `Ctrl+M`, `Ctrl+0`, `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+−`, `F11` — **none re-bound**, and **a click is not a shortcut**: the pane's items restore none of them. **So `Ctrl+Q` does nothing, `Ctrl+R` cannot rescue a stuck renderer, and `F11` cannot fullscreen.** Only the edit keys survive, as Chromium content behaviour. **That is a consequence the design accepts, and the page does not bury it.**

**THE CENSUS MOVES `9 → 10` MEMBERS, IN THREE ROWS THAT ARE NOT THIS MODULE'S** — `ISO-4` twice (`tests/integration/…/isolation.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/…/isolation.test.ts`) and `S-11` (`tests/e2e/settings-carrier-retirement/scenarios.test.ts`), **all three in `operator-settings`' files, and two of them GATE**. **Two more rows were believed to measure the same census — `RET-4` and `tests/secure-exclusion.test.ts`'s census-with-control — and MEASURED THEY DO NOT: they count the TWO `storeChannels` constants (and the preload `security` member's five routes), not the nine bridge members. CORRECTED AT `D-197`, where their real obligation is named.**

**AND ONE PRECONDITION IS A DECLARATION RATHER THAN A DEFECT**: the newly created `docs/L3/app-shell/signatures.md` **reds `B-1` by name** until a `DECLARED_SCOPE` entry carries it — the same discipline `D-146` established, owed in the same edit that created the page.

**EIGHT OWEDs, AND FOUR ARE NOT THIS MODULE'S**: **what an admitted role does** (`OWED-1`, L1/user — the receipt-not-action gap above); **L2's `applied` word** (`OWED-2`); **`secure-panels.ts`'s `declare global` copy** (`OWED-3`); **`AL-7`'s carrier clause is the CLICK path's, not `provident.dispatch`'s** (`OWED-4`, L1 — `D-193` had already measured it unproducible); **the overlay's unthemed palette** (`OWED-5`, the user); **`X-5`'s re-grain** (`OWED-6`, `chrome`); **the `AS-1`…`AS-4` rows' home** (`OWED-7`, L1); **the gating census rows and the `DECLARED_SCOPE` entry** (`OWED-8`, other owners).

**FOUR FALSEHOODS WERE FOUND, THREE OF THEM OTHER PAGES'.** L1's debt 5 claims *"its SCAN widened"* — **measured unnecessary**: the scan already picks `menu` up, and **the debt's named owner, `settings-carrier-retirement`, names no map row**. L2 §5 says *"the role it **applied**"* (nothing applies one) and §7 says *"these **nine** rows"* against L1's eleven. And `preload.ts`'s `store` headstones say *"ONE constant"* while reading **two** — stale commentary over a live count.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-194`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a census that bans the very call the design needs and the reading that resolves it without weakening the ban, a route that admits rather than acts, ten shortcusts a user will feel missing, and a declaration owed in the same edit that created the page needing it.**

## D-196 — AN ADMITTED MENU ROLE **EXECUTES**: `main` maps the eleven to their `webContents`/`window` equivalents, the **focus rule** is named as a mechanism, and the seven stay refused regardless of how the click arrived

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, on `OWED-1`):** *"Execute them, with the focus rule"*.

**THE GAP THIS CLOSES.** The route answered **`admitted`** and **performed nothing** — because the thing that *did* the work was the native menu, and `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)` removed the **implementation** with the **surface**. **So the pane replaced the menu's surface and not its machinery**: eighteen items rendered, responded and reported, and no click did anything. **The ruling makes `admitted` mean what its name says.**

**THE ELEVEN, AND EACH ONE'S OPERATION — ALL ON APIS ALREADY IN PLAY.** `undo` `redo` `cut` `copy` `paste` `delete` `selectall` → **`webContents.<the same name>()`**; `resetzoom` → **`setZoomLevel(0)`**; `zoomin` `zoomout` → **`setZoomLevel(getZoomLevel() ± 0.5)`**, the half-step being **Chromium's own default for these roles** rather than a figure invented here; `togglefullscreen` → **`setFullScreen(!isFullScreen())`**, a toggle despite the name.

**AND THE FOCUS RULE IS A MECHANISM, NOT A CAVEAT — WITHOUT IT THE SEVEN EDIT ROLES EXECUTE AGAINST NOTHING** (**CORRECTED AT `D-207`: this row said "six of the eleven" and its own list of edit roles is SEVEN** — `undo` `redo` `cut` `copy` `paste` `delete` `selectall`). `webContents.copy()` and its siblings **act on the FOCUSED element**, and **clicking an authored `<div>` moves focus to that div first**. A native menu never has this problem because it lives **outside the document**. **So `startMenusItems` attaches a `mousedown` listener that calls `preventDefault()`** — which stops focus from moving while leaving the `click` to fire on mouseup — **and only then does the role execute, against the element the user was actually in.** **State it as the design's own rule: a menu item is a control that must not take focus, and the mechanism is `preventDefault` on `mousedown` beside the `click`.**

**THE SECURITY POSITION IS UNCHANGED, AND THE RULING DOES NOT WEAKEN IT.** `provident.dispatch` **synthesizes clicks on authored ids** — verified from the tool's own contract — so **every admitted role is agent-reachable**, and **the guard has always been `main`'s admitted set rather than the absence of a path.** **The seven stay refused in `main`, tested before any other arm**, so `quit`, `close`, `reload`, `forcereload`, `toggledevtools`, `minimize` and `zoom` (the Window role) remain unreachable **however the click arrived**.

**WHAT IT COSTS, STATED BECAUSE THE EXECUTION CHANGES WHAT AN AGENT CAN DO.** With execution, **an agent that synthesizes a click on `zoomin` or `togglefullscreen` changes the app's magnification or enters fullscreen** — both reversible, neither ending a session, and both within the admitted set the corpus drew on purpose. **That is the price of a working menubar and it is accepted:** the alternative was a receipt that reported a role nothing performed, which is the shape this corpus calls a row that cannot fail.

**WHAT THE DESIGN MUST NOW SAY, AND WHERE.** `app-shell`'s route **performs the operation after admitting** and answers **`admitted` only on success** — a throwing operation is a **failure answer**, not an admission. `renderer-wiring`'s `startMenusItems` gains the **`mousedown` `preventDefault`** beside its click. And the receipt carrier receives **what was done**, so the pane's own display can say it. **`AL-7` is therefore a real battery row at last**: eleven receipts through the real IPC **with an observable effect**, then seven refusals by name, **and the row dies if a refused role reaches the window**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-195`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a route that admits rather than acts and is made to act, a focus rule without which six roles act on nothing, a half-step derived from the platform rather than chosen, and an agent surface widened by exactly the amount the corpus had already decided was acceptable.**

## D-198 — `S-1` LANDS IN `src/` AND **NO ROW MOVES**: `applyCommand` resolves a string `target` by mirroring the `node` arm's own shape — and the only reds were the two artifacts a dirty tree produces

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-179`'s measurement (*"a mint's `target` must be a live Node OBJECT, and `applyCommand` never resolves one — so no JSON or IPC caller can mint"*), implemented as `docs/L1/app-layout.md`'s **`S-1`**.

**THE CHANGE, WHICH IS DELIBERATELY THE SMALLEST ONE IN THE UNIT.** `src/renderer/runtime.ts`, **`+25/−1`**, three arms added **beside their `node` twins** rather than in a new shape: **a string `target` that does not resolve is `rejected`** (never a throw); **an object `target` that is not a registered Node is `rejected`** (the existing `F5` arm's `isRegisteredNode` check); and **a resolvable string is substituted as the live Node before `supervisor.apply`**. The signature gains `target?: string`. **`node`'s arms, `source`'s, the two `mutation` guards, the compile loop, `render()`, the id-index rebuild, `resolveTarget` and the returned shape are BYTE-IDENTICAL** — and **no new status word was minted**, which is `D-191`'s clause rule: a refusal expressed as a clause on the existing token, never as a ninth.

**AND NO ROW MOVED, WHICH IS THE DESIGN'S OWN PREDICTION CONFIRMED RATHER THAN A LUCKY GREEN.** There is **no `src/**` or `tests/**` caller that passes a `target`** to `applyCommand` today — the minting turn is `S-4`'s and does not exist yet — so **the arms are unreachable from the tree at this head**. The only reds in the intermediate run were **the two artifacts a dirty tree always produces**: `DB-1`/`DB-2` on a bundle whose input hashes include `runtime.ts` (`D-118`), and `B-1` by construction. **The bundle was rebuilt and the commit taken; the full suite reads `2,946 passed / 2 skipped of 2,948` — the same figures as `D-175`, because nothing this pass touched had a row.** `typecheck` **0**, `typecheck:tests` **0**, `build` **0**, `marks` **0**.

**ONE CONTRADICTION IS OWED ITS PAGE, AND IT IS THE SORT THAT MATTERS.** `docs/L2/producing-runtime/interface.md` **rev 1 §3 states *"NO OBJECT-`target` GATE IS ADDED"*** — and **the implementation lands one**, on the brief's explicit instruction, because **an object `target` that is not a live Node would reach the engine and throw on `.clone()`**. **The tree is right and the page is wrong**: the object arm is exactly `F5`'s own reasoning, applied to the second member. **The page's re-grain is owed to its owner** (`D-46`: superseded by pointer, never silently reworded).

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-197`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a change that mirrors an existing arm rather than inventing one, a refusal expressed as a clause and not a new word, a green predicted before it was taken, and a page left saying the opposite of the tree it describes.**

## D-199 — `S-2` LANDS THE 72-NODE TREE, AND THE PASS LEAVES `S-4` ONE BLOCKER: **THE PROTOTYPE REFERENCES A COMPONENT WITH NO PROVIDER**, so the mint will reject with `rows-prototype-unresolved` unless the def is made real

**THE TREE, COUNTED INDEPENDENTLY RATHER THAN TRUSTED.** The design page said `72`; the pass **walked `demoEnvelope()` itself** and got the same: **root `1` + `app-surface` `59`** (itself `1` + top-bar `2` + top zone `26` + arrangement `28` + bottom `1` + opener `1`) **+ the overlay layer `11` + the row prototype `1`**. **A figure confirmed by a second measurement is a reading; the same figure twice from the same source is a hope** — so the pass's own walk is what the row records.

**WHAT LANDED, AND THE TWO PLACES IT HAD TO BE EXACT.** **The overlay's opener stays the ROOT'S LAST CHILD with the layer as its FOLLOWING SIBLING** — anything authored inside the root goes `inert` under the modal, so the scrim must remain a sibling (`D-178`). **And the drag region is three declarations and one deliberate absence**: the top-bar `-webkit-app-region: drag` with the measured `36px` strip, **the tabs row `no-drag` with `width: env(titlebar-area-width, 100%)`** — measured at `D-193` to resolve to `607px` — and **the controls' strip authored as NOTHING**, because the platform owns its region.

**THE BATTERY MOVED AS `D-193` PREDICTED, AND ONE ROW WAS STRENGTHENED RATHER THAN REPAIRED.** `INTERFACE_INVENTORY_NODE_DELTA = 34` is now a **named term**, and the census reads **`18 + 5 + 2 + 13 + 34 = 72`** — **a sum of named parts, never a bare figure** — across `M-2`, `X-1`, `I-10` and `P-TC-IM-2`, **the last of which gained a residue check at `0` rather than merely a new total**. `OV-6`'s literal follows the rename **with its subject intact** (the same handle node, a truer name). **And a deep-path row that silently landed on the top zone was re-pointed to `counter-card`'s third child — the `inc` button — named node-by-node**, with **two sibling rows carrying the same arithmetic fixed identically**, because a path index is a claim about a tree and three files carried it.

## D-200 — THE PROTOTYPE IS A REAL DEF AND THE NAME RESOLVES: `unresolved-reference` is **gone**, `S-4`'s op shape answers OK — and the fallout was **a row's arithmetic**, because the census has **FOUR categories** and the fourth was always zero until now

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-199`'s blocker, closed by restoring the shape `D-179`'s spike measured, and one row re-grained on a four-term sum.

**THE NODE, AND WHY ITS TWO ADDED FIELDS ARE THE WHOLE FIX.** The prototype now carries **`props.id`** and an **inline `component.value`**:

```
{ type:'div', css:{classes:['tab-row']}, props:{id:'tab-row'},
  component:{ reference:'tab-row', value:{ type:'div', css:{classes:['tab-row']} } } }
```

**The `value` is the def that makes the name resolvable** — exactly what `D-179`'s spike carried and the design page's shape lacked — and **`props.id` makes the provider addressable**. `div`/`tab-row` rather than the spike's `li`/`tab-row`: **`tab-row` is this app's own row class**, a `div` matches the tabs row (a `div` in the bar's flex row) and the app's other authored click targets, and **`li` needs a list this app never authors**. **No `props` in the def**, because the engine's `mintRowNode` copies only `type`/`css` off the shape — an authored `props` there would be **dead data**, which is the defect this corpus spends rows on.

**AND IT WAS VERIFIED BY READING THE ENGINE'S OWN WARNINGS RATHER THAN BY HOPE.** A throwaway probe drove **`translateLegacy` + a whole-slice `compile` + the renderer's `Runtime.load`**: the as-filed shape reads **`[{code:'unresolved-reference', pathKey:'root/node-72'}]`**, the fixed tree reads **`[]`**, `defRootPrototypeFor('tab-row')` answers a **def-root**, and **`S-4`'s op shape returns OK instead of `rows-prototype-unresolved`**. **That last clause is the spike's own refusal, now not firing** — so the blocker is closed at the exact point it would have bitten.

**THE FALLOUT WAS A ROW'S ARITHMETIC, NOT THE TEARDOWN — AND THE PROBE SAYS SO WITH NUMBERS.** After teardown the census reads **`registered: 72`** while **`destroyed + unplaced + inTree = 71`**. **The census has FOUR categories, not three**: **`prototypes`**, always present and always `0` until this row, now counts **the engine's out-of-tree def-root prototype** (state `'prototype'`, `isInTree` false, therefore neither destroyed nor unplaced). **`1 + 70 + 0 + 1 = 72` closes it, and nothing else does.** **So the row's sum gained its fourth term, and the row now SAYS why** — a reader who sees a four-term sum with no explanation will eventually delete the term.

**AND THE ROW'S NEW CONTROL BITES WHERE THE OLD ARM COULD NOT.** The pass found that **`nodeState({kind:'cssId', cssId:'tab-row'})` cannot fail** — **the def-root authors no `css.id` at all**, so that arm throws structurally, whatever the teardown does. **So the bite was put in the arm the name actually occupies**: **`nodeState('tab-row')` — the props arm — RESOLVES before `teardown()` and throws after**, measured on the same graph. **The cssId arm was kept verbatim as the guard on that absence**, which is what it was always worth.

**THE TREE IS UNCHANGED IN SIZE AND THE MINT IS ARMED.** Authored census **`72 → 72`**; **`registered` `72 → 73`** and **`prototypes` `0 → 1`** — the engine's own out-of-tree node, not the app's. **`S-4` can now pass a string `target` (`S-1`) at a hook whose prototype resolves (this row)**, which is every input the mint needs.

**THE READINGS AT THIS STAGE.** `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; the demo bundle **current** at `39` inputs; the module rows **18/18** and the full suite green apart from `B-1`, which reds **by construction on the dirty tree** and clears on the commit taken with it.

## D-201 — THE MINT WORKS, AND ITS OWN MEASUREMENT REFUTES TWO RULINGS: the **label rides the datum** and needs no `state-slice`, while the **active marker FREEZES under `keyField` reuse** — so `D-191`'s "required" and `D-194`'s "one listener per row, ever" are both superseded

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `S-4`'s landing (`src/renderer/renderer.ts`, `+78/−1`) and the rendered-HTML measurement it was required to take.

**THE TURN, AND IT IS ONE TURN WITH ONE TRIGGER.** `driveTabsRows(reading, runtime)` is a private call **from `holdTabsReading`**, so its trigger is **a `['tabs']` delivery and the boot read**, **on a `'committed'` reading alone** — an `unread`/`absent` reading mints nothing (`D-127`). Its operands: `target` the tabs-row id **as a string** (resolved by `S-1`), `hookName` **the same string the envelope declares** (not re-spelled), `mintKind: 'placement'`, `prototypeName` the prototype constant, **`placementName` spelled with a comment saying it names nothing** (the engine requires it and this app authors no container — a reader must not have to rediscover that), and **`keyField: 'id'`**.

**AND THE LABEL DOES NOT NEED WHAT THE DESIGN SAID IT NEEDED.** Measured: the minted row renders

```
<div data-wire="node-147" data-node-id="node-147" id="preempt-node-node-147" class="tab-row">First</div>
```

**The engine renders a minted row's text from its FIRST SCALAR SOURCE-ANCHOR BINDING** — so **placing `label` first in the datum composes it**, and a second delivery `{status:'applied', minted:[], dirtied:['node-77']}` **re-renders the reused node as `First · renamed`**. **So the label rides the DATUM, survives `keyField` reuse from the datum, and needs NO `state-slice`, no key→id map, and no second mechanism.** **`D-194` owed (3) is ANSWERED for the label, by measurement, in the direction the design page did not predict** — and the page's turn 1 and L2's §2, which both paint the label as a `state-slice` on the minted row, **are wrong and owe a re-grain.**

**BUT THE ACTIVE MARKER IS THE OPPOSITE, AND IT IS A REAL FORK RATHER THAN A GAP.** Measured: **a plain `active` member reaches no prop**; **`props.active` reaches the attribute AT MINT and then FREEZES** — with the record's flag moved, **reused nodes still read `active="true"`/`active="false"` under two `rows-reuse-shape-ignored` warnings.** **So a marker that MOVES cannot ride the datum under keyed reuse**, and **the turn cannot write it as a `state-slice` either**, because a keyed re-mint answers **`minted: []`** and a key→id map is `D-129`'s copy. **The design's two halves cannot both hold.**

**SO TWO RULINGS ARE SUPERSEDED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE AUTHORITY.** **`D-191`'s "`keyField` REQUIRED"** and **`D-194`'s "one listener per row, EVER"** were both reasoned from **`D-182`'s id-churn measurement** — whose premise was **that a churning id is a cost because something must address the row afterwards.** **The measurement here shows the reverse trade**: **with `keyField`, the label is re-applied but the marker freezes; without it, every node is minted fresh, so the label AND the marker are correct at mint — and nothing needs to address a row afterwards if the ATTACH turn re-attaches per mint**, which it can, because the old nodes are destroyed and their listeners die with them (no leak, no map, no stale id). **So the coherent shape is: mint fresh every delivery, attach fresh beside it, and let both the label and the marker ride the datum — with `keyField` NOT declared.** **The cost is DOM churn on each tabs delivery for N tabs, which is the cheaper of the two failures and the only one that leaves the marker correct.**

**WHAT IS OWED NOW.** **`S-5` (the attach turn) must re-attach per mint rather than once ever** — one `attach` per row per delivery, dying with the node — and **`S-4`'s `keyField` operand must be removed** when that lands, **in the same edit**, or the marker stays frozen. **The design page's turn 1 and L2's §2 owe the label re-grain**, and turn 2 owes the re-attach.

**THE READINGS.** `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; **`130/130` green** across `tests/unit/renderer-wiring/`, `tests/integration/store-tabs-record/` and `tests/theme-control.test.ts` — **identical to the pre-edit baseline**, because nothing yet addresses the minted rows; the demo bundle rebuilt. **The mint itself is measured working**, which is what `S-4` owed.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-200`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a label that rides the data it describes, a marker that freezes under the mechanism chosen to keep ids stable, two rulings superseded by the measurement that tested them, and a trade stated as a trade rather than a defect.**

## D-203 — **`css.style` WRITTEN AS AN OBJECT IS A SILENT NO-OP IN THE REAL RENDERER**: the shim serialises it as JSON text that *looks* applied, the browser writes **an empty attribute**, and so **every `display` the app has ever driven has never reached the screen** — including the tabs terminals since `D-92`

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `S-6`'s paint measurement, pursued to the engine. **This row is the most consequential finding of the unit and it is not about the layout at all.**

**THE MEASUREMENT, TAKEN IN A REAL ELECTRON DOM AGAINST THE APP'S OWN `Runtime` AND A TRIVIAL ENVELOPE.** One node, two `state-slice` writes to `css.style`, the computed style read afterwards:

| write | the answer | `style` attribute after | computed `display` | computed `height` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **object** `{ display:'none', height:'40px' }` | **`applied`** | **`""` — EMPTY** | **`block`** | **`18px`** |
| **CSS text** `'display:block;height:40px'` | `applied` | `display: block; height: 40px;` | `block` | **`40px`** |

**So an OBJECT value on `css.style` reports success and writes NOTHING.** The answer is `applied`; the attribute is empty; the browser applies nothing. **CSS TEXT works.** And a bare browser confirms the shape of the failure independently: an attribute literally carrying `{"display":"none"}` computes as `display: block` — **invalid CSS is ignored whole, not partially**.

**AND THE SHIM IS WHY NOBODY EVER SAW IT.** `renderedHtml()` under the DOM shim serialises the same object value **as JSON text into the attribute** — so a row reading the shim's HTML sees `style="{"height":"40px"}"`, which **looks like a style was written**, while the real renderer leaves the attribute **empty**. **That is a divergence between the shim and the real DOM on a property the `divergence` leg does not pin** — its `N = 9` structural properties do not include `css.style`'s serialisation — **so the one leg built to catch shim/real divergence could not catch this.**

**THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IT PREDATES THIS UNIT.** `drivePageDisplay` (`src/renderer/renderer.ts:256`) writes `value: { display: shown ? 'block' : 'none' }` — **an object** — and it is the **only** thing that shows or hides the two authored tabs terminals. **So the landing page and the error page have never been shown or hidden in the running app.** The rows that measure them (`DC-*`, `T-2`/`T-3`, the witness drives) all read the shim, where the write *appears* to land — **so every one of them passes while the surface does nothing.** **`S-6`'s paint writes objects too**, so the zones' dimensions and the pane's width would have joined it.

**THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER SITE AND IT IS A SPELLING, NOT A MECHANISM.** Write **CSS text**: `display: block` / `none` for the terminal drive, and `kebab: value;` for the paint's record. **Neither changes a single operand, a guard, or a route.** **The engine's object handling is upstream-owned** (`D-5`): it accepts a record on `css.style` and then bakes it to nothing in the real adapter — **a defect with a symptom, a reproduction (this probe), a suspected root cause (`adapters.js`'s `bakeValue` path writes the object through a serializer that produces an invalid `cssText`) and a proposed fix shape (stringify to CSS text, as `translate` already does for authored records)** — **recorded, not patched.**

**AND THE BATTERY GAP IS NAMED WITH IT: NOTHING GATES A RENDERED STYLE.** Every row reads markup; a style that is written-but-inert is invisible to all of them. **So this row asks for the one thing the corpus does not have — a row that reads a COMPUTED style rather than a serialised one** — and it belongs on a leg that gates (`D-37` puts the real-DOM leg outside the four-leg floor, which is why this survived).

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-202`'S** — this row moves no byte; its product is the measurement, the two sites, and the gap.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-202`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a write that reports success and does nothing, a shim that made it look like it worked, a leg that could not see the divergence, and every terminal the app has ever hidden on a screen where it was never hidden.**

## D-205 — THE ACTIVE MARKER IS DISCHARGED WITH **NO MECHANISM AT ALL**: `props.active` rides the datum, and because `keyField` is gone every mint is fresh — measured moving across two deliveries, with the engine's `props` rendering settled on the way

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-201`'s open half and `D-202`'s limit (i), closed by the premise `D-202` itself changed.

**THE GAP CLOSED ITSELF WHEN THE PREMISE MOVED.** `D-201` measured that **`props.active` reaches the attribute at mint and then freezes UNDER `keyField` REUSE** — so a marker that moves could not ride the datum, and the turn could not write it as a `state-slice` either (`minted: []`, and a key→id map is `D-129`'s copy). **`D-202` then removed `keyField`**, because the label could ride the datum anyway and the marker could not ride a *reused* node. **That made every delivery mint FRESH nodes — and a fresh mint re-applies everything the datum carries.** **So the marker became a datum entry rather than a mechanism, and `D-202`'s limit (i) — *"a marker that moves still needs a mechanism this turn does not have"* — is discharged by having no mechanism.**

**MEASURED, FOUR READINGS, THE MARKER MOVING.**

| delivery | `tab-1` "First" | `tab-2` "Second" |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `target="counter-card" active="true"` (`node-125`) | `target="echo-card" active="false"` (`node-126`) |
| 2 | `target="counter-card" active="false"` (`node-143`) | `target="echo-card" active="true"` (`node-144`) |

**The marker moved, and no row carries a stale value** — with ids churning `125/126 → 143/144` under `keyField: undefined` and `minted: [both]`, which is `D-202`'s fresh-mint premise confirmed from the other side.

**AND THE ENGINE'S `props` RENDERING IS SETTLED ON THE WAY, WHICH THE DESIGN PAGE HAD GUESSED.** Measured: **`false` ⇒ `active="false"`**; **`'true'`/`'false'` ⇒ the same text**; **omitted ⇒ NO attribute at all**. **The design page's idiom said `'true'` *or removed*, and the removal arm was not taken** — a boolean `false` renders a literal `false`, which is what the page's re-grain owes.

**THE DATUM, WITH BOTH PROPERTIES THE ORDER CARES ABOUT.** `{ label: record?.label ?? id, ...(record ?? {}), props: { target, active } }` — **`label` is still the FIRST scalar member** (so the engine's first-scalar source anchor still composes the row's text, `D-201`) **and `props` is still LAST** (so the object displaces nothing). **No `state-slice`, no map, no second mint, no operand moved, and no `keyField` restored.**

## D-206 — THE TWO CLOSED DOMAINS WIDEN AND `width`/`height` REACHES THE WHOLE TREE — including a **LIVE real-DOM drive that passes**, which is the first thing in this unit verified outside the shim that the layout depends on

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `S-7`/`S-8` (`view-shape.ts`, `view-record/index.ts`) and the propagation pass that followed, plus the demo's own live runner.

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `tests/e2e/app-layout/app-layout.test.ts` (new, unmarked, gating) — `AL-1`…`AL-11` from `docs/L1/app-layout.md` §5.

**THE BATTERY IS FIVE BOOTS FOR ELEVEN ROWS, AND THAT IS A MEASURED CHOICE.** The groups are **skeleton** (`AL-1`/`AL-2`/`AL-6`, read-only), **tabs** (`AL-3`/`AL-4`/`AL-5`, one record and three acts), **menus** (`AL-7` alone, because its declared failure mode is killing its own boot), **view** (`AL-8`/`AL-10`, both writing `['zones']`) and **driver** (`AL-9`/`AL-11`, one envelope and two acts); **strictly sequential**, because the live-boot lock is host-wide. **Every electron boot is a casualty risk** (`D-165`/`D-173`), so eleven boots would have been eleven chances to lose the battery to a flake.

**SEVEN PASS, AND THE FOUR REDS ARE THE ROWS DOING THEIR JOB.**

**`AL-3` — THE AGENT CANNOT CLICK A ROW.** The switch turn is a **DOM `click` listener**; **`provident.dispatch` runs declared handler bodies**, and the minted row **declares none**; and **a driver envelope's load tears the graph down**, so a body cannot reach a minted row either. **So the tab switch is reachable by a HUMAN and not by an agent** — which is `D-177`'s finding returning through a different door: the row stopped being a depiction **for a person**, and stayed one **for the agent**.

**`AL-5` — AND THIS ONE IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A TRADE: THE LANDING TERMINAL NEVER HIDES.** The error page follows the record; **the landing page's `display` write is issued by the SAME delivery that then mints**, and **the mint's upstream placement behaviour (`D-182`) discards it**. **So one of the two authored terminals cannot be hidden** — the first live-ish evidence that `D-182`'s routing defect has a user-visible consequence beyond the zone layout.

**AND `AL-10` READS MARKUP AND SAYS SO, BECAUSE COMPUTED STYLE IS UNREACHABLE ON A GATING LEG — MEASURED TWICE.** The app boots through `bootstrap()`, so `code.get('')` answers `value: null` and `code.set` refuses *"no envelope loaded"*; and **every driver envelope REPLACES the graph**, so a `getComputedStyle` body would compute the driver's nodes, not the app's. **So `D-204`'s missing instrument is still missing, and the row states both reasons rather than faking it.**

## D-209 — A MINTED ROW **CAN** CARRY A LIVE-FUNCTION HANDLER THAT `provident.dispatch` RUNS — measured, not traced — so the controls become agent-drivable with **no new preload surface at all**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, on `D-208`'s `AL-3`/`AL-7`):** *"Make the controls agent-drivable via authored handler bodies"*, established by a probe after a source trace.

**THE MEASUREMENT, WHICH WAS THE ONE THING THE TRACE COULD NOT SETTLE.** A probe mints two rows on the app's own `Runtime` (the real envelope, the DOM shim), **the first carrying a live-function handler**, then dispatches `click` at it:

```json
{ "mint": "applied", "mintedCount": 2, "first": "node-74",
  "ran": ["row-one"], "dispatchAnswer": ["ran-one"], "rowsInHtml": 3 }
```

**`ran` carries the closure's own side effect and `dispatchAnswer` carries its return** — so **a `rows-mint` datum may carry `handlers: [{ name, event: 'click', body: <function> }]`, the minted node renders with it, and `dispatchEvent` runs it with `ctx`.** **The datum shape is the record row plus `label`, `props`, and `handlers` as a top-level member beside them**; a **string** body would be adopted and **never run** (`rows-mint` does not compile bodies), so **the datum must carry a FUNCTION**.

**AND THAT MEANS THE CHEAPEST PATH IS ALSO THE SAFEST ONE.** The reach research found that a body is `new Function`-compiled in the renderer's global scope and **can name `window.provident`** — which would let an agent's `provident.dispatch` reach **every preload member**, since `dispatch` sits in the default grant outside MCP's `guarded` wrapper. **But a live-function body minted from `driveTabsRows` is a CLOSURE**: it can call the realm's own turn — **`focusActRoute` for a row** — **without naming the bridge at all.** **So the ruling is met by a closure rather than by a surface**, and **the security widening the reach research named is not taken.**

**AND THE MENUS PANE TAKES THE SAME SHAPE RATHER THAN AN AUTHORED BODY.** Its items are **authored**, so their bodies would be **strings** — which means `window.provident` in the envelope, which is the surface above. **The alternative is a wiring-installed `handlers` state-slice** (`node.js` adopts `handlers` from the data layer), **installing a closure that calls the same route the DOM listener does** — **so the pane's dispatch becomes agent-reachable without an authored bridge reference either.** **Both controls, one mechanism, no new surface.**

**WHAT IT COSTS, NAMED.** **(i)** The op is **journaled shallowly** (`{kind, …rest}`), so **a function sits in the journal** and a condense's byte estimate aborts contained (`condense-aborted`) — a fact the mint's own path now carries for every row. **(ii)** A body's return crosses `JSON.stringify`, so it must be **JSON-safe**. **(iii)** `keyField` cannot come back: a restored key would answer `rows-reuse-shape-ignored` on a differing datum (`D-201`'s trade, unchanged).

**WHAT IT CHANGES FOR `AL-3`/`AL-7`.** **`AL-3` stops being a row that cannot pass**: the minted row now carries a body, so an agent's `provident.dispatch` at its `nodeId` **switches the tab through the same act the human's click uses**. **`AL-7` likewise**: the menus items gain a wiring-installed handler, so eighteen dispatches produce eleven receipts and seven refusals **through the route `main` already guards**. **Both rows keep their subjects and lose only the reason they were red.**

**THE READINGS AT THIS HEAD ARE `D-208`'S** — this row moves no repo byte; its product is a measurement, a datum shape, and the reason the safe path is also the cheap one.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-208`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a trace confirmed by a probe, a closure preferred to a surface on security grounds rather than convenience, a journal cost accepted with its name, and two battery rows that can now pass without their subjects moving.**

## D-210 — THE LANDING TERMINAL NEVER HIDES BECAUSE ITS WITNESS IS **TAUTOLOGICAL**: `answer.landing` *is* the active row's id, so `activeIds[0] === answer.landing` can never be false — `D-208`'s stated cause is **refuted by measurement**, and **a test row pins the vacuous answer**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `AL-5`'s and `AL-3`'s reds, pursued through a reorder measurement to the predicate itself.

**`D-208`'S CAUSE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE.** That row said the landing page's `display` write *"is discarded by the mint"* (`D-182`'s upstream routing defect). **Measured in a real Electron renderer: the write is NOT discarded** — a `state-slice` `css.style` on `tabs-landing-page` read back `display: none;` **after two `rows-mint`s and after a whole delivery's dirtied set, in both orders.** **So the delivery order is neutral and the reorder that was tried changes no reading.** **The write is issued with the WRONG VALUE.**

**THE PREDICATE, AND WHY IT CANNOT FAIL.** `deriveTabsWitness` (`src/renderer/tabs-client.ts`) computes

```ts
const landingWitness = activeIds.length === 1 && activeIds[0] === answer.landing
```

**and `answer.landing` is defined as *"the id of the row reading active"*** (`src/main/tabs-record/index.ts:56-59`, **derived, never stored**). **So the second comparison compares the active row's id to itself**: `landingWitness` is **true whenever exactly one row is active, and can never be false for a legal record.** Probed on the app's own record shape (`landing` inactive, `second` active, `landing:'second'`): **`{"landing":{"witness":true,"activeIds":["second"]}}`** — **the wrong value, from a predicate that has no false arm.**

**AND NOTHING CAUGHT IT BECAUSE A ROW PINS IT.** `tests/integration/store-tabs-record/tabs-client.test.ts`'s **`TC-10`** asserts **`witness: true`** on `[{landing,false},{t4,true}]` with `landing:'t4'` — **the vacuous answer, asserted.** **So the defect has a green row defending it**, which is the `D-30`/`D-139` class at its sharpest: **a row that cannot fail and a row that pins the failure are the same row seen from two sides.**

**THE FIX IS ONE COMPARISON AND IT IS BLOCKED AT A BOUNDARY.** The landing page must be shown only when **the landing entry** is the active row — so the comparison must be against **the landing entry's own id**, which `src/main/tabs-record/index.ts:582` exports as **`TABS_LANDING_ID`** with a docblock saying *"its own `TABS_LANDING_ID` is this value, and a second literal in a client is the rename that half-lands"*. **But that docblock is not true of this client at this head**: **a VALUE import of that module pulls it into the renderer bundle and `npm run build` dies** (`Could not resolve "node:util"`), measured twice; every existing renderer→main import is `import type` and erases; and **`src/shared/` carries no browser-safe spelling of it** (`TABS_LANDING_PAGE_ID` is a different value). **So the single spelling the docblock promises does not exist on the renderer's side of the boundary** — and **adding a second literal in the client is exactly what the docblock forbids.**

**SO THE FIX NEEDS ONE SPELLING IN `src/shared/` FIRST** — the constant moves to where both sides can import it, `tabs-record` re-exports it rather than re-spelling it, the client imports it, **and `TC-10` is re-grained to the correct answer** (it is a battery row defending the defect, and its owner must move it in the same edit).

**THE READINGS.** `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; the tabs and wiring batteries **`69/69` green — *because* `TC-10` pins the vacuous answer**; `AL-5` and `AL-3` **red** with `landing="display: block;" error="display: block;"`.

**AND TWO PROSE DEFECTS ARE NAMED WITH IT**: both e2e rows' own messages still blame the upstream mint-render placement (`D-182`) rather than the witness's value, **so they will keep naming the wrong cause while red** — and those messages are owed a re-grain by the same edit that fixes the predicate.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-209`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a cause refuted by measurement, a predicate with no false arm, a row defending it, and a fix blocked by a spelling that lives on the wrong side of a build boundary.**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `AL-4`'s re-grain, and the qualification its author volunteered.

**`AL-4` NOW MEASURES THE TRADE RATHER THAN THE LOSING SIDE OF IT.** Its title is *"the marker MOVES across a re-mint and the fresh rows are still CONTROLS: every id churns, and that churn is the price"*. **Three clauses**: the **marker moves** across a re-mint (both per-target readings asserted as a pair, and the old row asserted `false` rather than *"not true"*); **no stale value** (each rendered marker compared row-by-row against `data.read(['tabs'])`'s own flag, so the rendering and the record must agree); **the churn as the cost** (`kept` must be `[]`, both targets must show a new id — measured `node-171/172 → node-196/197`) **and the churn is per delivery, not once ever**; **and each fresh row is still dispatchable** (a dispatch at the fresh row returns `focus <target>`, the row's `lastActiveAt` advances, the marker stays) — **the arm that separates *"the closure ran"* from *"'the act performed"*, which is `D-209`'s cost (ii) made a row.** **A `keyField`-restored control is named in the row's own words**: restore it and `D-201`'s reuse freezes `props`, so the after-read returns the before values and clause 1 reds. **Two one-line flips redded it alone**, restored md5-identically.

## D-214 — `D-204`'S INSTRUMENT EXISTS: an authored carrier the app writes its **COMPUTED** figures into, so a gating row can finally see the layout — and the moment it was measured it reported **why the app never painted at boot**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-204`'s missing instrument, built as a self-report turn (design at `docs/L3/renderer-wiring/design.md` rev 20, `W1`–`W5`) plus `app-envelope`'s `A-8` carrier (rev 6).

**THE SHAPE, AND IT IS THE ONE THIS UNIT ALREADY PROVED.** `AL-9` established that **a body can read a browser API and write the answer into an authored carrier, which a gating row then reads as MARKUP.** The app's own regions cannot be read that way — **every driver envelope replaces the graph** (`D-208`) — **so the read happens in the app's own realm**: `reportMeasuredFigures(runtime)` is **`driveLayoutRegions`' last act**, and it censuses `getComputedStyle` **first**, writing **nothing and throwing nothing** where the realm has no such function (the DOM shim, the whole unit suite). **The report lands in the carrier's `content` as `id.property=value;` text — never `css.style`**, because `D-203` proved that member's *object* form is the one place shim and browser disagree.

**AND THE INSTRUMENT WORKS, PROVED IN A REAL DOM BOTH WAYS.** Before any paint the carrier reads **`top.height=396px`** — the **fill**. A CSS-text write then reads

```
top.height=140px; bottom.height=60px; left.width=120px; right.width=90px; tabs-landing-page.display=block;
```

and **the OBJECT spelling puts it back to `top.height=396px`** with `applied` and an empty `style` attribute. **So the instrument catches `D-203` exactly: the inert write reports the fill rather than the record's figure.** **The row reads the CARRIER'S TEXT; the TURN reads the computed style** — and the design says it in those words so nobody later mistakes a markup read for a layout read.

**AND THE FIRST THING IT MEASURED WAS A DEFECT NOBODY HAD LOOKED FOR.** On a **cold boot the carrier is EMPTY across fifteen polls**, and `pane-menus` keeps only its authored `height: 100%; overflow-x: auto` — **because `startViewShape` calls `driveLayoutRegions` (and therefore the report) only from the DELIVERY subscription**, while its one boot read (`fill()`) adopts and logs. **So nothing is painted until something changes a record.** After **one induced delivery** the carrier reads `top.height=40px; pane-a.width=absent; pane-a.height=absent; pane-menus.width=100px; tabs-landing-page.display=block;` — **so a stated pane width is applied on a delivery and NOT at boot**, which is `F3`'s class (`D-164`) in the layout: **a delivery is the only trigger, so a second boot that receives none shows the authored CSS.** **Routed, not fixed: a boot paint is refused by `D-96`/`T-4`, so the fix is a decision, not an edit.**

**TWO SMALLER FINDINGS TRAVEL WITH IT.** **`pane-a`'s figures read `absent`** — **no authored element carries id `pane-a`** (the stage pane's box is `gutter-card`, which `D-194` already flagged as a record-id-versus-node-id mapping), so its report is honest and meaningless. **And `driveLayoutRegions`' own docblock still says the pane arm *"is INERT until `S-8` lands"*** — **false at this head**, since `view-shape.ts`, `paneOf` and the paint all carry the pair (`D-206`). **A stale paragraph inside the function it describes.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,957 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,959`** over **`145`** files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; the demo rebuilt to **`40`** inputs; the census rows (`M-2`, `X-1`, `I-10`, `P-TC-IM-2`) re-grained to **`73 = 18 + 5 + 2 + 13 + 35`**, **the fourth term named** as the interface inventory's 34 **plus the measured-figures carrier**, with **an independent walk of `demoEnvelope()` agreeing**.
