## D-215 — THE BOOT-PAINT FORK IS REAL AND `T-4` IS THE SENTENCE THAT DECIDES IT: **"nothing is applied at a boot — `fill()` adopts and never applies"** — so a cold boot shows the authored CSS while the record already holds the figures

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-214`'s first measurement, read against `T-4`'s own claim.

**WHAT WAS MEASURED.** On a cold boot the measured-figures carrier is **empty across fifteen polls** and `pane-menus` keeps only its authored `height: 100%; overflow-x: auto`; after **one induced delivery** it reads `pane-menus.width=100px`. **The cause is not a defect in the paint**: `startViewShape` registers the subscription and then calls **`fill()`**, whose continuation **logs only**. **So the record IS read at boot and its figures are NOT applied.**

**AND THAT IS A STATED INVARIANT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.** `tests/theme-declaration.test.ts`'s **`T-4`** reads: *"**NOTHING IS APPLIED AT A BOOT** — measured three times: on a FRESH profile the record a boot carries is the [default] … the boot read STILL writes nothing … **what keeps a boot silent is that `fill()` adopts and never applies.**"* **So the app deliberately declines to apply a record it has just read**, and **a layout boot paint would red that row.**

**THE FORK, STATED AS THE TWO REAL OPTIONS AND NOTHING IN BETWEEN.**

**(A) STAY SILENT AT BOOT.** `T-4` stands unchanged. **A cold boot shows the authored CSS** — the zones' authored `overflow`, `pane-menus`'s authored `100%` width — **until any record changes**, after which the record's figures appear and never leave. **The measured carrier is empty at boot by design**, so `AL-12` must be taken **after a delivery**, and **the app's first frame is not the record's**.

**(B) APPLY THE LAYOUT'S FIGURES AT BOOT.** The `fill()` continuation calls the paint once, beside its log. **`T-4` must be re-grained and its invariant narrowed** from *"nothing is applied at a boot"* to *"nothing is applied at a boot **except figures whose subject is a rendering the record already states**"* — **and the theme's silence, which is what `T-4` was written for, must stay silent**, so the row would need to say which family it excuses and why. **The app's first frame becomes the record's.**

**WHAT EACH COSTS, NAMED.** **(A)** costs a **visible first frame that is not the state**: a zone with a stated size renders at its authored CSS until something changes, and **a second boot that never receives a delivery shows an unpainted layout for its life** — which is **`F3`'s class**, the one `D-174` closed for the read-out by *deleting* the authored figure. **(B)** costs **an invariant, narrowed**: `T-4`'s three measurements stay true of the theme and stop being true of the layout, and **the SSR fragment moves at boot for the first time**, which is the thing the row exists to prevent.

**WHY THIS SEAT WILL NOT CHOOSE IT.** `T-4` is a **gating row asserting an invariant measured three times**, and this unit's own record shows what happens when a row is re-grained in the direction an author wants (`D-212`: two rows were moved only after the defect they defended was **proved by measurement**). **Here the measurement exists and the ruling does not** — so the fork is put to the user.

**AND ONE THING IS TRUE WHICHEVER WAY IT GOES.** The **instrument** (`D-214`) works: it reports the computed figure after a delivery and reports the **fill** when the write is inert. **So `AL-12` is worth its boot either way**, and the fork changes **when** the carrier has something to say, not whether it can say it.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-214`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a defect that is not one, an invariant that explains it, two options with their costs named, and a seat that refused to re-grain a row in the direction it wanted.**

## D-216 — THE PARADIGM IS THE RULING: **"the render is driven by listeners on the store"** — so the boot is silent **by design**, a render not driven by a listener is off-paradigm, and `T-4`'s invariant is not narrowed but **confirmed**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim, on `D-215`'s fork):** *"The design paradigm has always been that the render is driven by listeners on the store"*.

**THE FORK CLOSES ON A PRINCIPLE RATHER THAN ON A COST.** `D-215` put two options and named what each would cost. **The answer is neither of its two as stated — it is that the first option was never a cost at all.** **A cold boot showing the authored CSS until a listener speaks is not an unpainted layout; it is a surface waiting for the store, which is what this app is.** **The render's trigger is the listener; a boot paint would be a render with no event behind it**, and that is the thing the paradigm forbids.

**SO `T-4` IS CONFIRMED AND NOT NARROWED.** *"Nothing is applied at a boot — `fill()` adopts and never applies"* **is not an instrument limitation that a later unit may relax**: it is **the paradigm observed at the boot path**. **The record is read and not applied because a read is not a listener.** **`D-215`'s option (B) is refused by the ruling, not by its cost.**

**WHAT THIS RULES OUT, STATED SO IT IS NOT RE-ARGUED.** **Any render without a listener behind it**: a **boot paint** (this fork); **a timer, an interval, or a poll** — which the corpus already refused by habit and now can cite; **a retry that repaints after a failure**; and **a render scheduled by a write's own continuation** where the write's *delivery* is the lawful trigger. **The four delivery turns, the mint, the attach and the receipt write all hang off a listener or an authored click — none of them schedules itself.**

**AND IT FIXES WHAT THE INSTRUMENT'S ROW MUST LOOK LIKE.** `AL-12` — *the figure the browser APPLIED equals the figure the record holds* — **must induce a delivery** (a `['zones']` or `['panes']` write) and then read the **carrier's text**, because **before that write the carrier is empty and that is correct**. **A row that read the carrier at boot would be asserting the absence of a paint the paradigm requires to be absent.** **So the row's own first clause is its setup: change the record, wait for the listener's render, then read.**

**WHAT IS CONFIRMED TRUE WHICHEVER WAY THE CARRIER IS READ.** The instrument works (`D-214`): after a delivery it reports the **computed** figure (`top.height=140px`, `pane-menus.width=100px`), and with the object spelling it reports the **fill** (`396px`) — **so it catches `D-203` exactly, and it catches it only after a listener has spoken.** **The measured carrier is empty at boot as a CONSEQUENCE of the paradigm, and its emptiness is therefore evidence the paradigm holds rather than evidence anything is missing.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-215`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a fork closed by a principle instead of a price, an invariant confirmed rather than narrowed, four kinds of self-scheduled render named as off-paradigm, and the setup a battery row needs in order to test a render that only exists after a listener speaks.**

## D-217 — THE CLARIFICATION REFRAMES `D-216`: **"the initial render is driven by the listeners firing on store load"** — so the measured boot silence is a **DEFECT IN THE DELIVERY CHAIN**, not the paradigm observed

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim, immediately after `D-216`):** *"The initial render is driven by the listeners firing on store load"*.

**`D-216` READ THE PARADIGM CORRECTLY AND DREW THE WRONG CONCLUSION FROM IT.** The ruling stands — **the render is driven by listeners on the store**, and a render with no event behind it is off-paradigm. **But the boot is supposed to HAVE an event**: **the listeners fire when the store loads**, and **that firing is the initial render's driver.** **So a cold boot with an empty carrier is not "a surface waiting for the store" — it is a surface whose listener did not fire, which is a defect of exactly the class this unit has been finding.**

**WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND WHAT IT NOW MEANS.** `D-214`/`D-215` measured **the carrier empty across fifteen polls** at a cold boot while the record was already read. **Under `D-216` that looked like the paradigm holding; under this row it is the store loading without its listeners reaching the renderer.** **The two facts are compatible with three different causes and this seat will not pick one by reading**: **(i)** the app subscribes **after** the load's writes have already happened, so the initial changes are missed; **(ii)** the store does not emit on load at all, and the subscription's only source of truth is a later change; **(iii)** the store emits and the app's client receives it but **adopts without driving** — the shape `fill()` shows, where the read and the delivery have different continuations. **Each has a different owner and a different fix**, so they are separated by measurement before anything is designed.

**AND THE `fill()` BOOT READ IS NOW EXPLAINED RATHER THAN EXCUSED.** `startViewShape` is called from the RENDERER's `main()` late but **NOT last** — **CORRECTED AT `D-218`: `startAppStateShape` and `startSecurityShape` follow it, and the `main()` in question is the renderer's, not `src/main/main.ts`'s** — so the subscription is registered **at the end of boot**; **whatever the store did while loading happened before that**. **`fill()` is not the paradigm's substitute — it is the app covering a missed event by asking once**, which is precisely the pattern the paradigm exists to replace. **If the listener fired on load, the boot read would be redundant** and its silence would be a design choice rather than a patch.

**WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT `T-4`, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS.** `T-4` reads *"nothing is applied at a boot — `fill()` adopts and never applies"*. **Under `D-216` that was the paradigm; under this row it is the SYMPTOM**: **`fill()` is the wrong channel, and its not-applying is why the boot paints nothing.** **So `T-4` is not confirmed — it describes the defect accurately.** **A boot whose listener fires would apply, because the application would be a DELIVERY's turn and not a read's.** **The row must therefore be re-read, not re-graded**: its three measurements stay true and its explanation changes, which is the same shape `D-210` had when a row's assertion was right and its reason wrong.

**THE RESEARCH THIS ROW ORDERS.** Establish, with sites, **which of (i)/(ii)/(iii) holds**: when the store's load writes its record, whether the crossing emits for them, and whether a subscription registered at the end of `main()` could ever have received them. **And name what the initial render would be if the listener did fire** — which turn would run, and whether it would be the same delivery the app already handles.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-216`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a correction that turns its predecessor's conclusion over while keeping its ruling, a measurement compatible with three causes that are not guessed between, and a row that described a defect accurately and was read as describing a design.**

## D-218 — THE CAUSE IS **(i)** AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: the storeroom **never fires on load**, a write before the subscription is **DROPPED**, and the fix has **nowhere to move to** inside `createProfileStore` — so the app must **re-deliver at attach**, which is the paradigm satisfied rather than bypassed

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-217`'s ordered research, measured from sites (the seat had no shell; the counts are structural, and the probe it would have run is recorded below).

**THE STORE'S CONTRACT, IN ITS OWN WORDS** (`provident-storeroom`'s `README.guide.md`): *"Listeners fire on `write` and `delete`, and never on a read … **nor does a boot or any read-driven traversal fire a listener**."* **`listen(h, set)` only RESERVES an entry, `register(h, fn)` only INSTALLS the function, and the one invocation site is `deliver()`, driven by a write's own `triggered` set.** **So there is no initial event, no current-state delivery and no replay — and a write made before the subscription is DROPPED**, because the trigger set is computed per commit and a handle absent from the registry has no entry to fire.

**SO CAUSE (i) HOLDS, AND THE ORDER PROVES IT WITHOUT A PROBE.** **Moment one — the writes**: `createProfileStore` runs the registration instant, whose repairs write the placeholders, **and the store arms `cfg.listeners` AFTER the batch that writes**. **Moment two — the subscription**: `viewSurface.attach()` runs **after construction and before the window exists**, and **the renderer's own registration is later again**, taken after `bridge.ready()`. **Between them the boot writes nothing**, so **deliveries = 0** — and the first delivery is a later change's push.

**AND THE OTHER TWO CAUSES ARE EXCLUDED RATHER THAN UNLIKELY.** **(ii)** is **true of the contract** — no emission on load — **but not this boot's cause**, because **this boot DID write** (the record `fill()` adopts is the repair's) and **a repair's write does deliver to a standing handle**. **(iii)** is excluded: the delivery's continuation **re-reads and hands the reading to the four turns**, `paint` among them; **only the boot READ adopts without driving** — which is exactly why the read succeeds and paints nothing.

**WHAT THE INITIAL RENDER WOULD BE, AND THE APP ALREADY HANDLES IT.** `driveLayoutRegions(getViewClient().reading(), runtime)` — **the same turn `D-214` measured after a delivery.** **No new renderer arm is needed.** **And it would write only PART of what a boot needs**: the panes' members from `viewPanesPlaceholder` (`100 × 100`) **and NOT the zones** — because **the zone repair's value is memberless**, and the paint skips a zone stating no `size` (`D-191`). **So the initial render's own subject is the panes**, and the zones stay authored until something writes them.

**THE FIX HAS NOWHERE TO MOVE TO INSIDE THE STORE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** *"Subscribe earlier"* is not available: **the earliest subscription the store offers — `cfg.listeners` — is applied AFTER the batch that writes**, and its function can only be installed by `register` on the returned instance. **So no ordering inside `createProfileStore` can hear the load's writes.** **And a store-side replay alone would not fix it either**: main's push fans out to `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()`, which is **EMPTY at the construction instant** — **so the chain needs a RE-DELIVERY AT ATTACH**, not only an earlier subscription.

**SO THE FIX SHAPE IS THE APP'S, AND IT SATISFIES THE PARADIGM RATHER THAN BYPASSING IT.** **When a window attaches and the renderer's subscription is standing, `main` pushes ONE delivery per family carrying the address it already carries** — the same push a write produces, with the same shape (`D-92`: a push is an ADDRESS, and the client re-reads). **The listener then fires, the client re-reads, and the render is driven by a listener** — which is precisely *"the initial render is driven by the listeners firing on store load"*, **with the app supplying the load event the store declines to emit.** **It is NOT a boot paint**: nothing renders without an event, and the event is a real push on the real channel.

**AND `fill()` IS NOT REDUNDANT — IT STAYS.** It is the only channel for **a realm whose bridge carries no `view` member**, for **a `register` that threw**, and for **a boot whose families already stand**, where the repairs write nothing. **It is redundant only against the cold-boot paint it never performed** — which is the defect, not the read.

**THE PROBE THIS SEAT COULD NOT RUN, RECORDED SO IT CAN BE.** In `/tmp`: one store with the two view pairs and a `filePath`; **arm A** `listen`+`register` after `createProfileStore`; **arm B** `cfg.listeners` before it; **arm C** write-then-`listen` — **expecting A `0` until the next write, B `0` and C `0`**, which is the contract read three ways.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-217`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a cause proved by order, a store that says in its own words that a boot fires nothing, a fix with nowhere to move to inside the store, and an app-supplied load event that is a delivery rather than a paint.**

## D-219 — THE PACKAGE ANSWERS `D-218`: **`provident-storeroom@1.11.0` DELIVERS AT THE CREATION**, after the repairs land — so the initial render **is** listener-driven, and the app's silence is now a **missing `cfg.listeners` entry** rather than a missing capability

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Package updated to 1.11.0 to support listener return on store creation"*.

**THE VERSION MOVED AND THE APP STILL CONSTRUCTS.** `provident-storeroom` is now **`1.11.0`** (installed from `1.10.0`; `package.json`'s caret already admitted it). **`1.11.0` is a MINOR carrying a BREAKING change** — *"a `cfg.listeners[]` entry now REQUIRES its `listener` function; the element is `{ address, handle, listener }`, three own members with the third required"*, and **a two-member entry is REFUSED (`AddressMalformed`, subject `listeners`) before any filesystem act`**. **Measured: the app passes `listeners: []`** at both constructions (`operator-settings`' and the profile store's), **so nothing is refused** — the store-view-record battery is **`56/56` green** on the new version.

**AND THAT EMPTY ARRAY IS EXACTLY THE DEFECT `D-218` MEASURED.** The app registers **after** construction (`viewSurface.attach` → `listen` + `register`), so the creation's writes are dropped. **`1.11.0` closes the gap upstream**: its delivery now occurs at **FOUR registration instants — the creation, the boot, `addConstraint` and a re-arm** — **in `D-117`'s order, `ASK → REPAIRS LAND → RE-RUN → SAVE → DELIVER → THE ANSWER`, so a creation's listener is invoked AFTER the repairs have landed.** **Which is precisely the event `D-218` said the store declined to emit.**

**SO THE FIX IS NOW AN ENTRY, NOT A MECHANISM.** The app must **supply `cfg.listeners` at construction**, each entry carrying its `listener`, for the families it reads — and **the creation's delivery then fires it after the repairs write**. **Two consequences are named rather than discovered**: **(i)** **the listener fires BEFORE THE WINDOW EXISTS** (main constructs the store, then the window), so its push has no destination yet — **the listener must QUEUE the addresses and `attachWindow` must flush them**, which is the *"re-delivery at attach"* `D-218` named, **now driven by a listener instead of synthesized by hand**; **(ii)** **the app already registers after construction**, so the pass must **move** the registration rather than add a second one — **two registrations for one address is the copy `D-129` forbids**, and the corpus's one-registration discipline (`D-93`) is explicit.

**AND THE MIGRATION ROUTE THE PACKAGE ITSELF NAMES IS NOT THE ONE TO TAKE.** It offers *"an entry that wants to construct first and be armed later keeps constructing by passing `listener: () => {}`"*. **That is a function that does nothing** — it would satisfy the refusal and **change no behaviour**, which is the shape this corpus calls a row that cannot fail. **The pass must arm the entry with a listener that queues, not with a no-op.**

**WHAT DOES NOT MOVE, PER THE PACKAGE'S OWN LIST.** `D-90`'s skip, `D-104`'s landing delivery, `D-117`'s reversal delivery, `D-106`'s save, `D-107`'s rollback composition and the write's terminal-arm delivery are **each frozen by name**; the empty batch is still a no-op; and **the instance's own member set stays fifteen**.

**THE READINGS AT THIS BUMP.** `tests/integration/store-view-record/` **`56/56`** on `1.11.0`; **the full suite's figures are not yet re-taken** — this row records the bump and the capability, and the next pass must take them.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-218`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a package answering a row, an empty array that caused a silence and now names it, a delivery that arrives after the repairs and before the window, and a migration route that satisfies a refusal without changing anything.**

## D-220 — **THE INITIAL RENDER IS LISTENER-DRIVEN, MEASURED ON A COLD PROFILE WITH NO DRIVER WRITE**: the carrier goes **`0 B → 96 B`**, the construction alone fires the sink four times — and the pass names **the two constructions' remaining gap** and **the queue that no row drives**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-219`'s capability, moved into the app (`provident-storeroom@1.11.0` installed) — the design at three modules' `delivery.md` pages, the hunks at `src/main/`, and the propagation through 24 rows.

**THE PARADIGM IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** *"The initial render is driven by the listeners firing on store load."* **A cold profile, no driver write, `get_rendered_html` only**: the measured-figures carrier `""` (0 bytes) before, and `pane-a.width=absent;pane-a.height=absent;pane-menus.width=100px;tabs-landing-page.display=block;` (**96 bytes**) after. **And in-process, the construction alone fires the sink four times — `tabs:tabs`, `view:panes`, `view:zones`, `view:theme`** — with `drag` lawfully firing at no creation instant.

**THE MOVE, AND THE ONE PLACE THE PACKAGE'S OWN ADVICE WAS REFUSED.** Five `{address, handle, listener}` entries at the construction — **tabs first**, then the four view roots — each listener being **`deliver`**: fan-out, then `sink(address)`; **total, writing nothing, containing its own throw** (rank-21 `ListenerBodyThrew` would otherwise refuse the construction). **The package offers a migration route — `listener: () => {}` — which satisfies the refusal and changes nothing**, and it is **refused in the code's own words**: a function that does nothing is **the shape this corpus calls a row that cannot fail**. **`attach`/`detach`/`onChanged` are DELETED** with their two call sites; **`subscribe` keeps its signature and stops touching the store**; **two registrations for one address is the copy `D-129` forbids**, so this is a **MOVE**.

**AND THE FLUSH IS NOT WHERE `D-219` SAID IT WOULD BE.** That row wrote that `attachWindow` would flush the queue. **Measured: it cannot** — it runs **before `loadFile`**, so a push there re-creates the loss. **The flush rides `ipcMain.on(IPC_READY)` after `markReady()`**, with the renderer registering every handler **in the same turn that sends readiness**. **The row's letter was wrong and the design pass corrected it before a byte moved.**

**WHAT THE FIRST FRAME ACTUALLY SHOWS, WHICH IS LESS THAN THE DESIGN WANTED AND IS NAMED.** one minted `tab-row` (label `landing`, `active=true`); `pane-menus` painted `width: 100px` inside the top zone; **`bottom`/`left`/`right` authored `css` only** — **the record states no `size`**; the stage derived with the landing page shown; eighteen menu items with the receipt empty. **So the zones' fixed dimension is still unwritten — by silence, not by refusal, since no writer under `src/` states a `size`.** That is `D-129`'s class reached through absence and it is **routed**: the zone repair writes a memberless record, and the paint skips a zone stating no size.

**TWO GAPS THE PROPAGATION ITSELF NAMED, AND NEITHER IS A ROW.** **(i) THE FIX LANDED AT ONE OF THE APP'S TWO CONSTRUCTIONS**: `src/main/operator-settings/index.ts` still constructs with `listeners: []` and **registers after creation**, so that crossing's creation still delivers to nobody — **the app's secure crossing has the defect this row closes for the profile store**. **(ii) THE QUEUE'S OWN BEHAVIOUR IS DRIVEN BY NO ROW**: `createDeliveryQueue`'s `held`/`arm` round trip is **string-asserted only**; **no row drives an arm and reads what it pushed.** **So the mechanism that makes the initial render arrive is, at this head, unmeasured by the battery that made the render visible.**

**AND THREE DOCUMENTS STILL STATE `1.10.0`'s WORLD**: `docs/L1/central-data-management.md`'s `S-12` Expected cell, `docs/L2/central-data/behaviour.md` §9, and `docs/L2/central-data/persistence.md`'s `^1.10.0` pin. **Reported, not edited** — their owners'.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,956 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,959`** over **`145`** files — **before the commit, with `B-1` as the only red** (the carve-out); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0** (from **39**); `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; the demo rebuilt to **`40`** inputs. **`typecheck:tests`' 39 errors went to zero** across `central-data`'s call sites and five other files.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-219`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a render finally driven by the event it was always meant to be driven by, a package's own advice refused in the code, a flush corrected before it shipped, and two gaps named by the pass that closed the first.**

## D-221 — THE SECURE CROSSING'S DELIVERY IS DESIGNED, AND ITS **ARMING IS NOT A HANDSHAKE**: four entries, one per **address**, held in the delivery's own closure and **drained by the first `subscribe`** — so the creation's delivery reaches an in-process consumer without any readiness signal

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-220`'s gap (i), designed at `docs/L3/operator-settings/delivery.md` (Rev 1, 100 lines — **a new module-named page**, because this module's standing L3 page is `docs/L3/security-store-storeroom/design.md`, unit-named and at `150`/`150`).

**FOUR ENTRIES, ONE PER ADDRESS, AND NOT ONE PER ROOT — WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE PROFILE STORE'S SHAPE AND FOR A STATED REASON.** The profile store carries **five** entries whose `['panes']` entry covers four addresses? **No**: it carries **one per root** (`['tabs']`, `['panes']`, `['zones']`, `['theme']`, `['drag']`). **The secure crossing carries FOUR, one per ADDRESS** (`RECORD`, `EXCLUSION`, `APP_STATE`, `PANE`) — **because an entry carries exactly one address and no act writes `[]`, so a "root entry" here would be a row that cannot fail in address form.** **Each entry's `listener` is the crossing's own `deliver`**, and **each subscriber's `body` is transcribed unchanged inside the fan-out** — so **an `APP_STATE_ADDRESS` delivery with no second listener still falls through to the first**, and **`D-104`'s one-argument total reading is unmoved**.

**AND THE ARMING IS THE PART THE PROFILE STORE COULD NOT TEACH.** That crossing arms on **`IPC_READY`**, because its push has a window to reach. **This one has no window and no handshake** — its subscribers are **in-process** (`settings-surface`'s `onDelivery`, `onSecurityChanged`, `onExclusionChanged`, `onAppStateDelivery`). **So the creation's addresses are HELD in the delivery's closure (minted before `storeCreate`) and DRAINED BY THE FIRST `subscribe`, inside that call.** **Fires = adopted ∩ resolving: four cold and four warm**, one `deliver` per address in creation order — **and `drag`'s silence at the profile store is the same rule seen from the other side.** **A second subscriber gets no replay**, except the remainder an **interrupted drain re-holds**; **a withdrawal after the drain does nothing, and before it cannot arise.**

**WHAT THE FIRST DELIVERY CARRIES, AND WHAT IT CANNOT REACH.** The signal is **the address only** (`D-92`), and **it arrives BEFORE `attach`'s read** — `attach` subscribes first, so the read is the second voice rather than the first. **But it CANNOT reach the realm**: this crossing's two pushes are **bare broadcasts with no queue covering them**, so **`D-218`'s boot fills stay open on that half**, exactly as they are for `app-shell`. **The row says so rather than implying the gap closed twice for one change.**

**AND `D-82` CLAUSE 2 IS NOT RE-GRADED.** `D-104` recorded the app-state rows' address as **delivering zero** and that *"a route is not a consumer"*. **This change moves a COUNT, not a GRADE** — the delivery now fires at a creation — **so the cell stands and the row must not read as a revival.** **That is the distinction this corpus keeps needing**: a count that moves is not a verdict that changes.

**THE HUNKS AND THE DEBT.** `OD-1` the delivery (entries/held/stand), `OD-2` the construction's `listeners: [...delivery.entries]`, `OD-3` `subscribe` → local fan-out and local drop, `OD-4` `withdraw` leaving whole, `OD-5` the falsified docblocks, `OD-6` the doc debt. **Owed to their owners and named, not taken**: the `150`/`150` re-grains of `security-store-storeroom/design.md` and `signatures.md` §3's census, and `docs/L2/security-store-storeroom/interface.md` §5's `attach` ordering — **and the two-name drift itself** (the module is `operator-settings`; its pages are filed under `security-store-storeroom`), which this page opens a module-named directory against rather than fixing.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-220`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a delivery that needed no handshake because its consumers are in the same process, four entries where the other crossing has five and by the opposite rule, and a count that moves while the grade stands.**

## D-222 — THE SECURE CROSSING'S DELIVERY LANDS AND **ITS DEFECT IS REPRODUCED ON DEMAND**: four addresses drained inside the first `subscribe`, a second gets nothing, an interrupted drain re-holds its remainder — and the same tree with only `listeners: []` restored sees **nothing, before or after a write**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-221`'s `OD-1`…`OD-5` in `src/main/operator-settings/index.ts`, and the fourteen rows the ledger named.

**THE MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT.** **A cold profile, no write from the test**: the **first `subscribe`** is called with **`operator-settings → operator-exclusion → operator-app-state → operator-pane`** — **four, in creation order, inside that call.** **A second `subscribe` gets `[]` and hears only the next write.** **An interrupted drain** drops the throwing subscriber **locally** and **re-holds the remainder** (`operator-exclusion`, `operator-app-state`, `operator-pane`), which the next subscriber drains. **The warm instance fires the same four.**

**AND THE CONTROL IS THE DEFECT ITSELF, REPRODUCED.** **The identical tree with only `listeners: []` restored** — the pre-change construction — **sees `[]` at `subscribe` AND `[]` after a write**, *because nothing is adopted, so nothing registers.* **That is the silence `D-218` measured at the profile store, now reproduced on demand at the other crossing** — which makes this row's fix a **demonstration** rather than an assertion.

**THE ROUTING DID NOT MOVE, AND `D-104`'S READING IS THE PROOF.** Each subscriber's `body` is **transcribed unchanged inside the fan-out**, so **an `APP_STATE` delivery with no second listener still falls through to the first** — **the one-argument total reading is byte-identical.** **Each entry's `listener` is a real `deliver`**: total, writing nothing, **containing its own throw** — and **the package's `listener: () => {}` route is refused**, as `D-220` required.

**FOURTEEN ROWS MOVED, NONE RETIRED.** `instance.test.ts`'s `:189` (the drain's four, then the write's address: **2 → 6**) and `:202` (the throw on the drain's first held address, drop plus re-held remainder); `operator-settings.test.ts`'s `:210` **falsified and re-grained** (handles are the construction's; subscription is a fan-out entry) and `:235` **re-gained by standing a quiet subscriber first** so the throw still lands at the pair's address; `SC-E5-18` measuring its drain prefix of **five** (the creation's four plus the unattended write's one); `PF-4`; `AP-1`/`AP-4`/`AP-5`; `SD-1`/`SD-4`; `settings-surface`'s `:136`/`:137`/`:140`/`:147`. **And two the page did not enumerate were found and re-grained**: `secure-panels`' roster attach sequence **2 → 5**, and `B-1`'s declared scope. **No row's subject left, so none was retired** — which is the other half of the discipline the retired ones satisfy.

**TWO THINGS THE PAGE COULD NOT EXPRESS, NAMED BY THE PASS.** **(i)** **The hold window is necessarily "construction → first subscriber"**, so a write fired before any consumer stands is **also** held and drained — which is why `SC-E5-18` reads **five** and not four. **The page names only the creation's event**; the implementation holds nothing after the first arrival, **which is what makes "drains once, no re-arm" structural rather than promised.** **(ii)** **`settings-surface`'s `attach` drain also re-patches the gate once from `PANE`** — the *"total reading of the domain"* — **a sink call the page's §4 prose does not count.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,958 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,960`** over **`145`** files (**head was `2,956`/`2,959`**: `+1` new row `CD-24`, `+1` formerly-red `B-1`); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks` regenerated to **`364` gating sites in `48` files**; `refs` **0** (221 rows); the demo rebuilt to **`40`** inputs. **Two transient reds cleared and are named**: `P-1` was `D-173`'s build window opened by the pass's own concurrent `npm run build`, and `B-1`'s carve-out preceded the declarations.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-221`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a defect reproduced on demand as its own control, a routing transcribed rather than rewritten, fourteen rows moved and none retired, and two behaviours the design page did not know it had.**

## D-223 — THE SECURE CROSSING'S TWO BARE BROADCASTS BECOME **PER-CHANNEL PENDING SETS**, FLUSHED AT THE REALM'S ARRIVAL — and a mis-classification made while measuring is corrected in the row that recorded it

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-221`'s named gap (*"bare broadcasts with no queue covering them"*), closed in `src/main/main.ts`.

**THE GAP, MADE REACHABLE BY `D-222`.** The secure crossing's delivery now fires **at its creation** — when **`BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` is EMPTY** — so `onAppStateChanged`/`onSecurityChanged`, **which broadcast to every window**, went **nowhere**. **The two callbacks now record their channel before the realm stands and send immediately after.**

**THE SHAPE, AND ITS THREE DELIBERATE CHOICES.** **TWO SETS AND NEVER ONE**: `IPC_MODULE_CHANGED` and `IPC_SECURITY_CHANGED` are **separate** entries, because **a window that missed one may not have missed the other**. **A SECOND FIRING BEFORE THE FLUSH IS ONE ENTRY** — the push is a **signal** and the read is the consumer's, so two held pushes would tell a realm nothing the first did not, **and the flag is what keeps the hold from growing with the app's age**. **`flush` SETS `armed` FIRST**, so a change delivered **during** the flush is **sent rather than re-held**, then sends the one pending entry, **then clears unconditionally** — a realm that reloads is owed **no second creation delivery**.

**AND THE ORDER IS THE PASS'S WHOLE CLAIM**: `markReady() → tabsDeliveries.arm() → viewDeliveries.arm() → moduleChanged.flush() → securityChanged.flush()`. **The two pushes are APPENDED** so **no existing arrival's order moves** (`D-220`'s tabs→view order byte-unmoved), **and they sit after `markReady()`** because **each push's consumer answers with a re-read over the backend's readiness gate** — a flush before it would hand the realm a signal whose read is not yet armed, **the same drop one step later**. **The rationale stands outside the handler body** because a row reads that body and the body must carry no exclusion token.

**THE PROOF, AND ITS LIMIT.** **No Electron window can be driven in this sandbox** (`app.whenReady()` never resolves; the main process traps, exit `133`), so the proof is the **landed 22 lines** extracted by brace-matching and **de-types** by the project's own esbuild: **`11/11`** — record-not-send, two pre-ready pushes are **one entry per channel**, a second flush sends **nothing more**, a post-ready push is **immediate**, an unfired channel sends **nothing**, a push **inside** the flush is sent, and the five-site `READY` order ascends. **That is a probe of the mechanism, not a boot of the app**, and the row says so.

**AND ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM `arm()`'s LETTER, NAMED.** `arm()` pushes **unconditionally** (a reloading realm is owed its delivery). **This flush sends only what is pending**, because **these two consumers each own a boot fill** — the reason `docs/L3/app-shell/delivery.md` §9 already records — **so `arm()`'s unconditional rationale does not transfer**, and the difference is stated rather than smoothed.

**THE MIS-CLASSIFICATION, CORRECTED WHERE IT HAPPENED.** `B-6` read **RED on three consecutive full runs**, and this seat was one step from calling it **a stable regression from this change** — it even ran the suite **with the change stashed** and found it green, which looked like proof. **A fourth run with the change in place is GREEN** (`2,958 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,960`). **So `B-6` is the `D-173` casualty class, not a regression** — **and its own instrument carried the evidence honestly**: the transport **bound**, the POST **arrived**, **no answer came**, and **the child was still running**. **That is the fifth distinct victim that class has had**, and **three consecutive reds was luck, not a signal** — which is exactly why `D-165`'s practice (a green needs a re-run) cuts both ways: **a red needs one too, and neither a single red nor three is a cause.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,958 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,960`** over **`145`** files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0** at **`364` gating sites in `48` files**; `refs` **0** (222 rows before this row); the demo rebuilt to **`40`** inputs. **The five broadcast-count rows (`AP-1`, `AP-4`, `SD-1`, `SD-4` and `settings-surface`'s four) were listed and left** — they are green as they stand, because a flush that sends only what is pending is the same count those rows already measure at the moments they drive.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-222`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records two bare broadcasts given a hold, an order chosen for what it protects rather than for what it enables, a proof that is a probe and says so, and a cause this seat nearly named wrong and corrected in the act of recording it.**

## D-224 — `AL-12` CLOSES `D-204`'S INSTRUMENT — **a gating row now reads a COMPUTED figure** — and it measured that the boot **IS no longer silent**: `D-216`'S *"the boot is silent"* is superseded by the delivery `D-220`/`D-222` put there

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `AL-12` (`tests/e2e/app-layout/app-layout.test.ts`, group `view`, five boots / twelve rows) and the reading it took on its first run.

**THE INSTRUMENT EXISTS AND IT GATES.** `D-204` named *"nothing gates a computed style"* as the project's highest-value missing instrument, because `D-203`'s defect — a `css.style` write whose value is an **object** answers `applied` and writes **nothing** — passed a fully green suite for months. **`AL-12` reads the carrier `D-214` built, and the row says in its own words what the split is: *the row reads the carrier; the TURN reads the computed style*.**

**WHAT IT MEASURES, IN ORDER.** **Before its own write** the carrier reads `top.height=64px; bottom.height=33px; pane-a.width=absent; pane-a.height=absent; pane-menus.width=140px; tabs-landing-page.display=block;`. **After `data.write(['zones','top','size'], 140)` and the listener's render** it reads **`top.height=140px`** — **the browser-applied figure** — and `tabs-landing-page.display=none` / `tabs-error-page.display=block` **against an authored `display: block` on both pages**, so **the record's `none` standing there is painted-from-record and never rendered-from-authored-CSS**. **A reversion to the object spelling leaves the carrier reporting the FILL (`396px` over a record's `140`), so it reds** — which is the row `D-203` should have had.

**RED-PROVEN.** On a byte-saved copy, clause 2 was made to expect the fill (`396px`); `-t 'AL-12'` answered `1 failed | 11 skipped` with `expected '140px' to be '396px'`, **`AL-12` alone**; restored byte-identically (sha256 identical both sides).

**AND IT SUPERSEDES A RULING BY MEASURING IT.** `D-216` said a cold boot shows the authored CSS *"until a listener speaks"*, and `D-217` said the boot's silence was a defect. **`AL-12` measures the boot now: the carrier is FULL at boot** — `pane-menus.width=140px`, the landing terminal's `display`, and the zones' authored figures alongside. **So `D-217`'s defect is CLOSED, and `D-216`'s *"the boot is silent"* describes a head that no longer exists.** **What remains true, and what `T-4` actually pins, is narrower and was always the right claim**: **the boot READ applies nothing** — `fill()` adopts and never applies — **while the boot's DELIVERY does.** **The read is not the listener, which is exactly `D-217`'s sentence; the listener now fires, and the paint is its turn.**

**THREE LIMITS THE ROW ITSELF NAMES.** **(i)** **`pane-a.width`/`height` read `absent`** — no authored element carries `pane-a` (its box is `gutter-card`; `D-194`'s mapping gap), so the stage pane's figures are **stated and unmeasured**. **(ii)** **A computed figure cannot distinguish the record's value from a fill that happens to equal it** — the row reads equality with the record, and `140` versus `396` is what makes the difference visible **here**. **(iii)** **The boot is not silent at this head**, so **clause 1 is `D-216`'s silence read as this row's own figure** rather than as an empty string — **its literal empty-string form is measurably false**, and the row says how it re-formed rather than pretending `D-216` still holds as written.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,959 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,961`** over **`145`** files (`+1` row for `AL-12`); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks` regenerated to **`365` gating sites in `48` files**; **the `app-layout` battery is `12` of `12`** and its five-boot teardown assertion held.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-223`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records the instrument the project was missing, a row that reds on the defect it was built for, and a ruling superseded by the fix that followed it — with the narrower claim that was true all along named beside it.**

## D-225 — THE PANE-NODE MAP LANDS AND **NEITHER NAME MOVES**: `pane-a`'s figures are measured for the first time, `AL-10` gains the arm that can catch a wrong-but-existing node, and the tree is green

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-224`'s last open item, designed at `docs/L3/renderer-wiring/design-pane-node-map.md` and landed as `M1`…`M4`.

**THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE DESIGN.** Renaming `gutter-pane` to `pane-a` — or re-keying the record — **would contradict a stated position** (`src/shared/view-shape.ts:135-139`, verbatim): *"**THE AUTHORED DOM PANE IS A DIFFERENT NAME** … **the store's family is keyed by the id the COMPOSITION addresses, and that is the rendering's business, not the address's.**"* **So the two names differ BY DESIGN, and the paint — which is the rendering — declares the correspondence**: `PANE_NODE_IDS`, **two explicit entries** (`pane-a → 'gutter-pane'`, `pane-menus → 'pane-menus'`), **both spelled even where the ids already match, because that equality is a MEASUREMENT and not a law.**

**AND THE LOOKUP'S MISSING ARM IS `null`, NEVER THE PANE ID.** **An identity fallback would be right once and would hand every undeclared id a route to a same-named element**; **a missing entry writes nothing to the DOM, resolves nothing, and states `pane-x.<member>=absent` at the RECORD's own key** — **a declared reading, never a silent skip**, and **no fifth word** (`D-174`).

**THE INSTRUMENT GAINED THE ARM THAT CAN CATCH A MAP THAT IS CONFIDENTLY WRONG.** **`AL-10` now spells `gutter-pane` in markup** — **its real instrument**, because **the write and the report share the map**, so **a wrong-but-existing node is invisible to the carrier**: the carrier would report a figure from the wrong element and call it right. **`AL-12` gained the `pane-a` carrier clause** and re-grained its quoted `absent` text; **its negative arm survives unmoved** — a computed figure still cannot separate the record's value from a fill.

**AND A SENTENCE TWO BLOCKS ABOVE THE NEW ENTRY HAD TO GO WITH IT.** `DECLARED_SCOPE`'s **`docs/L3/app-envelope/design.md` entry still called itself *"the last entry this union is owed"*** — **already two blocks stale**, and **`D-195`'s neighbour had read it through rather than reword it**. **It is now a dated reading of that page's one-offender moment at `D-174`'s head, naming the entries that followed, and stating that every pass writing a path RE-OPENS the union.** **A list that says it is finished and then grows teaches the next reader that its own claims are decorative.**

**A FALSE PARAGRAPH INSIDE THE CHANGED FUNCTION WAS DELETED WITH IT**: the one calling its pane arm *"INERT until `S-8` lands"* — **measured false since `D-206`**, and **it described the very function the pass was editing.**

**AND ONE OBLIGATION THE PAGE LEAVES OWED RATHER THAN MET**: **`PM-1`** — **a `tests/unit/renderer-wiring/` source probe of the map's totality** — **is named and not yet a path**, and **it will need its own `DECLARED_SCOPE` entry when it is written.** **The map's own completeness is therefore the one thing about it no row measures**: a third declared pane added without an entry would render nothing and report `absent` — **honest, and silent**.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,959 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,961`** over **`145`** files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; the `app-layout` battery **`12`/`12`**; the demo rebuilt to **`40`** inputs; `DECLARED_SCOPE` **`231` entries, `231` unique**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-224`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a rename refused by a stated position, a map whose miss is a declared absence, an instrument given the one arm that can catch a confident error, a finished-looking list corrected above its own new entry, and an obligation its page names rather than hides.**

## D-226 — `PM-1` MEASURES THE MAP'S **TOTALITY AND SPELLING** AND SAYS IT PROVES NOTHING ABOUT CORRECTNESS: the probe reads the wiring's bytes against a real import of the domain, reds on a deleted entry and on a planted pane, and leaves the one thing it cannot see named

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-225`'s owed `PM-1`, landed as **three rows in one unmarked gating file** (`tests/unit/renderer-wiring/pane-node-map.test.ts`).

**THE PROBE, AND WHY IT READS BYTES.** `PANE_NODE_IDS` is **private**, so the row **derives the map's `paneId`s from `renderer.ts`'s own text** and compares them against **a real import of `DECLARED_PANE_IDS`** — **pane by pane**, each declared id **asserted present by name**, each carried id **asserted declared by name**, **then the sets whole**. **Never a bare count** (`D-26`/`D-43`).

**THREE CLAUSES, EACH WITH ITS OWN REASON.** **`PM-1` totality** — **a third declared pane added without an entry reds it**, which is the silence `D-225` named. **`PM-2` spelling** — **every entry's `nodeId` must be a SPELLED LITERAL**, because **a derived id (`nodeId: paneId`, a template, string surgery, a node-side identifier) would put the correspondence where this probe cannot read it**; and **it also measures that the map is NOT the identity map**, which is the one thing the design says must never be assumed. **`PM-3` the control** — green on a fabricated **total** map, and **red on a fourth declared pane, an entry naming an undeclared pane, a DUPLICATED `paneId` (the red a set comparison cannot make), a derived node id, two empty sides, and prose masquerading as an entry.**

**RED-PROVEN TWICE AND BOTH RESTORED BYTE-IDENTICALLY.** **Deleting the `pane-menus` entry** reds **`PM-1` alone over the whole directory run** (`1 failed | 18 passed` of `19`; `PM-2`/`PM-3` green) with *"the pane `pane-menus` is declared by `DECLARED_PANE_IDS` and carried by an entry of `PANE_NODE_IDS`"*. **Planting `'pane-tabs'` in the domain** reds `PM-1` alone in-file. **Both files restored to their digests.**

**AND THE ROW SAYS WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, WHICH IS THE POINT.** **Totalty and spelling only — NEVER correctness.** **A wrong-but-existing node id is invisible here BY DESIGN**, because **the write and the report share the map** (`D-225` limit (ii)). **`AL-10`'s markup arm is the arm that catches that**, and **the row names it as the arm that does**, so no reader mistakes `PM-1` for a proof that the mapping is right. **That is the same discipline `D-210` needed** — **a row whose subject is narrower than its title must say so in its own words**, or a later reader will believe the wider claim.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,962 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** over **`146`** files (`+3` rows and `+1` file for the probe); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks` regenerated to **`368` gating sites in `49` files**; `refs` **0**. **One intermediate run carried `B-6` and the re-run was clean** — the casualty `D-223` classified, confirmed by its own re-run rule.

## D-227 — THE BOOT CASUALTY IS **STARVATION, NOT THE `dist/` WINDOW** — `D-173`'s two halves are **mutually incompatible as landed** (the shared build lock **livelocks**), and capping the fork pool takes the rate from **1 green in 4** to **2 in 3**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** the patch pass on `D-173`'s unfinished half, and four runs with no patch at all.

**FIRST, THE PATCH `D-173` ASKED FOR **CANNOT WORK AS DESIGNED**, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS A LIVELOCK.** `D-173` said *"move `artifactsWithin()` inside the lock"* **and** *"give the three builders one shared build lock"*. **The first half landed at `D-175`.** **The second half, written and measured, deadlocks the suite**: **a booter waits — INSIDE the lock — for artifacts only a build can produce, while the build waits for that same lock.** Measured on a `rm -rf dist` tree: **ten holds × `60 000 ms`, ZERO builds in `600 s`, the run killed.** **So the two halves are incompatible as landed**, and **the cure is booter-side** (release-and-retry around the artifact wait, or the booter building under its own lock). **The patch was reverted clean rather than kept.**

**AND `D-165`/`D-173`'S CAUSE IS REFUTED FOR THIS HEAD.** **On a pristine tree, `dist/main/main.mjs`'s mtime did not move in any run — no `npm run clean` ran at all — and the rate was THREE OF FOUR RED**: `B-6` twice (a `60.5 s` hang) and `AL-5` once (a `10 ms` paint race). **`B-6`'s own instrument says it plainly**: *"http transport ready on … /mcp"* → *"http POST /mcp"* → **no answer in `60 011 ms`, the child alive, the artifacts never rewritten**. **The `54 ms` window was a real measurement of a real race in `arrangement`'s harness; it is not what is failing now.**

**AND THE REMAINING CANDIDATE — STARVATION — IS CONFIRMED BY REDUCING IT.** `vitest.config.ts` set **no pool limit**, so the tree ran **146 files across 23 fork workers**; capping at **`maxForks: 8`** and re-running **three times on a clean tree gives TWO GREEN** (`2,962 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`) **against one in four before**. **The cost is nil**: the wall clock is unchanged (the green walls match baseline), because the booters' own host-wide lock already serialises the boots and the cap only stops the other 138 files from starving them.

**THE RESIDUAL IS TWO DIFFERENT ROWS WITH TWO DIFFERENT SHAPES, AND NEITHER IS THE `dist/` WINDOW.** **(i) `B-6`** — the HTTP `initialize` unanswered within `60 000 ms` **under load**, with the child alive and the transport bound; **its bound is the file's own ~720× the p95**, so this is a hang, not slowness, **and raising the bound would hide it**. **(ii) `AL-5`** — *"with the landing tab active the landing page must be SHOWN and the error page HIDDEN"* — reads the **stale** pair with **ONE bounded re-read**; under load one re-read is not enough, and **`AL-12` already shows the pattern that is**: a bounded dump loop. **So `AL-5`'s own instrument is under-sampled**, which is a row defect rather than a product defect — **the paint is right and the reading was early**, exactly the class `D-213` fixed for the receipts.

**WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM.** **The casualty is not eliminated**: two in three, not three in three. **`B-6`'s hang has no patch here**, and **the shared build lock needs a booter-side redesign before it can be taken at all** — both named rather than left implied. **And `D-165`'s practice still stands and now has a third reading behind it**: a single run — green *or* red — is not a rate.

**THE READINGS.** Three runs at the capped pool on a clean tree: **`2,962 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** twice and **`2,961`/`2,964`** once; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; the four uncapped baseline runs at the same head were **three red**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-226`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a fix that would have deadlocked the suite, a cause refuted on a tree where nothing was rebuilt, a cap that more than doubles the green rate for nothing, and two residuals whose shapes are a hang and an under-sampled read.**

## D-228 — THE DEADLOCK IS GONE BY CONSTRUCTION: **the booter builds under the lock it already holds**, so a build is never a second claimant — cold runs build **exactly once**, warm runs build **never**, and the wall clock matches baseline

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-227`'s cure shape **(2)**, landed across seven files.

**THE SHAPE, AND WHY IT CANNOT DEADLOCK.** Every boot hook now takes **`acquireLiveBoot` FIRST**, then calls **`ensureArtifacts()`**: **all artifacts present and non-empty ⇒ return with NO build**; **otherwise `npm run build` runs ONCE, in this process, under the lock it already holds**, then the set is **re-measured**. **A build that throws, or that exits zero without the set, raises an `Error` naming the command, the bound and the child's own stderr — never swallowed.** **`artifactsWithin` is gone.** **And the three in-suite builders take the same path** (`boot-contract`, `arrangement`, `emission` — their `beforeAll` is lock → ensure → release), **with the lock helper duplicated verbatim into them**, because the corpus's own rule is that the same `tmpdir()` derivation is what makes one contended path.

**SO THE CYCLE HAS NO SECOND EDGE TO FORM.** `D-227` measured the old shape as **hold-and-wait**: a booter holding the lock and waiting for `dist/`, against a builder waiting for the lock to make it — **10 holds × 60 s, zero builds in 600 s**. **There is now no party that wants the lock for a build's sake without already holding it**, **so no ordering rule, no release-and-retry and no second lock is needed**: the cure removed the claimant instead of sequencing it.

**MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH WAS THE POINT.**

| tree | builds | wall | deadlock |
|---|---|---|---|
| **COLD** (`rm -rf dist`), three runs | **exactly one per run** | 26 s / 70 s / 85 s | **none — no 60 s hold** |
| **WARM**, two runs | **zero** | **27 s** | — |

**The build count is evidenced, not asserted**: a **PATH `npm` shim logged every npm child** — **one `run build` and its one `run clean` per cold run, never two** — and **all four artifacts' mtimes landed inside the run's first second**, with builds starting **0.4–0.6 s after launch**. **The warm wall (27 s) matches a `HEAD` baseline measured by restoring the seven files (25.5 s / 26 s).** **And the 70/85 s cold runs are `B-6`'s own hang, not a lock wait** — the distinction `D-227` made, still holding.

**NO SECOND CLAIMANT REMAINS INSIDE `npm test`, AND THAT IS CHECKED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** All **seven** `npm run build` sites in `tests/` are **inside `ensureArtifacts`**, each reached only after `acquireLiveBoot`. **An injected-failure check** (a failing `npm` shim, cold tree, one booter file) **reds every row with the build's own stderr, leaves NO lock directory behind, and shows five boots taking the lock in turn rather than queueing.**

**AND THE RESIDUAL IS NAMED, NOT ABSORBED.** **`B-6`'s bind-and-answer hang — `D-227`'s residual (i) — reds in most runs at this head**, including two consecutive runs during this pass's own floor. **It is not the lock's subject and it is not fixed by this row.** **The lock work is measured complete**: cold builds once, warm builds never, no hold, no cycle. **What remains is a different defect with a different shape**, and the suite's green rate will not reach parity until it is taken.

**THE READINGS.** The last full run carried **`B-6` only**: **`2,961 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** over **`146`** files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; `refs` **0**; **`B-1` green with an empty offender list** after the two builder paths were declared **by their real locations** — **the pass corrected the brief's own quoted path** (`tests/integration/` where the file is `tests/unit/`), **and declared the real one because declaring the quoted one would have left `B-1` red**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-227`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a deadlock removed by deleting its second claimant, both directions measured with the build count evidenced by a shim, a wall clock matched to a restored baseline, and the one residual it does not touch named as a different defect.**

## D-229 — THE HANG WAS **A DOUBLE `listen()`, NOT A FLAKE** — `start()` is idempotent, `B-6` is green in every run, and the suite is **green three times running** for the first time in this unit's life

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** the `/proc` instrument `D-227`'s diagnosis produced, and the fix it pointed at.

**THE ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED.** **An http boot calls `start()` twice on one instance.** `settingsSurface.attach(mcp)` (`main.ts:896`) delivers the exclusion, whose `followExclusion` **binds the port**; then `main.ts:939`'s **`await mcp.start()` re-binds the same port** and fails `EADDRINUSE`. **With no `'error'` listener that was an uncaught exception, and the main thread PARKED** — measured: **alive, state `S`, `wchan` `poll_schedule_timeout.constprop.0`, ZERO CPU ticks over 200 ms, no stderr line after `http transport ready`, the POST never accepted.** **That is `B-6`'s signature exactly.**

**SO THE CASUALTY WAS A REAL DEFECT WEARING A FLAKE'S CLOTHES, AND THREE ROWS OF THIS SEAT WERE WRONG ABOUT IT.** **`D-165` called it a spawn race; `D-173` measured a `54 ms` `dist/` window** — a real race in `arrangement`'s harness, and **not this**; **`D-227` called it starvation** and capped the pool, which **helped the rate without touching the cause**. **All three were reasoning from an instrument that could not see the child**: **the app logs nothing between the POST and the answer**, so the only shape a trace could ever show was *"POST logged, no answer"* — **and that shape has many causes**. **The `/proc` sample is what distinguished them**: an **idle** child (state `S`, `poll`) is **waiting**, not working — and a waiting child that logged the POST had **never been given a request to answer**.

**THE FIX, AND NEITHER COMPOSITION CALL IS DELETED.** **`start()` is idempotent** (in `mcp-server.ts`, not the composition), because **both callers are right about their own subject**: **`attach` intends the RECORD's enable** — `D-123` makes the port the exclusion delivery's consequence — and **`await mcp.start()` intends the COMPOSITION's**, and **on `stdio` it is the only enable there is** (`followExclusion` refuses that transport). **So the fact judged — *is a socket bound* — is the instance's own.** **An enable already landed returns without touching the socket; an enable in flight is awaited through its own promise** so the boot still waits for the real bind; **`started` is written only by a successful bind and cleared by `close()`**, so **the re-open edge still binds**; **and a start after a FAILED bind re-attempts and re-rejects** rather than being swallowed by the guard. **Observed once**: a manual http boot prints **one** ready line, **zero** `EADDRINUSE`, **zero** `fatal`, and an `initialize` POST answers **`200`**.

**AND THREE MORE THINGS LANDED WITH IT, EACH BECAUSE THE DIAGNOSIS NEEDED IT.** **`readBody` is bounded at `5 s`** — answering **`408`** with a `-32004` error and a `method + url` line — **because a body that never completes is the other way to park this path**, and **5 s is far under the row's `60 s`** so the refusal arrives **before the row dies**. **`listen()` gained the `'error'` listener that REJECTS `start()` with the error's own text** — **and that listener is what exposed the double bind**: before it, the second bind was **an uncaught exception**, which is why the defect had never been named. **And the two under-sampled e2e reads were re-grained to sample the whole pair** (`AL-5`, then `AL-4`) — **assertions byte-identical**, zero cost when the first sample matches — **because a poll that returns on a stale sample reds a correct product.**

**THE READINGS, AND THIS IS THE FIRST RUN OF THREE GREENS THIS UNIT HAS HAD.** **`npm test` three consecutive times: `2,962 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** over **`146`** files, **exit `0` three times**; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; `refs` **0** (228 rows before this one); the demo bundle **current** at **`40`** inputs; **`B-6` green in every run at ~340 ms** (from a `60 s` hang) and **`B-6` alone green `9/9`**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-228`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a flake that was a defect, three rows that named three wrong causes and were each half right, the instrument that finally distinguished them, a guard placed where both callers stay correct, and a suite green three times running.**

## D-230 — THE TAB ROW BECOMES A TAB: the user looked at the running app and found the bar's rows **rendered and unstyled** — the element was always there, and nothing gave it a look

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"There's no tab row in the top-bar"* — and they were right about what they saw.

**THE ROW WAS IN THE BAR AND INVISIBLE AS A ROW.** Measured from the running app: the top-bar carries `display: flex; align-items: center; flex: 0 0 36px; app-region: drag` and holds its name plus **`#tab-rows`**, whose one minted **`.tab-row`** renders **`landing`** with **`active="true"`** — **and all three looked like nothing**, because **`#tab-rows` had only `-webkit-app-region: no-drag; width: env(titlebar-area-width, 100%)`**, the **minted row carried no `style` attribute at all**, and **the page stylesheet carried not one rule for `.top-bar` or `.tab-row`** — **while `.card`, `.btn`, `.counter-value` and `.layout` are all styled there.** **So beside the app name sat the bare word `landing`: a tab row with no tab in it.**

**THE FIX IS PRESENTATION ONLY, AND IT USES THE FILE'S OWN PRECEDENT.** **`.card`/`.btn` are authored provident nodes styled by class in this same stylesheet**, so **the element stays provident data and only its looks are page CSS**. **`.top-bar` adds only what the inline `topBarStyle` leaves open** — `box-sizing`, horizontal padding, background, bottom border, colour, `font-size` — **and never `display`/`flex`/`app-region` again**; **`#tab-rows`** gets `display: flex; align-items: center; gap; height: 100%; overflow: hidden` **with its inline `width` still authoritative**; **`.tab-row`** becomes a chip (padding, border, radius, background, `font-size`, `line-height`, `nowrap`, `cursor`, `user-select`, a transition and a hover state); **and `.tab-row[active="true"]` darkens the current tab.**

**AND THE ACTIVE RULE KEYS OFF THE PAINTED ATTRIBUTE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON IT CAN WORK.** **The paint writes `props.active` to the DOM as `active="true"`/`"false"` and CANNOT SET A CLASS** — **so a class rule would never fire**, and an attribute selector is the only lawful expression of "the record's active tab". **That distinction is stated in the comment**, because the next person to want a variant state will reach for a class first.

**NOTHING BUT PRESENTATION MOVED.** **No markup, no node, no `active`, no hook, no TypeScript, no test.** **`build` 0** with the rules copied into `dist/renderer/`; the `AL` battery **`12`**, the theme batteries **`58` + `10`**, all green **before and after**, because **no markup changed and the `AL` rows read the graph**.

**AND THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN BRIDGED: THE LOOK IS UNVERIFIED.** **Screenshotting is refused in this sandbox** — `import` and `spectacle` **cannot reach the X socket** — so **this pass verified the rules, the copy, the minted row and the batteries, and claims nothing about appearance**. **Whether it now LOOKS like a tab row is the user's judgement**, and **recording it as theirs is the difference between a measurement and a hope** — the class `D-213` named when a row was green because its instrument sampled the wrong thing.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,962 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** over **`146`** files; the app **live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`** with the styled bundle, its window armed, and **one `http transport ready` line** — the duplicate claim `D-229` left named is **gone at this head**.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-229`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a user seeing what an instrument could not, an element that was present and unpresented, a rule keyed off the one signal the paint can write, and a visual judgement left where it belongs.**

## D-231 — THE APP WAS MOUNTED INSIDE HAND-WRITTEN DEMO SCAFFOLDING, AND **A SCREENSHOT IS WHAT FOUND IT**: a UI-authority violation had shipped, been styled around, and passed every row

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** a screenshot of the running app, after which *"there's no tab row in the top-bar"* became a different and larger finding than the one `D-230` fixed.

**THE DEFECT, AND IT WAS IN THE SHELL'S OWN PAGE.** `src/renderer/index.html`'s `<body>` carried:

```html
<header><h1>Provident-Electron — MCP endpoint demo</h1><p>…</p></header>
<main class="layout">
  <div id="app" class="card"></div>
  <div id="panes"></div>
</main>
```

**So the app root rendered HALF the window width** (`grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr`), **inset by `.card`'s border, radius and padding and by `body`'s `1rem`**, **under a hand-written title and subtitle** — **and the top-bar's name wrapped onto two lines for want of room**, with the menus rendering as a vertical string of bare words. **Every one of those observations came from a screenshot; none of the suite's `364` gating sites could see any of it.**

**AND IT WAS A UI-AUTHORITY VIOLATION, WHICH `AGENTS.md` STATES AS A NON-NEGOTIABLE**: *"every element outside the Electron shell's own chrome is provident data … never hand-written DOM; an element rendered outside it is invisible to `provident.dispatch`, `get_rendered_html` and `get_markdown`."* **The `<header>` was exactly that** — two elements on screen that no agent could dispatch to, read, or markdown. **It had been there since the demo page and survived every pass**, because **the app never *looked* at itself**: the rows read the graph, and the graph was correct.

**WHAT WAS REMOVED, KEPT AND ADDED.** **Removed**: the header and its paragraph, `header h1`/`header p`/`.layout`, and the dark-pair line that existed only for the header. **Kept**: the `color-scheme: light` pin, `body`'s explicit `color` (its `padding` → `0`), `.card` (authored cards use it), and `D-230`'s `#tab-row` rule with its comment. **Added**: `#app { position: fixed; inset: 0 }` — **chosen over `width`/`height` because a fixed box leaves the document flow entirely, so no future page content can open a scroll range under the app** — plus **`.app-surface { height: 100% }`, the single declaration that makes the root's inline `display: flex; flex-direction: column` viewport-tall** and lets the stage's authored `flex: 1 1 0` be the remainder.

**`#panes` WAS KEPT WITH EVIDENCE AND NOT DELETED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERED.** It **is a real realm host**: `renderer.ts:1090` mounts `SecurePanels` on it and **both live legs read boxes inside it** (`panes-live`'s `P-3` requires a **non-zero** `[data-group]` box). **So it was taken out of the visual flow by `position: fixed; left: -10000px`** — **deliberately NOT `display: none` and NOT zero-size**, because either would have reddened the legs that need its box to be real. **A deletion would have looked right and broken a realm.**

**AND THE TWO PROPORTION DEFECTS THE SCREENSHOT SHOWED.** **`.top-bar` gained `white-space: nowrap` and the tabs box `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0`**, so **the row yields room instead of squeezing the name onto two lines** — the name is the node's `content` and cannot shrink gracefully. **`.menus-menu` became a compact bordered box whose name leads its items, and `.menu-item` an inline chip**, with **`.menu-item[disabled="true"]` greyed and struck through** — **keyed off the record's painted attribute for `D-230`'s reason: the paint cannot set a class.**

**THE LESSON THIS ROW EXISTS TO CARRY.** **Three rows in a row this seat reasoned about appearance from markup and got it wrong** — `D-230` found an unstyled row by *grepping a stylesheet*, and **this row found a UI-authority violation only because the user sent a picture**. **The suite cannot see the page's own scaffolding, because the page is not provident data** — **so the one class of defect the corpus's authority rule exists to forbid is also the one class no row can catch.** **A screenshot is the instrument for it, and this project had never taken one.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,960 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** with **two edit-set rows** (`F-9(b)` owner `gesture-session`, `I-12` owner `gutter-ui`) that clear on commit; `typecheck`/`typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; **every markup and CSS row green, the theme rows included** (`T-8`, `T-9`, `PRE-3`/`X-3`, and `X-5`'s one-match reading still **`1`**). **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`**, its `get_rendered_html` **now starts at the graph's root** with **zero `<header>`** and the only `<h1>` the authored landing page's own.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-230`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a non-negotiable violated in the shell's own page, a realm host spared by requiring evidence before deletion, and the admission that the instrument which found it was a person looking.**

## D-232 — THE FOUR THINGS THE USER FOUND BY LOOKING: dropdowns, a working Close for a **person**, a drag surface, and a handle — and the **singleton-lock trap** that looked like a regression

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"Convert the menu into dropdowns (only File, Edit, View, and Window should be visible by default, other dropdown vertically on click)"* · *"Close button doesn't close"* · *"No drag surface in top-bar"* · *"No reposition handle on menu pane"* — plus two rulings: **"A person's click works; an agent's dispatch stays refused"** and **"No — the app's bar is at the very top"**.

**1. THE DRAG WAS INERT FOR A MEASURABLE REASON.** `#tab-rows` carried `-webkit-app-region: no-drag` **and** `width: env(titlebar-area-width, 100%)` — **so a no-drag box blanketed the whole bar and Chromium had no draggable pixel left**, drag regions being computed as *elements with `drag`* **minus** *elements with `no-drag`*. **The fix moves `no-drag` from the CONTAINER to the CHIPS** — off `tabsRowStyle`, onto the row **prototype's `component.value.css`**, **whose copy is confirmed rather than assumed** (`translate.js:665-675` mints the prototype from `component.value.css`; `ops.js:477` builds each row as `css: fields.css ?? shape.css`). **`.top-bar` needed nothing**: its inline `drag` is authored and untouched.

**2. THE MENU PANE'S HANDLE WAS THERE AND INVISIBLE.** `#menus-vertical` is `#pane-menus`'s first child with `cursor: col-resize; width: 14px` — **exactly the design's "handle on the left side of a horizontal pane"** — and **`.gutter-handle` had no rule at all**. It is now a painted grip **with its box scoped to `#menus-vertical`**, because **`gutter-handle` is the SHARED class of `#gutter-horizontal`** and an absolute box on the class would have lifted the stage's strip out of its own row onto the window.

**3. THE MENUS ARE DROPDOWNS, AND THE STATE IS CSS BECAUSE THE PLATFORM ALREADY HAS ONE.** Each `menus-menu` gains **`props.tabindex: '0'`** and page CSS does the rest: `.menus-menu > .menu-item { display: none }`, `.menus-menu:focus-within > .menu-item { display: block; position: absolute; top: 100% }`. **A click focuses and a click elsewhere blurs, so `:focus-within` IS the click** — and **`tabindex` makes the name Tab-reachable, so a keyboard user gets the same gesture**. **ALL FOUR NAMES AND ALL EIGHTEEN ITEMS REMAIN IN THE MARKUP**: **the hiding is CSS, not deletion**, so `provident.dispatch` still reaches every item. **Two clip releases were needed and are stated as reasoning, not screenshots**: `overflow-x: auto` computes its other axis to `auto`, so `#pane-menus` and `#top` would clip the dropdown — released by `:has(.menus-menu:focus-within) { overflow: visible !important }`, which is the only way a sheet outranks an authored inline declaration.

**4. THE CLOSE ITEM NOW WORKS FOR A PERSON AND STAYS REFUSED FOR AN AGENT — THE USER'S RULING, MADE MECHANICAL.** `MENU_REFUSED_ROLES` (`quit`, `close`, `reload`, `forcereload`, `toggledevtools`, `minimize`, `zoom`) **still refuses every one of them on the MCP surface**, with **the message byte-unchanged**. **The distinguishing signal is `event.isTrusted`**, which Chromium sets **true only for real user input** and which **synthetic events can never set** — **so a trusted gesture is a person and an untrusted one is a machine, and that is a boundary rather than a convention.** **And the event site had to be found BEFORE implementing**: `runtime.ts`'s `handleDomEvent` **receives the real `Event` and DROPS it**, passing only a target value — **so `isTrusted` is nowhere in a body's scope** and the renderer's own item listener is equally empty. **Hence `preload.ts` — on the route, isolated world, already owning the channel — witnesses it** with a **capturing `window` click listener that records the clicked role only when `isTrusted === true`**, one-shot and cleared by `setTimeout(0)`, **handed to main as the channel's second argument**. **The declared bridge member stays `menu(role)`**: no new member, no new channel, **no lockstep move in `secure-panels.ts`**. **`menuRoleAnswer(role, trusted)` refuses the seven when `!trusted`; a trusted call falls through to the act switch; the eleven are untouched; a missing or malformed second argument is untrusted.** **Live evidence of the untrusted arm**: dispatching `close` answered `role-not-admitted` and the transport kept answering, while `copy` stayed admitted.

**AND THE DEBT IS NAMED: THE TRUSTED ARM IS UNEXERCISED BY ANY ROW.** **No row can produce a real `isTrusted` gesture, and a trusted `close` or `quit` would kill the very boot that measured it** — **so the seven's execution is evidence by code path only**: real click → preload capture → item listener → `menuRoleAct` → `menu()` → `invoke(…, true)` → `menuRoleAnswer(role, true)` → the act. **That is a row the corpus owes and cannot yet write.**

**AND A TRAP THAT COST TWO LAUNCHES AND LOOKED LIKE A REGRESSION.** After killing instances **by port**, two launches died with `Trace/breakpoint trap (core dumped)` **immediately after `http transport ready`** — **and this seat read it as the last commit breaking the boot.** **It was Chromium's SINGLETON LOCK**: a lingering child still held the shared `--user-data-dir`, and **a second instance on the same profile traps**. **A launch on a fresh profile boots to `renderer ready` and reports its four reads normally.** **The lesson is the session's own**: **`D-223` said a red needs a re-run, and this is the same rule for a *boot* — before calling a crash a regression, vary the one thing that is not the code.**

## D-233 — THE DROPDOWN GETS A PANEL AND THE ALREADY-ACTIVE TAB STOPS RE-MINTING — and the three defects that remain are **structural, with named causes**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** two screenshots and five reports — *"No background on dropdown"*, *"Clicking on the 'landing' button makes it disappear … expected behavior: clicking on landing makes it the focused tab if not already"*, *"Menu pane does not drag when clicking and dragging handle"*, *"Other drop zones (top, bottom, sidebars) do not exist or do not present or respond to drag if they do"*, *"Close/minimize/maximize buttons still do nothing"*.
