**FIXED (2) — THE CLICK ON THE ALREADY-ACTIVE TAB IS NOW A NO-OP, AND THAT WAS THE PERCEIVED DISAPPEARANCE.** **Measured first**: clicking the row answered `focus tabs-landing-page` and **re-minted it** (`node-225` → `node-249`) **with `active="true"` still set** — **so the record was never at fault; the DOM element was replaced on every click, and that churn is the only thing a person could perceive.** **The user's own sentence named the cure.** `focusActRoute` now **returns the committed reading when the resolved seat's row is already `active === true`**, skipping the write and the mint **while the act still answers its own word**, so a dispatcher sees no change. **Measured live**: the active click leaves **the node id unchanged and `lastActiveAt` frozen**; **a click at an inactive target still writes** (`243/244 → 268/269`, stamp advanced); **a repeat no-op stays put.** **And the stage cannot disagree**: one member decides both pages' `display`, and the only member `rowForSeat` would change on an already-active row is `lastActiveAt`, **which no stage reads**.

**AND `AL-4` HAD TO BE RE-GRAINED AGAINST ITS OWN OLD ARM.** **It asserted exactly the write and the churn the fix removes** — **so a gating row was pinning the defect the user reported.** **`(b)(i)` is now the no-op half** (ids and `lastActiveAt` frozen across **six samples**, `results` unchanged, **asserted positively rather than by dropping an assertion**) **and the write half moved to a seat the record shows NOT active**, where the stamp advances and the marker moves. **`AL-3` already clicked a non-active row and needed nothing.** **That is the third time this session a row had to be re-grained because its subject changed** — and the first where **a row was defending a defect**.

**THE THREE THAT REMAIN ARE STRUCTURAL, AND EACH HAS A CAUSE ALREADY MEASURED.** **(3) THE MENU PANE'S HANDLE DOES NOT DRAG** — **the gesture is wired to ONE element**: `elementForNodeId(GUTTER_AFFORDANCE_ID)` with `GESTURE_KEY = GUTTER_AFFORDANCE_ID`, i.e. **the stage's `#gutter-horizontal` alone**; **`#menus-vertical` carries an `axis` attribute and no gesture**, so the handle is painted and inert. **It needs a second gesture instance per handle — the machinery exists and is single-addressed.** **(4) THE ZONES DO NOT PRESENT** — **`driveLayoutRegions` writes a zone's fixed dimension only from `['zones', <id>, 'size']`, and `A ZONE STATING NO size IS WRITTEN NOTHING: no fallback, no default`** — **and NOTHING WRITES A SIZE**: `D-220` named it (*"no writer under `src/` states a `size`"*), **the `zones-must-stand` repair writes a memberless record**, **so the four zones are invisible by design until the record states one.** **The fix is a WRITER — the zone repair should repair a default `size` exactly as `panes-must-stand` repairs a pane's geometry** — **and it is a view-record change, not a styling one.** **(5) THE OVERLAY BUTTONS ARE INERT** — the min/max/close at the bar's right are the `titleBarOverlay` controls, **drawn and unresponsive**; **the app can stop depending on them**: `minimize` and `close` are two of the seven roles the trusted-click path `D-232` built **can now execute for a person**, **so the app could draw its own three controls as provident nodes** — **but `maximize` is not in the menu-role vocabulary (`zoom` is macOS's), so that route needs a role the corpus does not have.**

## D-234 — THE ZONES PRESENT: **a stated default size per zone**, repaired at the root and carried, proven on two cold profiles — and the paint's own cost is **routed rather than hidden**: the zones now lose their authored scroll

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-233`'s item 4, and the user's *"Other drop zones (top, bottom, sidebars) do not exist or do not present"*.

**THE GAP WAS A WRITER'S, NOT A PAINTER'S.** `driveLayoutRegions` writes a zone's fixed dimension **only** from `['zones', <id>, 'size']`, and **"a zone stating no `size` is written nothing: no fallback, no default"** — **while the `zones-must-stand` repair AND the cold-profile placeholder both wrote a MEMBERLESS record**, so a cold profile had **four invisible strips**. **`panes-must-stand` had always done the analogous job for panes; the zones never got it.**

**`DEFAULT_ZONE_SIZES` NOW STANDS AS THE ONE SOURCE** in `view-shape.ts`: **`top` 140 and `bottom` 60 as HEIGHTS, `left` 120 and `right` 90 as WIDTHS** — **the figures an instrument probe measured this session, kept unchanged**: **200 and 210 leave the stage the remainder**, and **every figure is positive enough to see and to press** (the envelope's own `14px`-handle argument). **The repair triggers at the family ROOT only** — the registration instant, a write **AT** `['zones']`, or a whole-family landing — **when the family stands and admits but a declared zone states no finite non-negative size**; **it REPLACES whole and carries every zone that states its own figure**, so **a caller's custom `240` and even a `0` minimize marker survive**, and **a write AT or BELOW a zone id is never repaired** (`D-151` H4's scalar hand-out kept). **The placeholder states the same four and `repairZones` builds from it, so the two cannot drift**; **`zoneIn` still answers no default of its own.**

**PROVEN TWICE ON COLD PROFILES.** Four style strings — **`height: 140px`, `height: 60px`, `width: 120px`, `width: 90px`** — **and a second, separate fresh profile rendering the identical four**, so **the placeholder path states them and no carried state does** (the profile file carries no `zones` key). **The carrier reads all four** beside the panes.

**AND THE PAINT'S COST IS ROUTED, NOT HIDDEN.** **`paintStyle` REPLACES `css.style` whole**, so **the zones' authored `overflow-x`/`overflow-y` does NOT survive** — **the zones now render and lose their own scroll**, which the design requires. **That is the same collision class as the gutter's authored flex (`D-225`'s routed finding), and it belongs to `app-envelope`'s `paintStyle`, not here.** **A zone that renders without scrolling is better than a zone that does not render — and neither is the design.**

**SEVENTEEN ROWS OWED RE-GRAINING, ALL SEVENTEEN LANDED, NONE RETIRED, NONE WEAKENED.** **The size-less zone is still constructible BELOW the root** — `data.write(['zones','bottom'], {})` commits because a write at a zone id is never repaired — **so the state those rows pinned survives and MOVED rather than leaving.** **`AL-10` WAS NOT FLIPPED**: its control is now **two arms**, each zone carrying **the record's own `size`** on the axis that zone fixes, **and the paint's no-default arm still reached and proven through the carrier** — one zone cleared, its figure leaving the carrier while its sibling stays measured, the figure returning on restore. **Its MARKUP half is named DEBT**: after the clear the attribute still read `height: 33px`, **because the paint has no clearing arm**, so rendered HTML cannot separate a stale figure from a painted one.

## D-235 — THE UI STOPPED LYING: **the seven are un-greyed** because they work for a person, the mark now **vetoes at both layers**, and `AL-6`/`AL-7` were re-grained **off the paint onto the act**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"New issue, clicking on the greyed out options makes app nonresponsive"* — and the ruling *"Un-grey them — they work for a person, so show them enabled"*.

**THE BUG WAS A CONTRADICTION THIS SEAT INTRODUCED, AND IT HAD TWO HALVES.** **`disabled` on a `div` DOES NOTHING** — it is a form-control attribute — **so the seven items were STYLED disabled and still clickable**; **a real click is `isTrusted === true`**, so **`D-232`'s trusted path executed them**: **`Reload`/`Force Reload` reload the renderer** (which a person reads as a freeze), **`Toggle Developer Tools` opens devtools, `Minimize` minimises, `Close` closes, `Quit` quits.** **The record marked those roles `disabled` as an AGENT-SAFETY signal, and the trusted path made them live for a person** — **the UI had been lying about what it would do**, and the lie only became reachable when the trusted path landed.

**THE CHANGE, AND IT WAS SEVEN LINES BECAUSE THE MARKING WAS PER-NODE.** The `disabled` member was authored **literally on seven `props` entries with no set behind them** — **so the seven members are gone** and **nothing else moved**: **eighteen roles, eighteen labels, four menus, the eleven and their acts untouched, and `MENU_REFUSED_ROLES` with the agent's refusal answer BYTE-IDENTICAL** — **dispatching `close` still answers `role-not-admitted` in the same sentence, and the transport keeps answering.**

**AND THE MARK NOW VETOES AT BOTH LAYERS, SO THE CONTRADICTION CANNOT RECUR.** **The item's click listener returns before the act when the mark is present**, **and `preload`'s capturing witness records no gesture for a marked element** — **so a marked control can never earn `trusted`.** **Both layers matter**: the first stops the act, **the second stops the *permission*, which is the half that had made a styled-dead control live.**

**THE SAFETY REVIEW THE USER ASKED NOTHING FOR AND THE ROW OWES ANYWAY — WHAT A PERSON NOW GETS, ROLE BY ROLE.** **`Reload`** re-boots the renderer realm and **its graph re-mints** (fresh node ids; transient counter, receipt and drag state gone) **while main's record survives** — panes, tabs and theme re-read at boot, zone sizes from the repaired defaults. **`Force Reload`** the same, cache bypassed. **`Toggle Developer Tools`** opens devtools. **`Minimize`** minimises. **`Zoom`** toggles the **MAXIMISED** window state on Linux — **not page zoom**, which is the eleven's `Zoom In`/`Zoom Out`/`Actual Size`. **`Close`** closes the window and, being the only window, **quits**. **`Quit`** quits.

**AND THE TWO ROWS THAT BROKE WERE THE TWO THAT WERE WEAKEST.** **`AL-6` and `AL-7` derived their "refused" set from `item.disabled` in the markup** — **so they measured the PAINT, not the REFUSAL**, and **would have agreed with a mark that lied**, which is exactly what the last hour produced. **Both now DISPATCH ALL EIGHTEEN at each item's own `data-node-id` and split on the route's own answer** — `admitted <role>` for the eleven, **the seven's sentence byte-for-byte** for the seven — **with the mark's absence, the eighteen-role census and the shape kept STRUCTURAL and said so, because the census is the address book** (an unaddressable item could not be dispatched at all). **The rows got stronger by losing the thing they trusted.**

## D-237 — `Close` WAS TWO DEFECTS AND ONE OF THEM WAS **THE HARNESS**: the reply never settled when the act destroyed its own caller, and **`--in-process-gpu` made `quit` never exit** — so the window that "would not close" was partly this session's own launch flag

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"Close currently doesn't close the window, the window becomes unresponsive"* — **a correction of the reading `D-236` accepted**, and the reason `D-236` documented a behaviour that was not happening.

**THE PROBE REFUTED THIS SEAT'S OWN HYPOTHESIS AND FOUND THE REAL ONE.** **A window destroyed synchronously inside `ipcMain.handle` does NOT hang the app** — **it closes and the process exits `0`** — **but the caller's `invoke` reply NEVER SETTLES (`0` of `3` runs)**, **so a person's click is answered by nothing, and the window they were told would close appears to freeze instead.** **That is why `D-236` documented `Close` as working: the act fired; the confirmation never came.**

**AND THE DEFERRAL WAS MEASURED ARM BY ARM RATHER THAN CHOSEN.** `queueMicrotask` **`0/3`**, `setImmediate` **`1/3`**, **`setTimeout(…, 0)` `3/3`**, `setTimeout(…, 50)` `3/3`. **The lost race is exactly the process-boundary crossing the reply has to make** — **a microtask cannot yield to it, and `setImmediate` fires in the same loop iteration and loses it two times in three.** **One timer turn is the smallest reliable thing.** **`close` and `quit` are the only acts moved**; `reload`, `forcereload`, `toggledevtools`, `minimize`, `zoom`, `togglefullscreen` and the eleven were **each probed and left synchronous because their replies settle.** **The act is unconditional, so a lost race costs the receipt and never the act** — **and its cost is stated in the code**: those two answer `admitted` **before** acting, so **their failure can no longer be a refusal**; it is said on main's console, **and the vocabulary keeps its three words.**

**AND THE SECOND CAUSE WAS THIS SESSION'S OWN LAUNCH FLAG.** **With `--in-process-gpu` — which every launch this seat has made carried, because an early probe needed it — the app reaches `quit` and its process NEVER EXITS.** **That is exactly what "the window will not close" looks like**, and **it is not the app**: **without the flag it boots normally and the process can exit.** **So the symptom had two causes — a lost reply and a harness flag — and the flag was invisible because it had been constant for hours.** **The lesson is `D-223`'s and `D-232`'s a third time**: **a constant in the environment is indistinguishable from a property of the code, and the way to tell them apart is to vary it.**

**WHAT DID NOT MOVE.** `MENU_REFUSED_ROLES` is **untouched in the diff**, and **the agent's refusal is byte-identical**: dispatching `close` and `quit` still answers `role-not-admitted` with the same sentence, `copy` still answers `admitted`, and the transport keeps answering. **`D-236`'s fork notes stand unchanged** — **the one sentence the fix made false was in the act switch, not the notes** (*"`quit` AND `close` END WHAT THEY END BEFORE THIS CALL RETURNS"*), and it is replaced.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,962 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** over **`146`** files, **zero reds**, identical to `D-236`'s head; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; **one file changed** (`src/main/main.ts`). **The probe lives at `/tmp/menu-close-probe`.** **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`, relaunched WITHOUT `--in-process-gpu`.**

**THE RESIDUAL, NAMED**: **the end-to-end TRUSTED click is still unexercised** — an OS-level XTest clicker did not reach the window under this Wayland session, **so the trusted arm needs the user's hand**, and **that has now been true for two rows.**

## D-238 — THE MENUS PANE'S HANDLE DRAGS: the gesture is **generalised from one element to a declaration list**, the second handle costs one line, and **a latent NaN bound would have made it inert even with the gesture wired**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-233`'s item 3, and the user's *"Menu pane does not drag when clicking and dragging handle"*.

**THE DEFECT WAS SINGLE-ADDRESSING, AND ONE LAYER UNDER IT WAS A NaN.** **The gesture was wired to `elementForNodeId(GUTTER_AFFORDANCE_ID)` with `GESTURE_KEY = GUTTER_AFFORDANCE_ID`** — **the stage's `#gutter-horizontal` alone** — so **`#menus-vertical`, visible since `D-232` painted it, was inert.** **And wiring it would NOT have been enough**: **`pane-menus` stores no `bounds`**, so **`paneBoundsOf` answered `undefined`, `clampToBounds` turned it into `NaN`, and EVERY MOVE WAS INVALID.** **`readPaneBounds`' `undefined` arm now answers the measured pair it already computed for its other degradation arms**, with **a stored pair still winning verbatim** — **a fix that had to be found rather than assumed**, because **the handle would have looked wired and stayed dead.**

**THE SHAPE: `PANE_DRAG_HANDLES`**, a module-scope readonly list of **`{handleId, paneId, sign}`** looked up the `PANE_NODE_IDS` way, **with `startGutterAffordance` iterating it over the ONE session and the ONE `createPaneDrag`** — **so the call-site count stays `2`, there is no second gesture copy, and a third handle is one line.** **The axis member is deliberately NOT declared** and **stays the record's own zone selection** (`adjustableMemberNameOf`), **so the list cannot disagree with the design's orthogonal-axis rule.**

**AND THE SIGN IS ONE COEFFICIENT, BECAUSE THE TWO HANDLES SIT OPPOSITE.** **The stage's grip is at the TOP-RIGHT and grows the pane as it moves right/down; the menus grip is at the LEFT, so dragging right must SHRINK it.** **One mapping, negated for `sign: -1`.**

**AND `PS-1` WAS RE-GRAINED STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN TO A NEW LITERAL.** **Its subject is now *"every DECLARED handle is resolvable, and the declaration is the envelope's"*** — **derived from the wiring's own per-entry reading, with no handle id spelled in the row** — **because a three-item list needs editing per handle, and a row edited per handle is edited carelessly.** **The harness now answers an element double for every id the envelope authors**, so **"resolved to nothing" becomes a reading rather than an absence.** **And it was PROVED RED TWICE on plants restored byte-identically** — a handle answering `null` reds by name, and a truncated census side reds the census.

## D-239 — THE BAR STOPS CROWDING AND THE UI CAN ADD TABS: the row's **width claim is deleted** so flex computes the remainder, and a `+` control is authored **beside** the row set because **a mint replaces it**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"narrowing the window until the title and window buttons crowd over the tab row doesn't cause a scroll"* · *"I don't see a way to add new tabs in the ui"*.

**THE CROWDING WAS TWO WIDTH CLAIMS FIGHTING, AND THE LOSER WAS THE NAME.** **`#tab-rows` carried an inline `width: env(titlebar-area-width, 100%)` AND page CSS `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0`** — **and an explicit `width` becomes the flex BASE SIZE**, so **the row claimed the whole free area and the name was left fighting for the remainder**, overflowing rather than yielding. **THE FIX DELETES THE WIDTH CLAIM ENTIRELY** (`tabsRowStyle` and the row's `css.style` are gone; **the node now renders with no `style` attribute**), **because the charter says the tabs row occupies *the space in between* — which flex computes exactly, where `env()` was only a proxy.**

**AND THE `env()` CLAIM DOES NOT FULLY HOLD, WHICH IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `titleBarOverlay` draws the platform's controls **over the strip's right end** and `getTitlebarAreaRect()` answers **`x: 0`**, **so the row's remainder ends UNDER those controls at extreme narrowness** — **a design item, deliberately not patched here**, and **the old width never reserved them either.**

**THE NAME IS FIXED WITHOUT A SELECTOR, AND THAT TOOK FINDING A LANGUAGE FACT.** **A text run is an ANONYMOUS flex item** — **no selector reaches it** (`:first-child` matches `#tab-rows`; `::first-letter` styles a glyph) — **so `flex: 0 0 auto` on the name is achieved through the BAR's `white-space: nowrap`**: **with `nowrap` the run's min-content IS its whole width, so its automatic minimum clamps its shrink to zero while grow stays `0` and basis stays `auto`.** **`#tab-rows` keeps `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto` and is the one box that yields** — **which is what the user asked for two turns ago.**

**THE `+` LIVES BESIDE THE ROW SET, AND THE MINT IS WHY.** **`driveTabsRows` MINTS into `#tab-rows`, and a mint REPLACES that row set** (`D-201`'s shape) — **so a control authored inside it would be wiped, and one minted as a datum would be a tab.** **`#tab-add` is authored as the row's FOLLOWING SIBLING**, carrying **its own `css.id`/`props.id`, a `+` label, `app-region: no-drag` and a `handlers` entry**, with **`startAddTab` following the menus' path exactly** — census by `props.id`, **one `state-slice` replacing `handlers` under the same pair with a live closure**, and the DOM click. **No channel, no bridge member.**

**AND ITS TARGET MUST DIFFER, NEVER THE ID.** **`seatOf` mints `tab-<n>` from `order.length`** and **the act is untouched**; **`newTabTargetOf` derives the first `untitled-<n>` that no row's `target` carries and that this realm did not just hand**, **so a double press cannot open two rows sharing a target** — **the corpus had measured that a repeated target seats the existing row and writes nothing.**

**MEASURED LIVE**: rows **1 → 2** on a press, the new row `target=untitled-1` and `active`, `dispatch` answering `add tab`, **a second press reaching 3** with `untitled-2` and the record's `order` carrying both. **AND THE NEW TAB'S PAGE IS EMPTY** — **the new row is active but is not the landing entry, so both authored terminals are `display: none`** — **and the placeholder is OWED by the envelope and L2 rather than invented at L4.**

**THE CENSUS MOVED BY EXACTLY THE ONE NODE AND WAS RE-GRAINED AS ITS OWN TERM.** **`74 = 18 + 5 + 2 + 13 + 35 + 1`** — **the `+` is a FIFTH DECLARED TERM named *"the add-tab control (`tab-add`)"***, **NOT folded into the fourth term's `34`**: **every term is one landing's own declared bill, and absorbing it elsewhere would restate another layer's count to hide a mover this pass authored** (`D-26`/`D-43`). **The walk was re-taken off the tree** (top-bar `2 → 3`, `app-surface` `60 → 61`), **the closed-list prose was reopened** (*"the four terms sum to the figure"* → five terms and `74`), **and an identity row was added** so a duplicate `tab-add` reds. **Eleven of twelve expressions red if a second authored node arrives without the census being re-taken** — **which is the property those rows exist for.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,960 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** with **only the two worktree rows** (`F-9(b)`, `I-12`) red before the commit; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; **`theme-control` `61`/`61`**, `theme` + `app-layout` **`70`/`70`**; the demo rebuilt. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`**, `#tab-rows` with no `style` at all and `#tab-add` beside it.

**AND ONE STALE FIELD IS NAMED, NOT PATCHED**: **`strata/modules.json`'s `app-envelope` row still reads `endpoints: 19`** while this adds the twenty-first published name — **its owner re-takes it (`D-41`/`D-26`)**, and **nothing in `npm test` reads that field.**

## D-240 — THE BAR RESERVES THE CONTROL STRIP **AND THE NAME YIELDS**: `env(titlebar-area-width)` belongs on the **bar**, not the row — and the only lever that lets an anonymous text run shrink is `white-space`, measured three ways

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"Scroll happens only after the tab row is covered by the buttons"* — with a screenshot of a 249px window showing the name and the platform's controls crowding over the bar and the chips squeezed to nothing.

**THE `env()` WAS IN THE WRONG ELEMENT FOR TWO ROWS.** `D-239` **deleted** the row's `width: env(titlebar-area-width, 100%)` so flex could compute the remainder — **right** — **and never moved that claim to the element that should hold it**, so **the bar's content ran to the window's edge underneath the controls**. **`getTitlebarAreaRect()` had been saying it all along: `{x: 0, width: 607}` on a 720-wide window, `607 = 720 − 113`** — **`env(titlebar-area-width)` IS the free area with the controls excluded**, and **this seat read past it twice.**

**THE FIX IS ONE DECLARATION, AND `box-sizing` IS WHY IT WORKS.** **`.top-bar { width: env(titlebar-area-width, 100%); box-sizing: border-box }`** — **`border-box` is not decoration**: **the bar's authored padding is `24px`, and without it the border box would be `env()` PLUS its padding and would overrun the free area again by 1.5rem.**

**MEASURED IN A REAL RENDERER OVER CDP** — because **the app's own endpoint grants eight tools and no `eval`, so a computed style is not readable from it** — **and with `window.resizeTo` on the actual window, since Electron's CDP has no `Browser.setWindowBounds` and emulation does not move `env()`.**

| window | bar = `env(...)` | name | row client / scroll | `+` vs free area |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 980 | 867 | 117.78 | 677 / 677 | **855 ≤ 867 ✓** |
| 560 | 447 | 70.34 | 305 / 510 | **435 ≤ 447 ✓** |
| 420 | 307 | 65.66 | 169 / 510 | **295 ≤ 307 ✓** |
| 300 | 187 | 65.66 | 49 / 510 | **175 ≤ 187 ✓** |
| 249 | 136 | 65.66 | **0** / 510 | **125.66 ≤ 136 ✓** |

**AND THE RESIDUAL WAS THE NAME, SO THE NAME HAD TO YIELD — MEASURED FOUR WAYS.** **At 249 the name run alone was `118px` plus `24px` padding = `142` against a `136px` free area**, so **the row computed zero and the `+` sat under the controls again.** **The name is an ANONYMOUS flex item and `nowrap` made its min-content its whole width, so it could not shrink.** **The levers were tested, not chosen**: **`white-space: normal` drops the run's automatic minimum from its max-content `117.78` to its MIN-CONTENT `65.66` at the hyphen the name carries**, so **it yields first and wraps to two lines inside the 36px strip**; **`overflow: hidden`/`clip` alone does NOT zero an anonymous item's automatic minimum** (name stayed `117.78`, `+` stayed `154..178`); **`min-width: 0` on the bar did nothing**; and **the ellipsis is simply UNAVAILABLE** — **the run's own `overflow` is unreachable, and on the bar `text-overflow` has no other landing place, since the chips and the `+` are element flex items and never inline content** — **so it was removed rather than left dead.** **And a `ch` `max-width` "on the bar's first content" is not expressible without a selector**, which is the same finding as `D-239`'s.

**THE RESIDUAL, STATED**: **below a free area of about `126px` — roughly a `238px` window — one hyphen-piece plus the fixed `72px` of padding, gaps and the `+` exceeds the bar**, and **there the bar clips at its own right edge instead of painting under the controls** — **a clip is the honest failure, because it cannot hide a control the user needs.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,960 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,964`** with **only the two dirty-tree edit-set rows** (`I-12`, `F-9(b)`) red before the commit, **both reading `170`/`170` with the file stashed**; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-239`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records an `env()` finally placed on the element that owns it, a border-box that is load-bearing rather than decorative, four measured levers of which three are dead, and a failure mode chosen because it cannot hide a control.**
## D-241 — THE NAME BECOMES A NODE, THE `+` STOPS BREAKING RENDERING, AND A NEW TAB LANDS ON THE LANDING PAGE — with the real blocker being **the terminal's key**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"'+' button causes the tabs row and stage to stop rendering until it is reloaded"* · *"The new tab should be coerced to the landing-page content by repair if it isn't seeded with any"* · *"The overflow also causes the title to switch to two lines"* — and the ruling ***"Make the name an element so it can truncate."***

**1. THE NAME IS A NODE, AND `D-177` IS SUPERSEDED FOR IT.** **A text run is an anonymous flex item no selector can reach** — so the name **could only wrap (the two lines the user reported) or overflow**. **`#app-name` is now a `span` carrying its `css.id`, `props.id` and the string and NOTHING ELSE**, **the bar's FIRST child so the order (name, row, `+`) is unchanged**, with **`flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`** — **and the bar's `white-space: normal` removed with the run it existed for.** **MEASURED IN A LIVE RENDERER**: at a **452px** window the name box is **`80px` against `scrollWidth 118` at `19px` height — ONE LINE, truncating**; `45px` at 332 and `30px` at 281, **always one line, the row still scrolling and the `+` still inside the bar.**

**2. THE `+` BUG WAS FOUND BY MUTATIONOBSERVER, AND IT WAS NONE OF THE THREE SUSPECTS.** **A press left `#tab-rows` EMPTY and rendered every fresh row as a child of the MOUNT ROOT.** **The mechanism**: **`Runtime.applyCommand` re-compiles the mint's `dirtied` set each focused on itself**, so **the rows' focused states are written LAST and the render emits them at the root** — **while the boot row is placed by the full bootstrap compile**, **which is exactly why it looked like *"until it is reloaded"*.** **The mint answered `applied`, threw nothing, and the pages' drive still ran** — **so all three guesses (a clobbering `state-slice`, a throwing mint, a swallowed throw) were wrong.** **THE FIX**: **one settle `state-slice` on `tab-rows` re-asserting its authored `props.id` after the mint**, **which re-compiles the row node's state and carries its family children**; **a plain re-emit (`bootstrap()`) was tried first and MEASURED INSUFFICIENT.** **The engine half is recorded upstream-owned** (`D-5`).

**3. THE LANDING REPAIR, AND WHERE IT CAN LAWFULLY LIVE.** **A `committed` delivery whose ACTIVE row's `target` is this realm's own `untitled-<n>` placeholder writes the row WHOLE with `target: TABS_LANDING_PAGE_ID` through the existing data route** — **so THE RECORD changes and the repair converges.** **It lives in the RENDERER because the record cannot know which pages are authored** — that is the envelope's, in this realm. **And a `provident.focus` tab with a caller's unknown target KEEPS IT, unrepaired** — **the wider "resolves no page" key was measured to red gating e2e `F-1`** (which asserts `/delta` is carried), **so the app's own no-seed marker is the key.**

**4. AND THE REAL BLOCKER WAS THE TERMINAL'S KEY, WHICH THE PASS NAMED ITSELF.** **With the target coerced, both terminals STILL read `display: none`** — **because `deriveTabsWitness` compared the ACTIVE ROW'S ID to `TABS_LANDING_ENTRY_ID`**, **and a coerced tab's id is `tab-2`.** **It now reads `activeRows.length === 1 && activeRows[0].target === TABS_LANDING_PAGE_ID`** — **`D-210`'s independence survives because it reads a DIFFERENT ROW MEMBER (the content pointer) against a constant the ENVELOPE authors**, **and its false arms (`/delta`, the error page, a pre-coercion `untitled-n`, no active row) stand.** **LIVE PROOF: after a `+` press the landing terminal reads `display: block` where it read `none`.**

**5. FOUR ROWS AND A CENSUS MOVED, ALL RE-GRAINED, NONE WEAKENED.** **`AL-1`** now asserts **the name as its own node, the bar's text run empty, and `childIdsOf(top-bar) == ['app-name','tab-rows','tab-add']`** (depth-counted, so minted chips are not siblings). **The census reads `75 = 18 + 5 + 2 + 13 + 35 + 1 + 1`** — **`app-name` as its own sixth named term, never folded into another layer's count** — **with the walk re-taken (`top-bar 3 → 4`, `app-surface 61 → 62`) and the closed-list prose reopened.** **And five fixtures** (`DC-5`, `TC-1`, `TC-2`, `TC-11`, `TC-12`) **pinned the OLD id key with made-up targets** — **all re-grained to the target key, importing the constant, one `landingRow` helper so the four cannot disagree.**

## D-242 — THE BACKWARDS SWITCH: `exactly-one-active`'s `written` referent came from **an order-sensitive `JSON.stringify` diff**, so it kept the **last** active row in `order` instead of the row the act named — and `D-211`, deferred for a hundred rows, was finally taken

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"clicking on any tab (including the currently active one) switches the active tab to the landing"* — which the previous row partly cured, **and which then exposed `D-211` as the remaining defect**: **clicking an EARLIER chip does not switch, while a forward click does.**

**THE CAUSE, CONFIRMED FROM THE BYTES.** **`written` was derived by a `JSON.stringify` diff** — **`pre` being `read()`'s PROJECTED rows** (`rowOf`'s fixed order `id, target, active, [error], label, lastActiveAt`) **against `viewOf`'s RAW store rows** (a `+`-minted row stores **`{id, target, active, lastActiveAt, label}` — `label` LAST**, and `rowForSeat`'s open arm writes no `label` at all while the seat heal appends it). **`JSON.stringify` is order-sensitive — the module's own `canonicalRecord` says so in words: *"MEMBER ORDER IS NOT PART OF THE RECORD … `JSON.stringify` is order-sensitive"*.** **So an UNCHANGED row matched spuriously, the loop OVERWROTE `written` at every match, and `written` became the LAST ACTIVE ROW IN `order`** — **then `healedFamily` kept that as its survivor and rewrote the caller's row back to `active: false`.** **A FORWARD switch worked only because the genuinely-changed row happened to be last in `order`.**

**THE FIX, AND THE FIRST PART IS THE WHOLE OF IT.** **The body HAD the act and threw it away** (`void context`), so **`exactlyOneActive` is now UNWRAPPED** — **the kernel's `{address, op, tier, value}` reaches it and `written = address[1]`** under **`deeperThanRecord(address)` plus a row-still-held guard**, **which is exactly what the constraint's own docblock already claimed: *"THE CALLER'S OWN WRITTEN REFERENT"*.** **The root-address diff is kept but CANONICALISED through `canonicalRow`** — **the one row projection `canonicalRecord` already uses** — **so member order can no longer match a row nobody wrote.** **And `read()` stores `lastView` from `viewOf`**, so **the module's memory is one spelling of the record rather than two.** **NOT a two-row act and NOT a second activeness authority: the repair already cleared the other row — only its SURVIVOR was wrong.**

**AND THE CORPUS WAS MISSING THE ROW THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT.** **No gating row drove a BACKWARD switch** — **`AL-4` avoided the direction and `AL-3` pinned only a forward move** — **so a defect that inverted half the act's cases had no instrument.** **The new row writes two rows, activates the LATER one the way the app writes a new tab (`rowForSeat`'s open arm, whose stored member order is what tripped the diff), then LEAF-WRITES THE EARLIER one**, asserting **the earlier `active`, the later `inactive`, and exactly one active.** **And it was PROVED RED TWICE on the pre-fix build** — **once by restoring the module byte-identically, once live** — **so neither the row nor the measurement is vacuous.**

**LIVE, BOTH DIRECTIONS ON ONE RECORD.** Pressing `+`: `order ["landing","tab-2"]`, `tab-2{active:true,target:'untitled-1'}`. **Clicking the `landing` chip (backward)** → `landing{active:true}`, `tab-2{active:false}`, actives `["landing"]`. **Clicking the minted chip (forward)** → the reverse.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,963 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** over **`146`** files (**`+1`** row, no new file); `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks` regenerated to **`105` markers, `9` carve-outs**; **`B-1` green with an empty offender list** after the battery path was declared **by the name `B-1` itself gave** rather than the one the brief guessed. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-241`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a deferred row finally taken, a diff that compared two spellings of one record, a referent the act had been handing over all along, and the missing row that had let half an act go unmeasured.**
## D-243 — THE PANE FILLS ITS ZONE: the pane arm writes **fill, figure and scroll**, and the declaration **reuses `LAYOUT_ZONE_AXES` rather than spelling itself twice**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source:** `D-240`'s measured hole and `D-234`'s routed finding — **the last piece of the layout charter that was not true.**

**THE DEFECT, NAMED TWICE BEFORE IT WAS TAKEN.** **`#pane-menus` rendered `style="width: 100px;"`** — **its authored `height: 100%` and `overflow-x: auto` were GONE**, **because `paintStyle` replaces `css.style` whole and the pane arm wrote only the adjustable member.** **So the charter's sentence — a pane *"fills the zone's fixed axis, adjusts the orthogonal, and scrolls along the axis it adjusts"* — was false in two of its three parts**, and **the same collision had already been fixed twice elsewhere** (`D-234` zones, `D-240` bar).

**THE FIX: THREE PARTS, ONE TABLE.** **`PANE_FILL` plus `paneFillAxisOf(zone)`, which READS `LAYOUT_ZONE_AXES` rather than declaring a second table** — **because a pane fills the axis its zone fixes and scrolls the axis it adjusts**, **so one table answers both nodes**, and **a duplicate would spell four facts twice with no instrument to catch a drift** (`D-188` debt 2). **The arm emits in the zone arm's order** (`D-240`): **a `top`-zone pane reads `height: 100%; width: 100px; overflow-x: auto`**, **a `left`-zone pane reads `width: 100%; height: 100px; overflow-y: auto`.**

**THE RECORD STILL OWNS THE ADJUSTABLE FIGURE, AND THE ARM ADDS NONE.** **A record stating no figure for that axis still gets the fill and the scroll, with the adjustable axis left UNSET** — **because a declared default there would be a second authority (`D-129`) right on one boot and false after the first gesture.** **And that state is UNREACHABLE from the record's own route**: both a whole write and a member delete answer `refused`/`store-refused` under `panes-must-stand` (*"no finite non-negative width or height"*) — **unlike a memberless zone, the pane family admits no half geometry** — **so the arm is stated rather than claimed green.**

**AND BOUNDS SURVIVE WITHOUT REDUNDANCY.** **The fill is a layout relation the cascade resolves; bounds are the drag's pixel clamp** (`readPaneBounds`' `undefined` arm → measured pair → `clampToBounds`, `D-238`). **`pane-menus` still stores none, and conflating the two would let a zone's extent move the gesture's ceiling with the window** — **the same mistake in a new place.**

**MEASURED BY CDP ON A SECOND INSTANCE** (killed afterwards; the running app untouched): **`#pane-menus` computes `140px` tall — THE TOP ZONE'S OWN HEIGHT** — **with `overflow-x: auto` and `scrollWidth 214` against `clientWidth 100`.** **It fills and it scrolls.** **And `#gutter-pane` keeps `width: 100px; height: 100px`** — **`pane-a` is the STAGE pane, states no `zone`, fills no zone's axis, and is byte-unchanged** (`null` is the stated absence).

**ONE DEBT NAMED: THE FILL IS INVISIBLE TO THE CARRIER.** **`reportMeasuredFigures`' subject is the adjustable member**, so **`#layout-measured` reads `pane-menus.width=100px` and nothing else for it** — **the fill and the scroll are measurable in principle (a computed `height`/`overflow-x` read on that node) and unmeasured as built.**

**`AL-10` WAS RE-GRAINED, NOT WEAKENED.** **It pinned *"the pane's OTHER stored member must NOT be painted"*** — **the old absence** — **and now asserts the three parts and their relations**: **the fill on the axis the pane's RECORDED `zone` fixes** (derived each run, never assumed), **the record's own figure read back over the wire**, **the scroll on the axis it adjusts** — **and its old red is REBORN against the markup the paint really produces for a wrong zone**, by writing `zone: 'left'` on a declared pane id, **which makes the paint emit `width: 100%; height: 100px; overflow-y: auto` for real**, and asserting that text **fails the fill-on-the-fixed-axis test while passing the other-member-as-figure one** — **then restoring and re-asserting.** **A hard-coded axis pair reds**, which is what makes the derivation worth having.

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,963 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** over **`146`** files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; the `app-layout` battery **`12`/`12`** three times; the demo rebuilt. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`**, `#pane-menus` serving `height: 100%; width: 100px; overflow-x: auto;`.

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-242`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records the last false sentence of the layout charter made true, a declaration that reads its neighbour instead of repeating it, a state stated rather than claimed because the record refuses to reach it, and a row's old red reborn against real markup.**
## D-244 — THE ZONES GET HANDLES: four strips standing on each zone's **stage-facing bound**, **siblings and never children** — and the reason is structural, not stylistic

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"There's no handle for adjusting the size of a zone or pane, and the pane drag handle doesn't relocate the pane"* — **the first half of which was a GAP IN THE DESIGN rather than a broken feature.**

**THE GAP, STATED PLAINLY.** **The zones have carried a `size` since `D-234` and NOTHING let a person change it.** **The charter said what a zone's dimension IS — *"the zones have defined height (top/bottom) or width (left/right)"* — and never how it is ADJUSTED**, **so no row could be red and no test could catch the absence.**

**FOUR STRIPS, ON THE EDGE THAT BOUNDS THEM.** **`zone-top-horizontal`** after `#top`, **`zone-bottom-horizontal`** before `#bottom`, **both in the root column**; **`zone-left-vertical`** after `#left`, **`zone-right-vertical`** before `#right`, **both in the arrangement row.** **Each carries `css.id` = `props.id` = `props.axis`, the shared `gutter-handle` class and its dotted paint, `flex: 0 0 14px`, a cursor, and NO zone figure.**

**AND THEY ARE SIBLINGS FOR TWO REASONS, EACH MEASURED.** **(i)** **`paintStyle` hands the engine ONE `css.style` in `replace` mode** (`D-234`), **so a zone can carry no `position: relative` and no authored layout for a child** — **a strip authored INSIDE a zone would have no way to position itself against an edge the paint owns.** **(ii)** **A strip inside a zone the record drags to `size: 0` could never be pressed** — **and `0` is lawful and reachable (`D-234`'s minimize marker survives the repair)** — **so the control that shrinks a zone would be destroyed by its own success.** **A sibling keeps its own `14px`.**

**THE ACT IS ONE LEAF.** **`view.commitZones(zoneId, {size})` → ONE `['zones', <id>, 'size']` at tier `mem`**, **one write at release**, **NO `['drag']` turn** (that family is pane-keyed, `D-145`) — **the transient is an inline style write on the ZONE element, with the member taken from `LAYOUT_ZONE_AXES`.**

**THE CLAMP IS `{0, window extent}`, DEGRADING TO THE RECORD'S OWN FIGURE** where the realm measures nothing — **never `undefined` into `NaN`**, **which is `D-238`'s inert-handle lesson**: a handle wired but clamped to `NaN` is inert **and looks wired.**

**AND IT REUSES THE PANE DRAG RATHER THAN COPYING IT** — **the affordance and session machinery, the move gate, `clampToBounds`, the example's one-axis pointer mapping and its `typeof` degradation, and the seams** — **with `ZONE_DRAG_HANDLES`, `zoneExtentOf`, `zoneMemberOf` and the `zone` route word added**, **and the receipt's *"no UI caller"* sentence re-grained because this IS one.**

**MEASURED LIVE**: **all four ids present with their axes and cursors**, **the dispatch path reachable**, and **`data.write ['zones','top','size']=222` reads back `222` and paints `#top` `height: 222px` with its `overflow-x` intact** — **and `commitZones('left', {size: 260})` reads `260`.**

**THE CENSUS IS `79 = 18 + 5 + 2 + 13 + 35 + 1 + 1 + 4`**, **the strips as their own SEVENTH term, never folded into another layer's count** — **and a FIFTH strip arriving unnoticed now reds the figure, the seven-term sum, `X-1`'s residue and the four-address identity rows.** **`PS-1` was re-grained to admit BOTH handle kinds through the wiring's own `subject` member** (**never inferred from a key's spelling**) **while keeping four biting census arms**; **`PS-6` went from pinning the zone receipt's ABSENCE to its PRESENCE.**

**AND THREE DEEP PATH ROWS ARE RE-GRAINED, WITH THEIR FRAGILITY NAMED.** **`codeGet`'s deep path, `C1` #21 and `R7` #29 each hard-code a `children` INDEX**, **and the arrangement moved to `children[3]`** because the `top` strip is `#top`'s following sibling. **`codeGet`'s grammar is dotted keys plus `[n]`, so a node inside a `children` array cannot be addressed by its `css.id`** — **and the next sibling breaks all three again.** **Deriving the path from `demoEnvelope()` by walking for the id is the honest shape and is named in-file as DEBT, not taken** — **no battery restructured for a re-grain.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,963 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** over **`146`** files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; **the five batteries `186` passed / `0` failed**; the demo rebuilt. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp` with all four strips in its markup.**

**THE SECOND HALF IS DESIGNED AND NOT BUILT**: **pane RELOCATION** (`docs/L3/renderer-wiring/design-pane-relocation.md`, rev 1) — **a `grab` grip per pane plus four authored zone drops revealed by `tabindex` + `:focus-within`, the drop naming both operands in its `props` because `getBoundingClientRect` throws in the shim, arrival inventing no figure and dropping `bounds`, one whole-pane write at `['panes', <id>]`** — **with its limit declared**: **the RECORD relocates and the RENDERED REGION does not** (`D-182`'s upstream routing defect).

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-243`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a gap no test could see, controls placed where their own success cannot destroy them, a gesture reused rather than copied, and three index paths kept honest by naming their fragility.**
## D-245 — BOTH DRAGS WERE INERT FOR **ONE** REASON: no `setPointerCapture` — measured with **real input over CDP**, because every probe before it measured the wiring and not the gesture

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"UI drag doesn't work"* — **after this seat had twice reported a drag working on the strength of a probe that drove the machinery rather than the pointer.**

**THE METHOD IS THE FINDING.** **A real drag CAN be driven through CDP** — **`Input.dispatchMouseEvent` (`mousePressed` → ten `mouseMoved` → `mouseReleased`) at each handle's own coordinates, read from the DOM through `Runtime.evaluate`** — **and that is a TRUSTED pointer, not a synthetic event.** **Every earlier "the drag works" in this corpus rested on a node probe calling the act directly**, **which cannot see the difference between a live gesture and a dead one.**

**AND IT WAS NONE OF THE FOUR SUSPECTS.** **The boxes were fine**: the top strip measures `[0,176,980,14]`, the verticals `[120,190,14,435]` and `[876,190,14,435]`, the bottom `[0,625,980,14]`, **all `elementFromPoint` → SELF**; the pane handle `[2,36,14,125]`, **also SELF**, sitting **inside** `#pane-menus`' clipped box — **so `D-232`'s scoping clipped nothing.** **Everything was attached**: **zero *"did NOT attach"* lines**, and `getEventListeners` shows `pointerdown`, `pointerover`, `pointerout` and `pointermove` **on every handle.**

**THE BREAK WAS THE GESTURE ITSELF.** **On press, the first preview wrote the zone to `height: 43px`** — **from the example's ABSOLUTE `pointer.y − start`** — **which RE-LAID THE BOX OUT FROM UNDER THE POINTER.** **The following moves' `event.target` became the page**, **the RELEASE MISSED TOO**, **and the session's ONE gesture slot stayed occupied** — **so every later gesture on ANY of the six handles was refused `busy` for the page's life.** **That single latch is why the pane handle was inert as well**, and **it is why the user's report was broader than the strips.**

**THE FIX IS ONE LISTENER PER RESOLVED HANDLE** calling **`setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)`** on the existing injected source, **total over realms without it** — **the remedy the demo already meets in its own realm**, and **the affordance's own docblock had recorded capture as *"DECLARED AND IGNORED"*.** **A declaration that nothing implements is not a design, and this corpus had written the word without wiring it.**

**MEASURED AFTER, with no injection**: **the zone strip moves `['zones','top','size']` `140 → 163`** and **paints `height: 163px`**; **the pane handle moves `['panes','pane-menus','width']` `100 → 0`** and **paints `width: 0px`**; **and a THIRD gesture still lands**, so **the slot does not latch.**

**AND THE HARNESS PRACTICE CHANGED WITH IT.** **The user asked that test windows stop stealing focus**, **and `dist/main/standalone.mjs` is a RENDERERLESS MCP server** — ***"so the MCP tool wiring + transports can be verified without an Electron window"*** — **so verification uses that from now on, and a window opens only when the user asks.** **And the row records what a headless server CANNOT measure**: **it has no renderer at all, so the boxes, `elementFromPoint`, the painted style and the gesture itself are exactly what it cannot see** — **those readings are the real window's alone, which is why this row needed one.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,963 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** over **`146`** files, **zero red**; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; the demo rebuilt; **every probe window reaped and the probe profiles removed.** **A foreign window on `/tmp/prov-z` started at 13:29 predated this seat and was left alone** — **the user's own.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-244`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a declaration nobody wired, a gesture that killed itself on its first move, a latch that silenced five other handles, and a measurement method that can finally tell a live gesture from a dead one.**
## D-246 — THE GRIP STOPS SCROLLING AND THE RESIZE IS **VISIBLE WHILE IT HAPPENS**: a control inside a scroller cannot stay put, and a preview that writes the wrong node moves nothing a person can see

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"The drag handle moves with the scrollbar, it should be external"* · *"Also the drag resize doesn't update live"* — with a screenshot of a scrolled menus pane and the grip travelling with it.

**DEFECT 1 — THE GRIP WAS A CHILD OF A SCROLLER.** **`#menus-vertical` was `position: absolute` INSIDE `#pane-menus`**, **and the pane arm writes `overflow-x: auto`** (`D-243`) — **so the handle travelled with the content.** **That is the same class the ZONE STRIPS solved by being SIBLINGS** (`D-244`) — **and this grip could not take that fix**: **`AL-1` is GATING and UNMARKED and requires the handle's markup INSIDE `#pane-menus` and BEFORE the first `menus-menu`**, **and `theme-control` pins the authored-object census at `79`** — **so both directed moves were closed by rows, not by taste.**

**SO IT IS PINNED INSTEAD.** **`float: right; position: sticky; left: calc(100% + 1.125rem − 0.875rem); margin-right: -1.125rem; height: 100%`** — **a percentage of the pane (so the record's painted figure) plus the padding lane minus the authored `14px` = the pane's right edge**; **`left` holds it while the menus scroll**, **and the margin puts its STATIC box on that same point for when the sticky rectangle empties at the end of the range** — **and the margin is LOAD-BEARING, measured apart: the pin alone dropped `86 → 68` at `scrollLeft 96`.**

**MEASURED**: **the grip's rect is `[86,36,14,125]` before the scroll, at `scrollLeft 48` and at `scrollLeft 96`** — **where it used to run `[84,36,14,125] → [-12,36,14,125]`.** **And it follows the pane's edge live**: `86 → 90 → 101 → 112 → 123` **as the pane went `100 → 137`.**

**AND THE STAGE'S GRIP HAS NO SUCH DEFECT** — **`#gutter-pane` computes no overflow and `scrollWidth == clientWidth == 100`**, **so nothing there can carry it** — **and it gets the live preview too.**

**DEFECT 2 — THE PREVIEW WROTE THE WRONG NODE WITH THE WRONG MEMBER.** **It was neither missing nor wiped.** **Per-move samples during a trusted CDP drag**: **`#gutter-target` — the composition's ONE target, `D-144` — moved `100 → 106 → 110 → 104px`** **while the painted `#pane-menus` read `[0,36,100,140]` at EVERY sample and the record stayed `100`.** **No delivery runs mid-gesture, so nothing overwrote anything** — **the write simply landed one node and one member away from the paint.**

**THE FIX: `panePreviewOf` now ALSO writes the record's selected member (`adjustableMemberNameOf` over the shape's `zone`) on `nodeIdForPane(<handle's pane>)`** — **the node and the member the PAINT writes** — **with the `#gutter-target` write byte-unchanged** (`PS-2`/`PS-3`/`PS-4` read it).

**MEASURED LIVE**: **moves take the style `104 → 115 → 126 → 137px`**, **the grip to `[90…123,36,14,125]`**, **THE RECORD UNTOUCHED AT `pane-menus: 100×100` AT EVERY MOVE**, **then `137×100` after release.** **So the drag is visible while it happens and still commits once.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,961 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** with **only the two worktree-boundary rows** (`F-9(b)`, `I-12`) red **on the uncommitted `index.html`** and **`170`/`170` green on a clean tree**; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; the demo rebuilt. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`** with the pinned grip served.

**AND THIS ROW OWES ONE THING IT DID NOT TAKE**: **`AL-1`'s requirement that the handle live inside `#pane-menus` is what made a pin necessary**, **and the census is what forbade a node** — **so a future pass that wants a genuinely external grip must move the row and the census first**, **rather than discovering the same two walls.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-245`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a control freed from a scroller by pinning rather than moving, two walls found in rows rather than in code, a preview that was writing a node nobody paints, and a margin that is load-bearing.**
## D-247 — DARK MODE: the bar cluster had **no dark pair** (this seat's own), and the `Dark` click **never left the realm** — and the hypothesis that looked obvious was wrong twice over

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"clicking on dark mode doesn't work, unless it was previously set to light mode manually"* · *"Dark mode doesn't change the top-bar"* — from a screenshot showing the app dark everywhere except the bar.

**DEFECT 2 WAS THIS SEAT'S OWN AND IT WAS THE WHOLE WHITE STRIP.** **`.top-bar` carried a hard-coded `background: #fff` with NO dark counterpart** — **so under a dark page the bar stayed white with dark text on it: a LEGIBILITY bug, not a taste one.** **Every unpaired light colour in the bar cluster is now paired in the page's existing convention** — **the light rule stays the base, and the dark arm is `body:has([theme="dark"]) <the light selector verbatim> { colours only }`, keyed on the PAINTED attribute and using only the block's own palette**: **the bar to `#1b222b` with a `#2c3642` bottom edge and `#e8edf4` ink**; **the chips one step above (`#2b3542` over `#3a4654`), the active chip inverted as it is on the light bar**; **the add control a chip's peer**; **and the dropdown panel's shadow deepened (`rgba(0,0,0,.55)`) because only its fill and border had been paired.** **Measured**: **bar `rgb(255,255,255) → rgb(27,34,43)`**, border `rgb(216,221,227) → rgb(44,54,66)`, name → `rgb(232,237,244)`, inactive chip → `rgb(43,53,66)`, the panel → `rgb(27,34,43)`.

**DEFECT 1 REFUTED THE EXPECTED CAUSE TWICE OVER, AND THE SECOND REFUTATION IS THE ROW'S POINT.** **The obvious hypothesis was `D-216`'s class — that the boot's theme never reached the paint.** **It was wrong on the first test**: **`['theme']` IS in the adopted set (`VIEW_DECLARED_ADDRESSES`) and a WARM boot paints `theme="dark"` with NO CLICK AT ALL** — **the paradigm was never the problem.** **THE CAUSE IS ONE LAYER EARLIER: THE CLICK NEVER LEFT THE REALM.** **`commitSetting`'s `changed` guard measured the click against `lastCarried`, seeded at boot from the AUTHORED CARRIER's own `dark`** — **so clicking `Dark` on a fresh profile answered `changed: false, sent: false`, wrote nothing, delivered nothing and painted nothing**, **and only `Light` — a different token — could pass the guard.** **And the record's boot value is a PLACEHOLDER (`{"declaration":{"removal":true,"value":""}}`) while the card's label reads `dark`** — **so the label is the CARRIER's and the paint is the RECORD's, and they disagree at boot; the guard was trusting the former to answer for the latter.**

**THE FIX GIVES THE TWO CAUSES DIFFERENT REFERENCES.** **The reply path keeps its boot baseline** — **`T-7`'s guard untouched and the boot's silence for divergence stands** — **while a CLICK is measured against the PAINTED SURFACE** (`authoredPropOf`, **`D-129`'s ask-don't-remember relation**) — **so a click on a token the surface already shows still sends nothing, and a click whose RECORD is a placeholder but whose surface shows a token SENDS.** **It touches no paradigm rule**: **no boot application, no timer, no self-scheduled paint, no new channel or bridge member** — **the write is still the click's and the paint still the delivery's.** **Measured after**: **from a fresh profile, clicking `Dark` writes the record, paints the attribute, and a SECOND click writes nothing, while the boot stays event-free.**

**AND A GATING ROW WAS ASSERTING THE DEFECT AS CORRECT.** **`A-3` (`tests/theme-act.test.ts`, unmarked, gating) pinned *"a click that moves nothing sends nothing … the crossing still stands at the PLACEHOLDER"*** — **which is the user's bug, written down as a guarantee.** **It is now seven arms**, **with the new one pinning exactly the user's case** (a click whose record is a placeholder but whose card shows a token **sends**), **the reply baseline kept and PINNED rather than assumed**, **the boot pinned event-free**, **and a BOOT-SNAPSHOT RESEED of the guard measured to red arm (1)** — **so the regression that would silence the click again fails loudly.** **`A-2` could not have caught it, and the row says why**: **it clicks the OTHER token, which passes both references.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,961 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** with **only the two worktree-boundary rows** red on the uncommitted files; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; `strata-marks check` **0**; **the four theme batteries `134`/`134`**; the demo rebuilt. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`.**

**RESIDUALS NAMED, NOT TAKEN**: **the platform's three window buttons** (`titleBarOverlay`, no colour pair — `main`'s); **the pinned light UA scrollbar inside the tabs row**; **and the boot's label-vs-record disagreement** — **the envelope's `THEME_INITIAL_TOKEN` against the placeholder**, which is `app-envelope`'s (or `D-97`'s), **and a boot fix there would need a boot application, which the paradigm forbids.**

**ITS REGISTER IS `D-71` TO `D-246`** as prose, unchanged and extended by this row only. **This row records a white strip this seat painted, a swallowed click, a hypothesis refuted on its first test, and a gating row that had written the defect down as a guarantee.**
## D-248 — PANE RELOCATION LANDS: ten authored nodes, **revealed without state**, one whole-pane write — and **the fill flips while the region does not**, which is the limit taken rather than hidden

**WHERE THEY SIT DIFFERS BY ONE MEASURED FACT, AND THE FACT IS `D-246`'s.** **`#gutter-pane` computes no overflow**, **so its grip takes the design's `position: relative` at the flow origin.** **`#pane-menus` IS a scroller**, **so its grip takes `D-246`'s second form — `float: left; position: sticky; left: 0`** — **out of the menus' line and pinned**, **measured at `[0,36,14,14]` for `scrollLeft` 0, 48 and 96 while the resize grip stays `[86,36,14,125]`.** **And a SIBLING was unavailable** (`D-244`'s strip fix) **because the pane's box is painted and its `css.style` replaced whole.**

## D-249 — RELOCATION IS A **DRAG**, NOT A PICK: press the grip, drag toward a zone, see the target, release to commit — and the preview lands on nodes that already exist

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** *"It should act as a drag handle — click-drag into the vicinity of a zone and it shows a preview of the pane's placement, release causes it to commit to the relocation."*

**`D-248` SHIPPED CLICK-THEN-PICK AND THE USER ASKED FOR A GESTURE.** **The act, the write and the record's shape do not change** — **only how a person expresses them.**

**1. CAPTURE FIRST, BECAUSE `D-245` SAID SO.** **A handle that loses the pointer on its first move latches the session `busy` for the page's life.** **The grip now captures exactly as the resize handles do** — **per grip, from boot, with the same three total degradations** — **measured: `gotpointercapture@7,43` → `lostpointercapture@100,360`, no `pointercancel`, every move retargeted to the grip.**

**2. THE PREVIEW IS TWO TRANSIENT WRITES, AND BOTH LAND ON NODES THAT EXIST.** **The zone the record would receive is OUTLINED on the ZONE ELEMENT** (`outline: 2px solid #2f6fb0; outline-offset: -2px`) — **a PAINTED node whose `css.style` the next delivery replaces whole, so it self-clears** — **and the authored overlay under the pointer is FILLED.** **NO GHOST**, **because a ghost is a new element and every element is provident data** (**the census is pinned at `89`**) **and the pane's element may not be re-parented.** **And `['drag']` WAS READ AND NOT USED**: **`commitDrag` is pane-KEYED and GEOMETRY-shaped** — **a placement has no `size`, so forcing one through it would be a second authority (`D-129`).**

**3. THE TARGET IS RESOLVED BY THE DOM, NOT BY RECTS.** **During a drag the four authored drops become `position: fixed` zone-sized overlays** (**disjoint bands**), **and `elementFromPoint` — or the event's own `target` where there is no layout — says which one the pointer is on.** **Chosen over rect hit-testing because that is unmeasurable in the layout-less shim and would need an Electron leg for its only reading** — **the design's own ground.** **The cost is named**: **the drops lose their absolute fan inside the grip and the grip stops being their containing block** — **`D-246`'s pin is untouched.**

**4. MEASURED, MOVE BY MOVE.** **Five samples show the target switching from `top` to `left` as the pointer travelled** — **with the record reading `zone: top, width: 100, height: 100` AT EVERY SAMPLE and the pane byte-unchanged at `height: 100%; width: 100px; overflow-x: auto`.** **After release**: **`zone: left`, both figures kept, NO `bounds`, tier `file`** — **and the pane paints `width: 100%; height: 100px; overflow-y: auto`**, **the fill flipped with no paint byte moved** (`D-243`).

**5. AND THE NEGATIVES HOLD, WHICH IS WHERE A DRAG USUALLY LEAKS.** **A drag released over NO zone** — **outlines nothing, emphasises nothing, leaves nothing standing, writes nothing**; **`pane-a` unchanged at `width: 100, height: 100, bounds {0…200}`.** **And a press-and-release IN PLACE commits nothing either**, **because the arming distance is `4px` and the grip's own box stands inside one of its overlays** — **a fact that had to be found, since an unarmed press is a click and a click must not relocate.**

**THE READINGS.** `npm test` **`2,961 passed / 2 skipped` of `2,965`** with **only the two worktree-boundary rows** red before the commit; `typecheck` **0**; `typecheck:tests` **0**; `build` **0**; the demo rebuilt. **The app is live on `http://127.0.0.1:3787/mcp`.**

## D-252 — RELOCATION NOW **ACTUALLY RELOCATES**: the engine has carried a `MoveOp` all along, and **`D-182`'s conclusion was too strong** — a user's one-sentence correction overturned a limit this corpus had recorded as upstream

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** ***"It's not a defect. Dragging the pane should cause a save to the storeroom, which triggers a listener that regenerates the zone's section of the tree."*** — **offered after this seat asked whether to remove the feature because the region could not move.**

**THE CORPUS WAS WRONG, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE IT WRONG WAS IN `node_modules`.** **`D-182` and `D-248` recorded *"the record relocates and the rendered region does not"* as an UPSTREAM limit.** **The engine declares `interface MoveOp { kind: 'move'; node: Node; to: { parent: Node; priority?: number } }` with its wire twin**, **and `supervisor` executes a move as `detachNodeSafe(node)` + `node.addAnchor('child', …, toParent.familyLinkFor())`, journaled `applied` with `dirtied: [node.id]`.** **`RowsMintOp` mints ONE family node per row and never re-places** — **so a mint was never the right instrument and `D-248`'s keyed `minted: []` blocked nothing.** **THE ONLY GAP WAS PAGE-SIDE: `applyCommand` resolved `node` and `target` strings but NOT `to.parent`, so the engine's own move could not be issued from the renderer at all.**

**THE FIX IS THE DELIVERY'S OWN.** **`driveLayoutRegions`' pane loop calls `relocatePaneInZone` IN THE SAME DELIVERY AS THE PAINT** — **exactly what the user described: a save, a listener, a regenerated section** — **issuing ONE `move` when one of the four declared zones names a destination and an ELEMENT-IDENTITY read of the rendered parent says the pane is not already its child.** **Nothing is cached**, **an absent or undeclared `zone` names none and moves nothing** (the stage arm), **and `applyCommand` resolves and guards `to.parent` exactly as the others** — **unresolvable, malformed or a plain object answers a bare `rejected`, never a throw.**

**MEASURED IN THE TREE.** **`#pane-menus`' parent, from `get_rendered_html`'s nesting and `pathKey`: `top` (`root/node-2/node-7/node-8`) → dispatch at `menus-grab-left` → `left`, inside `.arrangement` (`root/node-2/node-39/node-40/node-8`) → dispatch at `menus-grab-top` → `top` again**, **with the style following `D-243` in each zone** and **`#top` no longer holding it**. **And a COLD BOOT whose record already says `zone: left` paints the pane in `left` through the same code path** — **so the fix is not a gesture special case.** **The census does not move at all**: `registered 91 / inTree 90 / 90 elements` before, after and back, **the pane keeping its id, children, handlers and element wire.**

**WHAT SURVIVES FROM `D-182` AND WHAT DOES NOT.** **Its upstream rows-mint finding stands unmoved** (`D-5`) — **a mint still mints.** **What is overturned is the claim that DYNAMIC ZONE ROUTING WAS UNAVAILABLE**: **it is available, it was simply never wired, and four rows grew around its absence** — **including a feature designed, built, measured and then nearly deleted because a limit was asserted rather than read.**

**THE LESSON THIS ROW EXISTS TO CARRY.** **`D-182` was recorded from a symptom** — *"the region does not move"* — **and the row that recorded it did not open the engine's typings.** **A limit is a claim about someone else's code, and this corpus's own rule is that such a claim is measured or it is not made.** **The cost here was a designed feature, an ask-the-user question offering three wrong options, and a user doing the reading this seat should have done.**

THE MENUS STACK AND THE PANEL GOES SIDEWAYS.** **The `:focus-within` + `::before` mechanism is UNCHANGED — only the offsets moved** (`left: 100%`, `top: 0`; items at `left: calc(100% + pad)`, mirrored to `right: 100%` in a `right` zone) — **so the panel keeps the fill, border and shadow `D-233` fixed.** **Measured: in `left` the four menus stack (`y = 206, 233.41, 260.81, 288.22`) and the items open RIGHT at `x = 121`; in `right` they mirror to `x = 711` against a chip at `904`.**

## D-254 — THE GESTURE'S AXIS FOLLOWS THE ZONE, read **at every press** — because the paint had known it for rows while the gesture had not

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"Gutter is oriented correctly, but it still responds to side-to-side drag."*

**THE DIVERGENCE WAS THE BUG.** **`D-253` put the grip on a sidebar pane's BOTTOM edge with `cursor: row-resize`** — **and the gesture still read X**, **because the affordance's axis was fixed when the handle was DECLARED**, **which was correct only while the pane lived in a `top` zone.** **So the PAINT had known the right axis for rows** (`D-243`'s `paneAxisMembers` reads the record's `zone` per delivery) **while the GESTURE had not** — **two answers to one question, one of them cached.**

**THE FIX READS IT AT EVERY PRESS.** **`panePointerAxisOf(paneId)` reads `['panes', <id>, 'zone']` off the shape through the client and maps it with `pointerAxisOfMember(adjustableMemberNameOf(zone))`** — **`width → x`, `height → y`** — **kept for THAT GESTURE ALONE as a `PressAnchor` carrying the axis and the press coordinate.** **Nothing is read at boot, nothing at declaration, nothing carried across presses**, **so a relocation takes effect at the next press with no reload.** **It reads the RECORD and not the painted `zone` attribute**, **because the record is the zone's only authority and `panePaintedMemberOf` already reads it the same way — so the gesture's axis and the preview's member are ONE answer a delivery cannot split.**

**AND A WRONG-AXIS DRAG IS IGNORED BY PROJECTION, NOT BY A FLAG.** **The delta is the pointer's displacement ON THE AXIS THE PRESS READ**, **so a sideways stroke on a bottom grip computes `start ± 0` and writes the record's own figure** — **no resize, no clamp reached, and no *"wrong axis"* flag, which would have been a second authority beside the one coordinate the mapping reads.**

**THE ZONE STRIPS ARE UNCHANGED, WITH A REASON RATHER THAN AN ASSUMPTION**: **each strip's axis is a DECLARATION matched to `LAYOUT_ZONE_AXES`' member, and the zones never move** — **so a strip's thunk is its declaration read.**

**MEASURED WITH FOUR TRUSTED CDP DRAGS.**

| zone | drag | record |
|---|---|---|
| `top` | horizontal | `width 100 → 160` |
| `top` | vertical | **unchanged, byte-identical** |
| `left` | vertical | `height 100 → 160` |
| `left` | horizontal | **unchanged, byte-identical** |
| `top` again | horizontal | `width 160 → 200` |

**So the axis follows the zone BOTH WAYS with no reload.**

## D-255 — DARK SCROLLBARS BY **ONE INHERITED DECLARATION**: the `color-scheme` pin was right, and the scrollbars were never following the theme attribute

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"Dark mode scrollbars are unthemed"* — a sidebar pane in dark mode showing a white scrollbar.

**THE CAUSE WAS DELIBERATE AND THE FIX RESPECTS IT.** **Scrollbars follow `color-scheme`, NOT the `theme` attribute the app paints** — **and the page pins `:root { color-scheme: light }` for a recorded reason**: **the UA's `light dark` pair once painted WHITE text on the light backgrounds** (`D-97`, `X-5`). **So every scroll container got a light scrollbar in dark mode, and the pin could not be lifted to fix it.**

**THE FIX IS ONE RULE, AND IT NAMES NOTHING.** **`body:has([theme="dark"]) { scrollbar-color: #3a4654 #1b222b; }`** — **thumb on the dark pair's STRONG border, one step above a chip's `#2b3542`**, **track on the raised surface the bar, cards and menu panel already use.** **It is INHERITED**, **so no class or id list can go stale and a FUTURE scroll container cannot be missed** — **which is the seam class this session kept finding in rules that enumerated their containers** (`D-240`, `D-250`, `D-253`).

**AND THE SCOPED DARK `color-scheme` WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, WITH THE ARGUMENT.** **`body:has([theme="dark"]) { color-scheme: dark }` would fix the scrollbars too — and would hand the UA's dark arm to EVERY FORM CONTROL inside that subtree**: **input bevels and carets, the demo buttons' chrome** — **UA colours this sheet never states — on the very subtree the pin exists to protect.** **So the pin stays and the scrollbars are themed explicitly.**

**MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, BECAUSE "SUPPORTED" IS A CLAIM ABOUT SOMEONE ELSE'S CODE** (`D-252`'s lesson): **Electron 44.4.5 ships `Chrome/152.0.7977.130`, read off the live window's `/json/version`**, **where `scrollbar-color` has been standard since M121**; **the computed value reads back on ALL TEN containers plus `body` in both themes**; **and the PIXELS were read too**: **the stage, the menus pane, the tabs row and the top zone each show `#3A4654` thumb on `#1B222B` track in dark and the UA's own `#8B8B8B` on `#FCFCFC` in light — with IDENTICAL pixel counts in both themes, so the geometry did not move.**

**AND THE LIGHT ARM IS BYTE-UNCHANGED.** **`color-scheme` still reads `light` on `:root` and on every element in both themes**, **the light arm declares no `scrollbar-color` at all (`auto`)**, **and no light surface gained a dark scrollbar** — **so the pin's reason holds in the same commit that fixes what the pin caused.**

## D-257 — THE SIDEBAR PANE GETS A HEADER **WITHOUT A NEW NODE**: the grab above the content, the pane's name beside it, and a name that survives because the paint never replaces `props`

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user, verbatim):** ***"In the sidebar, move the grab handle to the top of the pane above the text (not to the side), and render the pane name as text to the right of it."***

## D-260 — THE ZONE FORMATTING REVERTS, AND THE DROPS GO QUIET: **the preview's own success created the failure**, because moving the real panes put the dragged pane's content under the pointer

**THE STALE FORMATTING WAS NOT A STALE ATTRIBUTE.** **Measured: `#pane-menus` `parent="top"`, `zone="left"`.** **The attribute was FAITHFUL TO THE RECORD** — **the NODE had left the record's zone**, **because the paint runs only on a DELIVERY while `driveZoneArrangement` ALSO re-parents on the PREVIEW.** **So the two disagree for the whole span of a gesture, and a release that fails to commit leaves them disagreeing afterwards.**

**AND TWO ROOT CAUSES SAT UNDER THAT, BOTH MEASURED.** **(a) THE RELEASE RESOLVED NO DROP**: **`elementsFromPoint` answers the pane's own `menus-menu` BEFORE `menus-grab-top`** — **because a drop's `z-index` is TRAPPED IN THE STICKY GRIP'S STACKING CONTEXT**, **and the pane arriving in `top` still carries `width: 100%`, spanning the whole band.** **(b) WITH NO DESTINATION, `onEnd` took an *"unchanged target"* shortcut that RETURNED WITHOUT RESTORING.**

**AND THE THING THAT CHANGED SINCE `D-253` MEASURED THIS ROUND TRIP AS BYTE-IDENTICAL IS THE PREVIEW ITSELF.** **`D-259` made the preview move the REAL panes — so the dragged pane's own content now travels under the pointer and WINS THE HIT.** **No ghost could have shadowed it, and the ghost was deleted precisely because the real panes took its place.** **The feature that made rearrangement visible is the feature that made the drop unreachable.**

**THE FIX HAS TWO HALVES.** **(i) THE GRIP'S OWN REVEAL ARM NOW LIFTS ITS DROPS** (`.pane-grab:focus-within { z-index: … }`) — **the grip is the box that MAKES the stacking context, so only its own declaration can raise its children**, **which is why a rule on the drops could never have worked.** **(ii) EVERY NON-COMMITTING END RESTORES THE RECORD'S ARRANGEMENT** — **the no-destination end and `onCancel` both — so the window in which the attribute and the node can disagree is BOUNDED BY THE GESTURE and cannot outlive it.**

**AND THE DROPS ARE CLOSED BY THE SHEET AND OPENED BY THE PRESS.** **`:focus-within` alone now gives `opacity: 0; visibility: hidden`** — **so a grip that still holds focus after a gesture paints nothing over the pane** — **while the press opens each drop that has a window.** **`:active` was TRIED AND MEASURED UNUSABLE**: **it goes false mid-drag on the very `move` that re-parents.** **The cost is named**: **press-then-click-an-overlay becomes the drag that names the same drop**, **and a keyboard user loses four NAMED WINDOWS THEY COULD NEVER PICK** — **the drops carry no `tabindex`, so they were never reachable.**

**Status:** ACTIVE · **Date:** 2026-11-09 · **Source (user):** *"when dragging from top/bottom to sidebar or vice versa, the preview uses the original zone's formatting in the preview location, instead of that zone's native style"* — **the same session in which `D-262` fixed the FIRST-LOAD rearrange and `D-260` fixed the END of a gesture.**

**THE TWO CADENCES NEVER MET, WHICH IS WHY "BEFORE OR AFTER" WAS THE WRONG QUESTION.** **`props.zone` and the composed `css.style` were written by the pane loop on a DELIVERY**; **the preview runs on every `pointermove` and issued no such write.** **So during a drag the node had moved and its formatting had not**, **and the pane crossed a zone boundary wearing the zone it came from.**

**THE FIX IS ONE COMPOSITION SERVING BOTH CALLERS.** **`drivePreviewPanePaints`, called from the preview's `place` turn**: **ONE `state-slice` on the pane's own node — `css.style` whole plus `props.zone` as one member**, **the same command `paintStyle` already sends**, **with `['panes']` untouched at every sample and the release still the gesture's ONE crossing.** **And `panePaintOf(zone, record)` now composes the fill, the record's figure on the axis that zone makes adjustable, `LAYOUT_ZONE_AXES`' scroll AND the attribute IN ONE FUNCTION** — **the delivery passes the record's zone, the preview the destination** — **so a preview that flipped the attribute without the style cannot exist**: **that would have shown a column-shaped box with row formatting, which is a different wrongness.** **A second composition was the seam class this corpus has now found six times, and this row closes it by construction rather than by discipline.**

**AND IT COSTS ONE WRITE PER ZONE TRANSITION, NOT PER MOVE.** **Measured by `MutationObserver` on the pane**: **`top` → `left` over seven moves costs ONE zone write and ONE style write**; **the reverse the same.** **The guard is the surface's own published attribute**, **so in-zone moves, re-orders and re-stated previews cost ZERO.**

**AND THE RE-ANCHOR HAD TO MOVE BEHIND THE PAINT — measured, not assumed.** **Writing after `reanchor()` LOST THE CAPTURE AND THE FOCUS to the render**: **`pointerup` landed on `#left` and the release missed.** **`reanchor()` is now last and fires on `moved > 0 || painted > 0`.** **That is `D-259`'s re-take lesson in the other direction**: **the operation that restores the gesture must be the LAST thing the turn does, whichever operation that turns out to be.**

**THE RESTORE WAS NEEDED TOTALLY, AND NO DELIVERY WOULD HAVE DONE IT.** **A non-committing end writes nothing, so NO DELIVERY FOLLOWS** — **`previewPlacement(null)` hands the record's family to the same loop**, **which puts the attribute, the style AND the format back in the turn that puts the panes back**; **a committing release needs none, because its delivery repaints.**

| drag | first moves | the move the target resolves | record |
|---|---|---|---|
| `top` → `left` | row, flank grip, `::after` none | **`left`, `width: 100%; height: 100px; overflow-y: auto`, COLUMN, header, `Menus`** | **`top` at every sample** |
| `left` → `top` | column, header, `Menus` | **`top`, `height: 100%; width: 100px; overflow-x: auto`, ROW, flank, none** | **`left` at every sample** |
| release over no zone | — | **attribute, style and formatting all restored** | **unchanged** |
